fact_units.text: Discipline, defence, and fast starts: how new head coach can reignite Manchester United | Manchester United | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigation

Jason Wilcox and Jim Ratcliffe (top left) are attracting the ire of United fans, while Bruno Fernandes (centre) has been openly critical of the team’s tactics.Composite: Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJason Wilcox and Jim Ratcliffe (top left) are attracting the ire of United fans, while Bruno Fernandes (centre) has been openly critical of the team’s tactics.Composite: Getty ImagesAnalysis
Discipline, defence, and fast starts: how new head coach can reignite Manchester United
Michael Carrick’s replacement must find solutions on the pitch and pressure the hierarchy to accept a share of blame

One of the final images of Michael Carrick’s time in charge will be of him standing in the rain on the Old Trafford touchlinewatching his side succumb to Bournemouth, while his sullen captain sat unused on the bench.
Bruno Fernandes was dropped after calling out his head coach’s tactics, although Carrick said it was for football reasons.

It was the second combustible television interview in as many Champions League games after Lisandro Martínez pointed the finger at the director of football, Jason Wilcox, for failing to provide a squad suitable for fighting on all fronts.
Fernandes was soon back in the fold, andMartínez apologised for his outburst, but it is clear internal discipline is an issue and will be central to getting the team back on track.

United will always draw more attention than almost any other club in the world and creating a circus around a failing team merely complicates matters when there are already enough problems to sort out on the pitch.
The players need to harness their anger to ensure they create headlines for performances, not interviews.
View image in fullscreenBruno Fernandes (centre) was left on the bench against Bournemouth, reportedly for tactical reasons.Photograph: Gary Oakley/EPA
One player Jason Wilcox could claim as a recruitment success was Senne Lammens but the goalkeeper’s form has joined that of his teammates in the gutter.
The Belgian endured a horror show for Bournemouth’s third goal when he rushed out of his area, and he made two errors in the4-4 draw with Aston Villa.
Leny Yoro was another to make a terrible mistake against Bournemouth, while Diogo Dalot’s efforts as a makeshift left-back can be categorised as somewhere between woeful and inept.
No team in Europe’s top five leagues have conceded more than United’s 30 in all competitions, which is clearly a worry.
Morale is at rock bottom but the chopping and changing in defence is creating more uncertainty.
The new head coach should pick a back four and stick with it where possible.
If Harry Maguire’s experience is deemed mandatory, he needs pace around him to make up for what he lacks.
Luke Shaw’s absence has created a left-back tombola as Dalot, Ayden Heaven and Noussair Mazraoui have been placed there.
View image in fullscreenLeny Yoro is among the United defenders to have made costly errors.Photograph: Dave Thompson/AP
Benjamin Sesko’s injury has cost United a No 9 for most of the season and Joshua Zirkzee has rarely been trusted in the role.
Matheus Cunha gave it a go as a false 9 and Bryan Mbeumo was tried as a more traditional centre-forward but without much success either.

Cunha has become more productive in a deeper role behind the striker, cutting in from the left as he did at Wolves, but United require someone to be a classic No 9, someone who can occupy defenders and be serviced by deliveries from wide.
Zirkzee, for his faults, has been a presence when used in recent weeks and scored against Aston Villa.
If a new coach can rebuild his confidence, the Dutchman could provide a short-term solution.
Alternatively, greater demands should be made of Marcus Rashford to play through the middle.
Marcus Rashford could fill in for the injured Benjamin Sesko.Photograph: Annabel Lee-Ellis/PA
A mix-and-match of expletives were aimed at those above Carrick at recent home games.
Wilcox has taken most of the individual criticism, but the ownership were told in no uncertain terms to sell up.
The Glazers have been instrumental in driving the club downwards in recent years and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s investment and involvement in football operations have yielded little success.
View image in fullscreenFrom left to right: Sir Jim Ratcliffe; Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada; and director of football, Jason Wilcox.Photograph: Jacob King/PA

Carrick was the face of the operation, as the new head coach will be, and he needs to put pressure on someone at the top to speak to the media to explain why the club is in such a mess because it is unfair to expect the coach to do so.
United fans know the person in the dugout cannot take all the blame and someone else has to be publicly accountable.
Three central midfielders and a backup goalkeeper did not make for an inspiring summer when everyone knew United’s squad required improvement in numerous positions.
Andrey Santos, Carlos Baleba and Youri Tielemans started together against Bournemouth and offered no evidence for why so much was spent on them.

Whoever comes in needs to be clear about what is required, whether in the winter or summer windows, because the deficiencies in the squad mean United cannot compete on all fronts and are struggling to cope with the rigours of the Premier League.
A new left-back and striker are a given, but there is plenty more work to be done.
View image in fullscreenAndrey Santos has struggled to prove his worth since joining from Chelsea for £50m in July.Photograph: Conor Molloy/ProSports/Shutterstock
Outrunning the opposition does not guarantee success but United have looked pedestrian on far too many occasions this season.

This could explain the number of slow starts to games in recent times: in the Champions League against Atlético Madrid and Como they conceded in the first and second minute respectively, and were two down at home to Roma after 17 minutes last week.

SoftBank’s billion-dollar loss may have put a cap on AI’s natural gas ambitions
Tim De Chant9:00 AM PST · November 12, 2026
SoftBank might not be the first to invest in a hot trend, but when it does, it goes big.
Witness its $30 billion bet on OpenAIin early 2025or its announcement in February that its SB Energy subsidiary would spend $33 billion on a 9.2-gigawatt natural gas power plant. If you can’t be first, be biggest, I guess.
That philosophy apparently spilled over into procurement, where orders were also supersized. Starting about two years ago, SoftBankreportedlyput down deposits on more than 13 gigawatts of turbines, almost 50% more than it needed.
The decision to over-order undoubtedly helped secure turbines and speed up SoftBank’s projects.
“SB Energy did not have a choice except to overbook turbines in the future if they wanted some turbines right away,” Peter Gardett, CEO ofNoreva, told TechCrunch via email.
The energy world was caught off guard by the swiftness and magnitude of AI’s rising power demands. Queues for turbine orders now extendinto the early 2030s. As natural gas was shaping up to be a go-to power source for the AI boom, CEO Masayoshi Son bet that by deploying his investment firm’s significant war chest, he could corner a portion of the market. If the AI world wanted power for its data centers, it would have to come to him.
Now, that bet appears to have fizzled. SoftBank announced a$7.1 billion quarterly losson Tuesday, with over half of that stemming from losses related to power-generating equipment. The investor had paid turbine manufacturers nonrefundable deposits to secure orders, and now it considered much of those worthless.
The move was also a costly bit of price discovery, Gardett said. Rather than overpay and potentially still be short of turbines, SoftBank overpaid and over-ordered.
“This charge is just that price discovery finally happening,” Gardett said.
The magnitude of that misplaced bet — over $3 billion — reflects some of the electricity mania that has overtaken the AI world. Faced with years-long waits to connect to the grid, many hyperscalers and developers have turned to natural gas as a sort of energy security blanket, something that is proven and familiar.
As AI data centers spend more time in operation, their operators are getting a better feel for what’s required to keep them operating. Natural gas might seem like a safe bet, but there are still risks, including winter curtailments when supplies dip and demand spikes, Brent Nelson, senior managing director of markets and strategy atAscend Analytics, told theEquity podcastWednesday.
In light of that, Nelson said the grid might still be their best bet. Most data centers would be best served by a grid connection, albeit a smaller one than they might normally request. To make up for the shortfall, large batteries are a cost-effective choice, Nelson said. They’d help shave peak loads or ride out requests from the utility to curtail electricity use.
Data center operators might be coming to that same conclusion, leading the natural gas market to develop more slowly than SoftBank expected.
SoftBank’s natural gas-related losses are unlikely to have a domino effect, leading to mass cancellations of gas power plants. AI’s power demand appears to be too large for that. For now, natural gas is riding high, though SoftBank may have found its ceiling.

Earth's fiery birth may have created hundreds of oceans' worth of water
Date:November 12, 2026Source:University of New MexicoSummary:Earth's water may have been born in the planet's fiery atmosphere rather than delivered by icy comets or asteroids. Scientists discovered that rocky pebbles reacting with hydrogen under extreme heat can produce water in minutes, potentially generating hundreds of oceans' worth during Earth's formation. The findings suggest that water may be a natural part of how rocky planets form, rather than something that must arrive from space.Share:FacebookTwitterPinterestLinkedINEmailFULL STORYEarth may have created hundreds of oceans' worth of water in its fiery early atmosphere, suggesting that water, and potentially life, could be common throughout the universe. Credit: University of New Mexico
Earth may have created a substantial amount of its own water as the planet was forming, rather than relying entirely on comets, meteorites, or other objects to deliver it from space. New research published inNature Geosciencesuggests that chemical reactions between rocky pebbles and the hydrogen-rich atmosphere of the young Earth could have produced enormous quantities of water.
The discovery offers a new explanation for how our planet acquired one of the most important ingredients for life. It also raises the possibility that other rocky planets throughout the universe could generate water through similar processes, potentially making habitable worlds more common than previously thought.
Researchers at The University of New Mexico investigated this possibility by recreating some of the extreme conditions that existed during Earth's formation. The study was led by graduate student Susmita Garai, along with Zachary Sharp, professor and director of Earth and Planetary Sciences, and Peter Olson. Their experiments examined what happens when rocks containing iron react with hydrogen at extremely high temperatures.
"Previous ideas about the source of water to Earth rely on an external source, such as comets or meteorites. Here we show that virtually any Earth-sized planet should have water by this newly identified mechanism," explained Sharp. "In order to evaluate the possibility of 'pebble' rain' being a source of water, we needed to construct and execute some very challenging high-temperature experiments. Dr. Garai's efforts paid off mightily, as she found that water is produced in just minutes in the high temperature environment of the Early Earth's atmosphere."
A New Explanation for the Origin of Earth's Water
For decades, scientists have debated where Earth's water originally came from. One prominent theory suggests that much of it was transported to the developing planet by icy material originating in the colder, more distant regions of the early solar system.
According to this explanation, water-rich objects, including small icy pebbles, traveled inward and eventually contributed to Earth's water supply. However, researchers have struggled to fully explain how enough of this material could have reached our planet from such great distances. There are also unresolved questions about whether this delivery process accounts for Earth's chemical composition.
The new study investigates a different route by which water could have appeared. Instead of arriving already contained in ice or other materials, water may have been produced directly through reactions involving the rocky ingredients that built Earth and the gases surrounding it.
During the planet's earliest stages, countless small pieces of rock gradually came together to form a larger body. Scientists refer to this growth process as pebble accretion. As Earth gained mass, it could have accumulated a dense atmosphere containing large amounts of hydrogen, with temperatures and pressures far higher than those found on the planet today.
Under those conditions, rocky pebbles falling through the atmosphere could have triggered a remarkable chemical reaction. Hydrogen in the surrounding gas would react with iron oxide inside the silicate rocks, transforming the iron oxide into metallic iron while releasing water vapor.
Experiments Reveal Water Can Form in Minutes
To determine whether this process could actually occur, the researchers exposed samples of silicate rock to temperatures ranging from 1,200 to 1,400 degrees Celsius. They conducted experiments using flowing hydrogen gas and repeated the tests with helium to provide a comparison. Each experiment ran for between 15 minutes and three hours.
The results provided strong evidence that the proposed reaction works under these extreme conditions. When the rocks were heated in hydrogen, almost 80% of their iron oxide was transformed into metallic iron, with water vapor produced during the reaction.
In contrast, the researchers did not observe the same reaction when helium was used instead of hydrogen. This difference confirmed that hydrogen played a crucial role in generating the water.
The speed and scale of the reaction were especially striking. Although the scientists had expected some water to form, the results suggested that the process could have been far more productive than anticipated. When they extended their experimental findings to conditions on the early Earth, their calculations indicated that the mechanism might have generated hundreds of oceans' worth of water.
"We had suspected and hoped that we would produce iron metal and water in our reduction experiments, but we really had no way of knowing how fast and how much. We were quite surprised to find that extrapolation of our work suggests that hundreds of oceans' worth of water were likely produced in this way. Looking out over a large body of water, it is hard to imagine that that water may have been produced 4 ½ billion years ago in a hell-like atmosphere, but it very well may have," said Sharp.
Earth's Fiery Beginnings May Have Helped Create Its Oceans
These findings suggest that the conditions of Earth's formation may have actively contributed to its water supply. Rather than being entirely dependent on water delivered from elsewhere in the solar system, the growing planet may have possessed the ingredients needed to manufacture water through its own chemical reactions.

Scientists May Have Discovered a Massive Starless Galaxy | WIREDSkip to main content
Some galaxies appearto contain all the ingredients needed to make stars, yet have failed to produce almost any.
Scientists have puzzled over why for years. Recent findings suggest that these “dark galaxies”—that is, galaxies that contain gas and dark matter but few or no stars—may be lurking throughout the cosmos. Finding them could help astronomers understand why some galaxies form stars while others remain dark, and test the best models of galaxy formation.
Researchers’ most successful model of the cosmos, known as Lambda-CDM, assumes the existence of two invisible ingredients: dark energy, the mysterious property thought to be driving the accelerating expansion of the universe, as well as cold dark matter, a hypothetical substance that physicists think makes up about 85 percent of the universe’s matter.
Clumps of dark matter, called haloes, provide the gravitational scaffolding for galaxies to form and grow, according to the model. Gas collects inside these haloes, eventually cooling and collapsing to form stars. But astronomers are still trying to understand why this process appears to happen in some haloes but not others.
One possibility is that some contain vast quantities of hydrogen gas, yet form very few stars. That would make them extremely difficult to spot.
Now, researchers have found a promising candidate for such a dark galaxy and publishedtheir findingsin the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society. The object, known as AGC 322753, contains roughly 2 billion times the sun's mass in hydrogen, yet appears to have no stars, though the researchers note that it is too big to be totally starless. However, if confirmed, it would be an unusually massive example of a starless galaxy.
Researchers at Swinburne University of Technology in Australia made the discovery by comparing observations from two existing radio surveys, one conducted by the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico and the other by China's Five-Hundred-Meter Aperture Spherical Radio Telescope. Both telescopes had picked up a massive cloud of hydrogen.
Although other researchers have identified several dark galaxy candidates over the past decade, this one stands out for another reason: It may be rotating.
Hydrogen gas emits radio waves at a signature wavelength, which shortens when the gas moves toward Earth and stretches when it moves away. The signal from AGC 322753 shows two distinct peaks, suggesting that one side of the gas cloud is moving towards us while the other is receding.
This could mean that the gas has settled into an organized, rotating structure, much like the discs in ordinary galaxies, despite apparently having formed no stars.
"The theoretical models and the simulations show us that dark galaxies shouldn't rotate, so this is extremely interesting," says Marco Monaci, an author of the study at Swinburne University of Technology.
If AGC 322753 really is a rotating disc with no stars, astronomers will have to explain how the gas organized into such a structure without producing them.
That isn’t the only puzzle. Most models of galaxy formation predict that a cloud holding this much hydrogen should have formed at least a few stars, as its densest patches collapse under their own gravity and ignite.
The paper’s coauthors suggest it may be very unlikely that AGC 322753 contains absolutely no stars. So, instead, they think it may contain stars too faint to see–an “almost dark” galaxy. If so, they must be very faint indeed, because even deep optical images from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys, which search for starlight rather than the hydrogen gas detected by radio telescopes, reveal none.
From this, the team estimates that AGC322753 contains at least 40 times more mass in hydrogen than in stars, raising questions about what exactly suppressed stars from forming.
But further observations, such as ones made by the Very Large Array, a network of radio antennas in New Mexico, will be needed to confirm whether AGC 322573 is truly a dark—or almost dark—galaxy.
"Finding out more about it really is an essential next step at the moment. It's intriguing, and I want to know more," says Robert Minchin at the National Radio Astronomy Observatory.
Minchin knows how misleading such signals can be. He was involved in the discovery of VIRGOHI21, a dark galaxy candidate found in the early 2000s that was later reinterpreted as a long stream of hydrogen gas pulled from a nearby galaxy by gravity, known as a tidal tail.
Gas torn away like this can keep some of its original motion and mimic the signature of rotation, so Minchin says more observations are needed to rule out the same explanation for AGC 322753. Yet there is no obvious nearby galaxy it could have come from.
Rhys Taylor, an astronomer at the Astronomical Institute of the Czech Academy of Sciences in Prague, says tidal debris is unlikely to explain the observations. Reproducing the candidate dark galaxy’s distinctive double-peaked profile through such a process “is technically possible, but it’s fantastically unlikely,” Taylor says.
Taylor and Minchin both flag another concern, though. The two radio surveys that the researchers used placed the hydrogen at noticeably different positions in the sky. That suggests AGC 322753 may be an extended cloud of gas rather than a compact galaxy, another possibility that follow-up observations could help untangle.
Whether AGC 322753 turns out to be completely dark or merely exceptionally faint, understanding objects like it could still help astronomers work out why some galaxies form stars while others apparently do not, says Elisabeth Adams at the Planetary Science Institute.
One possible reason is a galaxy that spins so fast that its gas stays too spread out to collapse. Another is that ultraviolet light from the universe’s earliest stars heated the gas, keeping it too warm to condense. Studying such almost-dark galaxies could help tell these phenomena apart, revealing how the conditions of the early universe shaped the galaxies we see today.
“Once it’s no longer a dark galaxy, people seem to stop caring, and I actually think that’s not the right approach,” says Adams.

In the Grand Canyon, there is a line in the rock where time seems to have gone missing. Ancient crystalline rocks mark its bottom, while sandstones laid down as life started to diversify during the Cambrian explosion mark the top. “It’s called the Great Unconformity, and it’s a gap in the geologic record,” says Nicolas Flament, a geoscientist at the University of Wollongong, Australia. “This gap can be anywhere between 200 million years, which is not that impressive, to more than a billion years.”
In a recent Nature study, Flament and his colleague Santosh Dhungana argue that this gap was carved with help from deep within the planet. According to their models, slow currents of hot rock in Earth’s mantle pushed entire continents up for hundreds of millions of years, letting glaciers grind them down and then let them sink, allowing fresh sediments to bury the scar. The largest hole in the rock record might be a fingerprint of processes happening deep in the planet’s interior.
The oldest sediments resting on the Great Unconformity in North America are between 635 and 482 million years old. Geologists have traced it across most of North America and parts of northern Europe and northern China. “Something seems to have happened, in particular in North America,” Flament says.
The leading explanation was glaciation. Between roughly 720 and 635 million years ago, glaciers reached the tropics, and some scientists think the entire planet froze over, a scenario called Snowball Earth. “Ice sheets are very good at grinding, scouring, scraping the surface,” Flament explains. He said that glaciers are about 10 times more effective than rivers at eroding rock away. But if the whole planet froze, the Great Unconformity should be found everywhere. And it’s not.
Other explanations included rifting, pulling and stretching of Earth’s crust, and a global drop in sea levels. But rifting acts mostly on the edges of continents, and a sea level change should have affected all continents alike. “There’s no doubt that there was extensive glaciation. There’s no doubt that there have been sea-level changes throughout time. The question is, was that enough to put the Great Unconformity puzzle together?” Flament says.
A fourth idea held that the mantle itself was moving continents up and down, a process called dynamic topography. “It had been proposed, but it hadn’t been quantitatively tested,” Flament says. So, his team set out to do so.
From roughly 100 to 200 kilometers beneath the surface down to nearly 3,000 kilometers, Earth’s mantle slowly convects. “An analogy would be a lava lamp, where some stuff comes up and some stuff comes down,” Flament explains. “Cold rock sinks and hot rock rises.”
The mantle is solid, yet a piece of rock can slowly travel from the surface to the deep Earth over some 200 million years. That motion tugs on the surface. Where cold slabs of ocean floor sink into the mantle at subduction zones, the ground gets pulled down; where hot mantle rises, it gets pushed up. The amplitude of this up and down motion is still debated, though. “The short of it is several hundreds of meters, and it’s still to be worked out exactly what that [precise value] is,” Flament says.
Dhungana and Flament ran six simulations of mantle convection going back 1 billion years, driven by reconstructions of how tectonic plates moved over that time. Then they grouped regions where the ground rose and fell in similar ways to find where the unconformity should have formed, and where it should have survived to the present. Flament, however, says the starting configuration of these simulations remains uncertain.
Magnetic records in ancient rocks reveal how far continents were from the equator, but not their longitude. “It’s possible that some continents may be in the wrong hemisphere,” Flament admits. The ancient ocean floor, long since recycled into the mantle, had to be invented entirely from scratch in the models. Still, the simulations produced a consistent story.
Laurentia, the ancient core of North America, had little or no subduction along its margins between about 930 and 510 million years ago, much like Africa today, so it sat above some rising mantle and was pushed up. Five of the six models showed this pattern of Laurentia seeing long uplift followed by sinking in the Cambrian. For northern Europe and North China, this pattern showed up in four.
But the uplift alone, Flament’s team concluded, was too gentle to strip away enough rock to create the Great Unconformity.
“The uplift could create a tilt for the whole continent, but it’s not great at creating a steep slope,” Flament says. The missing piece of the puzzle, he argues, were glaciers that ground through rock even on low ground and gentle slopes. The models show the uplift was still building when Snowball Earth hit. “This gentle uplift that’s continuous, and then that glacial erosion that comes on top, work together,” Flament explains. “They’re not coupled. They just happen to coincide in time.” When the continents sank in the Cambrian, seas flooded in and buried the eroded surface.
The models made by Flament’s team also explain why the gap is so obvious in North America but hard to find elsewhere. Compared with records of sediment preserved on each continent, North America and Eurasia show one long rise followed by one long fall, which the researchers interpret as the ideal recipe for the Great Unconformity.
South America and Australia, on the other hand, went through two cycles. “This would form potentially two unconformities, and then the Great Unconformity would be more difficult to see,” Flament says. Africa was a different case altogether—hemmed in by mountain belts at the time, its erosion and sediment were shaped by the mountains rather than by the mantle beneath.
But if the mantle goes through such up and down cycles on a regular basis, the remaining question was why we can see only one Great Unconformity, and not many.
The team says the Great Unconformity is unique in the geological record because of a combination of a rise-and-fall cycle lasting over 900 million years, a near-global glaciation that happened at the right moment, and rock records that get harder to read farther back in time.

fact_units.text: SoftBank’s billion-dollar loss may have put a cap on AI's natural gas ambitions | TechCrunch
SoftBank’s billion-dollar loss may have put a cap on AI’s natural gas ambitions
Tim De Chant9:00 AM PST · November 12, 2026
SoftBank might not be the first to invest in a hot trend, but when it does, it goes big.
Witness its $30 billion bet on OpenAIin early 2025or its announcement in February that its SB Energy subsidiary would spend $33 billion on a 9.2-gigawatt natural gas power plant.
If you can’t be first, be biggest, I guess.
That philosophy apparently spilled over into procurement, where orders were also supersized.
Starting about two years ago, SoftBankreportedlyput down deposits on more than 13 gigawatts of turbines, almost 50% more than it needed.
The decision to over-order undoubtedly helped secure turbines and speed up SoftBank’s projects.
“SB Energy did not have a choice except to overbook turbines in the future if they wanted some turbines right away,” Peter Gardett, CEO ofNoreva, told TechCrunch via email.
The energy world was caught off guard by the swiftness and magnitude of AI’s rising power demands.
Queues for turbine orders now extendinto the early 2030s.
As natural gas was shaping up to be a go-to power source for the AI boom, CEO Masayoshi Son bet that by deploying his investment firm’s significant war chest, he could corner a portion of the market.
If the AI world wanted power for its data centers, it would have to come to him.
SoftBank announced a$7.1 billion quarterly losson Tuesday, with over half of that stemming from losses related to power-generating equipment.
The investor had paid turbine manufacturers nonrefundable deposits to secure orders, and now it considered much of those worthless.
The move was also a costly bit of price discovery, Gardett said.
Rather than overpay and potentially still be short of turbines, SoftBank overpaid and over-ordered.
“This charge is just that price discovery finally happening,” Gardett said.
The magnitude of that misplaced bet — over $3 billion — reflects some of the electricity mania that has overtaken the AI world.
Faced with years-long waits to connect to the grid, many hyperscalers and developers have turned to natural gas as a sort of energy security blanket, something that is proven and familiar.
As AI data centers spend more time in operation, their operators are getting a better feel for what’s required to keep them operating.

Natural gas might seem like a safe bet, but there are still risks, including winter curtailments when supplies dip and demand spikes, Brent Nelson, senior managing director of markets and strategy atAscend Analytics, told theEquity podcastWednesday.
In light of that, Nelson said the grid might still be their best bet.
Most data centers would be best served by a grid connection, albeit a smaller one than they might normally request.
To make up for the shortfall, large batteries are a cost-effective choice, Nelson said.
They’d help shave peak loads or ride out requests from the utility to curtail electricity use.
Data center operators might be coming to that same conclusion, leading the natural gas market to develop more slowly than SoftBank expected.
SoftBank’s natural gas-related losses are unlikely to have a domino effect, leading to mass cancellations of gas power plants.
AI’s power demand appears to be too large for that.
For now, natural gas is riding high, though SoftBank may have found its ceiling.

evidence_pages.https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/nvidia-c:
Nvidia's leadership crisis could test its $500 billion AI financing betSkip Navigation
MarketsBusinessInvestingTechPolitics & PolicyVideoWatchlistInvesting ClubPROLivestreamMenu
Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia president, CEO and board member, the company's board said Thursday.
The chip giant announced in August memorandums of understanding with six major financial firms aimed at mobilizing more than $500 billion for AI infrastructure.
Huang's departure could see further scrutiny of those arrangements amid growing uncertainty over Nvidia's direction.
Follow your favorite stocksCREATE FREE ACCOUNT
Leadership change atNvidiahas the potential to threaten financing of the artificial intelligence boom and test Jensen Huang's $500 billion vision to turn AI chips into tradable debt securities.
TheNvidia CEO's resignation was announced Thursdayfollowing revelations that he had two extramarital affairs — one with an employee and the other with a woman believed by U.S. intelligence to be aChinese spy.
Shares in the tech giant — which has become central to the AI build-out in recent years — initially plunged more than 13% following Huang's resignation, before paring losses.
Nvidia has never identified a successor to Huang, who has led the chipmaker since its founding in 1993. Colette Kress, chief financial officer, has been named interim CEO.
The company has been dubbed the "central bank" of the AI build-out, with Huang seen as the "hypeman" for the sector and its chips considered the industry's gold standard.
Huang's departure raises a central question: whether his successor can carry forward a financing strategy designed to transform GPUs from rapidly depreciating hardware into bankable infrastructure assets
The $4.2 trillion firm's industry dominance, with Huang front and center, allowed it to sign memorandums of understanding with some of Wall Street's biggest asset managers, intended to secure third-party capital for alandmark $500 billion AI financing drive.
The preliminary agreements, involvingApollo Global Management,BlackRock,Blackstone,Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, andKKR, sought to tap institutional investors and private capital to finance a range of computing infrastructure, including data centers and chip factories. The funding would involve specialized financing vehicles, with Nvidia's AI chips used as underlying collateral, in arrangements comparable to real estate or toll roads securitizations.
The financing arrangements are still preliminary and subject to final agreements.
BlackRock and Goldman Sachs declined to comment on today's resignation. The other firms weren't immediately available for comment.
The arrangements could now face heightened scrutiny in the aftermath of Huang's departure.
Sunaina Sinha Haldea, global head of private capital advisory at Raymond James, said a leadership change gives every firm involved a "natural moment to pause and look at the terms again."
"The best thing a new CEO can do is leave these partnerships alone in the first few months and focus on getting the final agreements signed," Haldea told CNBC via email. "Jensen brought these firms to the table with his vision, and any potential successor will keep them there by showing that the business behind that vision hasn't changed."
She added: "I don't think the capital walks away, because these lenders are underwriting Nvidia's chips and the customer contracts behind them, but they could want to be paid more for the uncertainty."
Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo, said Huang's successor would need to reassure lenders that Nvidia's technology roadmap, customer relationships and strategic vision remain intact.
"I wouldn't expect Nvidia's financing partnerships to unravel simply because Huang leaves, but a leadership shake-up could make Wall Street more cautious, potentially slowing commitments or tightening financing terms," Chanana told CNBC via email.
"The bigger risk is a ripple effect across AI financing, particularly when rising debt, circular financing and uncertain investment returns were already under scrutiny," Chanana added. "This is not a financing crisis yet, but it could become a catalyst for a broader repricing of risk across the AI ecosystem."
Haldea added that she expects to see more discipline among investors in the aftermath of the scandal. "Lenders will ask harder questions about who is really carrying the risk in these structures, and that scrutiny will spread throughout the AI infrastructure deal market."

Jensen Huang agrees to testify before Congress | TechCrunch
8:36 AM PST · November 12, 2026Image Credits:Jose Sarmento Matos/Bloomberg / Getty Images
Jensen Huang agrees to testify before Congress
Ex-Nvidia CEOJensen Huanghas agreed to testify before Congress, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said on Thursday, according to reports fromBloombergandNBC News.
Huang, who stepped down as CEO following reports of an alleged affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, agreed to testify Wednesday after several senior lawmakers threatened to subpoena him.
Huang has agreed to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving, which falls later this month.
The development comes after House Republicans Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford sent Huang a letter on November 4 requesting thathe appear before their committees. Moolenaar chairs the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, Mast chairs the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and Crawford chairs the House Intelligence Committee.
“Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” Mast said to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.”
The testimony will take place behind closed doors, though Mast said he expects the briefing to be recorded on video and transcribed.

Cổ phiếu Nvidia lao dốc, bốc hơi 601 tỉ USD vốn hóa sau khi CEO Jensen Huang từ chức
Cổ phiếu Nvidia có lúc giảm tới 14% ngay khi mở cửa phiên 12-11 (giờ Mỹ), làm bốc hơi 601 tỉ USD vốn hóa, sau khi CEO Jensen Huang tuyên bố từ chức vì bê bối ngoại tình.
Cổ phiếu Nvidia lao dốc sau khi ông Jensen Huang từ chức - Ảnh: FINANCIAL EXPRESS
Theo Hãng tin Bloomberg, cổ phiếu Tập đoàn Nvidia lao dốc ngay khi mở cửa phiên giao dịch ngày 12-11, kéo vốn hóa thị trường của nhà sản xuất chip này xuống dưới ngưỡng 4.000 tỉ USD, lần đầu tiên kể từ năm 2025.
Động thái này diễn ra sau khi Giám đốc điều hành (CEO)Jensen Huangtuyên bố từ chức, liên quan đến bê bối ngoại tình với hai phụ nữ, trong đó một người bị nghi là gián điệp Trung Quốc.
Trong phiên đầu giờ, cổ phiếu Nvidia có lúc giảm tới 14%, chạm mức thấp nhất kể từ tháng 6-2025 và làm bốc hơi 601 tỉ USD vốn hóa. Nếu đà giảm này duy trì đến lúc đóng cửa, đây sẽ là phiên mất vốn hóa trong một ngày lớn nhất lịch sử đối với một mã cổ phiếu.
Tính từ mức đỉnh kỷ lục hồi đầu tháng 10, cổ phiếu Nvidia đã mất khoảng 35% giá trị, tương đương 2.000 tỉ USD vốn hóa chỉ trong vài tuần. Với mức định giá hiện dưới 3.800 tỉ USD, doanh nghiệp từng là công ty lớn nhất thế giới hiện đã bị Apple và Microsoft vượt mặt.
Trung Quốc nhắn nhủ Mỹ vụ CEO Nvidia Jensen HuangĐỌC NGAY
"Tôi chưa từng chứng kiến điều gì tương tự, chúng ta đang bước vào một vùng biến động chưa từng có tiền lệ. Trên thang điểm từ 1 đến 10, mức độ nghiêm trọng của sự việc này là 10", ông Ted Mortonson, chiến lược gia công nghệ tại Công ty tài chính Robert W. Baird & Co., nhận định.
Khả năng tiếp tục lèo lái công ty sản xuất chip trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI) quan trọng nhất thế giới của ông Huang bị đặt dấu hỏi lớn từ ngày 8-11, khi ông thừa nhận không chung thủy với vợ.
Người được đồn đoán có quan hệ tình cảm với ông là bà Alice Huang, cựu CEO Công ty trung tâm dữ liệu Megaspeed International (Singapore), hiện bị nghi hoạt động gián điệp cho Trung Quốc.
Đến ngày 11-11, tờNew York Timesdẫn các nguồn tin ẩn danh từng làm việc tại Nvidia cho biết ông Huang còn có quan hệ tình cảm với bà Kimberly Powell, Phó chủ tịch phụ trách mảng y tế của chính tập đoàn.
Trước giờ mở cửa thị trường ngày 12-11, Nvidia chính thức thông báo ông Huang rời vị trí, đồng thời bổ nhiệm Giám đốc tài chính (CFO)Colette Kresslàm CEO tạm thời và thành viên hội đồng quản trị Harvey Jones làm Chủ tịch đầu tiên trong lịch sử công ty.
Thông tin được đưa ra ngay trước thềm công bố báo cáo tài chính quý 3 vào ngày 17-11. Dù công ty được kỳ vọng tăng trưởng mạnh nhờ nhu cầu chip AI duy trì ở mức cao, các bê bối đời tư đang khiến giới đầu tư và phân tích đồng loạt bán tháo cổ phiếu Nvidia.
Trong tuần qua, ít nhất bảy công ty tài chính lớn tại Phố Wall đã hạ khuyến nghị đối với cổ phiếu Nvidia, còn chi phí bảo hiểm rủi ro vỡ nợ đối với các khoản nợ của tập đoàn cũng tiến sát mức cao kỷ lục.
Tính từ đầu năm 2026, cổ phiếu Nvidia đã giảm 15% và đang hướng tới năm tồi tệ nhất kể từ 2022.
Cấp dưới ở Nvidia bị tố ngoại tình với CEO Jensen Huang là ai?
Sau vụ bà Alice Huang, CEO Nvidia Jensen Huang tiếp tục vướng nghi vấn ngoại tình với cấp dưới là bà Kimberly Powell - Phó chủ tịch phụ trách mảng y tế của Nvidia.

fact_units.text: Nvidia's leadership crisis could test its $500 billion AI financing betSkip Navigation
Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia president, CEO and board member, the company's board said Thursday.
The chip giant announced in August memorandums of understanding with six major financial firms aimed at mobilizing more than $500 billion for AI infrastructure.
Huang's departure could see further scrutiny of those arrangements amid growing uncertainty over Nvidia's direction.
Leadership change atNvidiahas the potential to threaten financing of the artificial intelligence boom and test Jensen Huang's $500 billion vision to turn AI chips into tradable debt securities.
TheNvidia CEO's resignation was announced Thursdayfollowing revelations that he had two extramarital affairs — one with an employee and the other with a woman believed by U.S.
Shares in the tech giant — which has become central to the AI build-out in recent years — initially plunged more than 13% following Huang's resignation, before paring losses.
Nvidia has never identified a successor to Huang, who has led the chipmaker since its founding in 1993.
Colette Kress, chief financial officer, has been named interim CEO.
The company has been dubbed the "central bank" of the AI build-out, with Huang seen as the "hypeman" for the sector and its chips considered the industry's gold standard.

Huang's departure raises a central question: whether his successor can carry forward a financing strategy designed to transform GPUs from rapidly depreciating hardware into bankable infrastructure assets

The $4.2 trillion firm's industry dominance, with Huang front and center, allowed it to sign memorandums of understanding with some of Wall Street's biggest asset managers, intended to secure third-party capital for alandmark $500 billion AI financing drive.

The preliminary agreements, involvingApollo Global Management,BlackRock,Blackstone,Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, andKKR, sought to tap institutional investors and private capital to finance a range of computing infrastructure, including data centers and chip factories.
The funding would involve specialized financing vehicles, with Nvidia's AI chips used as underlying collateral, in arrangements comparable to real estate or toll roads securitizations.
The financing arrangements are still preliminary and subject to final agreements.
BlackRock and Goldman Sachs declined to comment on today's resignation.
The arrangements could now face heightened scrutiny in the aftermath of Huang's departure.
Sunaina Sinha Haldea, global head of private capital advisory at Raymond James, said a leadership change gives every firm involved a "natural moment to pause and look at the terms again."
"The best thing a new CEO can do is leave these partnerships alone in the first few months and focus on getting the final agreements signed," Haldea told CNBC via email.
"Jensen brought these firms to the table with his vision, and any potential successor will keep them there by showing that the business behind that vision hasn't changed."

She added: "I don't think the capital walks away, because these lenders are underwriting Nvidia's chips and the customer contracts behind them, but they could want to be paid more for the uncertainty."
Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo, said Huang's successor would need to reassure lenders that Nvidia's technology roadmap, customer relationships and strategic vision remain intact.

"I wouldn't expect Nvidia's financing partnerships to unravel simply because Huang leaves, but a leadership shake-up could make Wall Street more cautious, potentially slowing commitments or tightening financing terms," Chanana told CNBC via email.
"The bigger risk is a ripple effect across AI financing, particularly when rising debt, circular financing and uncertain investment returns were already under scrutiny," Chanana added.
"This is not a financing crisis yet, but it could become a catalyst for a broader repricing of risk across the AI ecosystem."
Haldea added that she expects to see more discipline among investors in the aftermath of the scandal.
"Lenders will ask harder questions about who is really carrying the risk in these structures, and that scrutiny will spread throughout the AI infrastructure deal market."

Jensen Huang agrees to testify before Congress | TechCrunch
8:36 AM PST · November 12, 2026Image Credits:Jose Sarmento Matos/Bloomberg / Getty Images
Ex-Nvidia CEOJensen Huanghas agreed to testify before Congress, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said on Thursday, according to reports fromBloombergandNBC News.

Huang, who stepped down as CEO following reports of an alleged affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, agreed to testify Wednesday after several senior lawmakers threatened to subpoena him.
Huang has agreed to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving, which falls later this month.
The development comes after House Republicans Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford sent Huang a letter on November 4 requesting thathe appear before their committees.
Moolenaar chairs the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, Mast chairs the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and Crawford chairs the House Intelligence Committee.
“Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” Mast said to reporters.
“I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.”
The testimony will take place behind closed doors, though Mast said he expects the briefing to be recorded on video and transcribed.

lead_title: Israeli Strikes on Gaza Hospital Kill 6 and Injure Dozens, Health Officials Say

evidence_pages.https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/11/world:
Israeli Strikes on Gaza Hospital Kill 6 and Injure Dozens, Health Officials Say - The New York Times
Middle East|Israeli Strikes on Gaza Hospital Kill 6 and Injure Dozens, Health Officials Sayhttps://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/11/world/middleeast/nasser-hospital-gaza-strike-israel.html
The Israeli military struck a hospital in the southern Gaza Strip on Thursday, killing at least six people and injuring 28 more, according to local health officials.
Dr. Ahmed al-Farra, general director of Nasser Hospital, said in a news conference on Thursday that two missiles had hit the facility and that among the dead was Rezeq Abu Shaira, 52, a doctor.
Health officials reached in Gaza by phone said that a man called Khaled Abu Anza had also been killed. A spokeswoman for the Israeli military, speaking on condition of anonymity in line with protocol, said that Mr. Abu Anza was a Hamas operative.
The Israeli security agency and military said in ajoint statementon Thursday that they had targeted Muhammad Abu Ismail, whom they identified as a Hamas commander “responsible for holding numerous hostages captive” during the Gaza war.
The Israeli authorities said that Hamas had established a command center at the hospital complex to stage operations against Israeli forces and was storing weapons there. They added that steps had been taken to mitigate harm to civilians.
Hamas said the Israeli claim that the hospital was used for military activity was a “blatant attempt to justify a heinous crime targeting a civilian medical facility.” Residents of Gazahave saidthat officials affiliated with Hamas-run Gaza government and security forces sometimes use the enclave’s hospitals as offices.
ImageMourners on Thursday carrying the body of a victim of the Israeli strike.Credit...Ramadan Abed/Reuters
In a statement, Gaza’s health ministry condemned the attack, calling it a “flagrant violation of international laws and conventions.” It did not respond to the Israeli claims.
Nasser Hospital, in Khan Younis, is the largest functioning hospital in southern Gaza. Video recorded in the facility, distributed by The Associated Press, showed remains of the munitions used in the attack.
Trevor Ball, a former explosive-ordnance disposal technician for the U.S. Army who is now an analyst at Armament Research Services, a consulting firm, said that the footage showed two 250-pound precision-guided, American-manufactured aerial bombs. In the footage, it appeared that one of the bombs had failed to detonate after penetrating the building. A serial number was still visible on the warhead.
Naseem Hassan, an emergency medical worker at Nasser Hospital, said in the hours after the attack that missiles had hit a four-story building in the hospital complex, damaging the surgery department.
The attack comes more than a year into a cease-fire between Israel and Hamas that has not brought an end to Israeli military strikes in Gaza and that has done little to alleviate thedire and deadly living conditionsfor the enclave’s two million residents.
Israel has continued to carry out frequent strikes in Gaza despite a U.S.-brokered cease-fire that Israel and Hamas agreed to in October 2025. More than 1,600 people have been killed by Israeli fire during the cease-fire,according to Gaza’s health ministry, which does not distinguish between civilians and combatants in its death tolls.
Nasser Hospital has been struck by the Israeli military multiple times since the Hamas-led attack on Israel on Oct. 7, 2023, prompted a devastating Israeli military response in Gaza. More than 74,000 people have been killed in the war, according to the health ministry.
In August last year, 20 people — including medical staff, rescue workers, patients and journalists — were killed in astrike on the hospitalthat drew a rare admission of error from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel, who called it a “tragic mishap.”
James McManagancontributed reporting.
An earlier version of this article, using information from an emergency worker, said that Khaled Abu Anza had been killed and that he was the governor of Khan Younis. Mr. Abu Anza was among the dead, but he was not the governor. The emergency worker also said that guards and a disabled patient had been killed in the attack; it is unclear whether they had been killed.
We acknowledge mistakes in our reporting with corrections. If you spot an error, please let us know atcorrections@nytimes.com.Learn more.
Ephrat Livni is a Times reporter covering news around the world. She is based in New York.

Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six Palestinians, health ministry says - BBC News
Surgeon films damage in Nasser hospital in Gaza
ByRushdi Abualouf,Gaza correspondent,Reporting fromIstanbul,David GrittenandClaire Keenan
Published12 November 2026, 03:32 GMT
Six people have been killed and about 30 injured in an Israeli air strike on Nasser hospital in the southern Gaza Strip, the Hamas-run health ministry says.
The hospital's director said two missiles hit a building containing surgical wards and intensive care units overnight, but that one of the missiles did not explode.
The health ministry said medical staff, patients and companions were killed, among them surgeon Dr Rizq Abu Shaira. It condemned the attack as a "flagrant violation of international laws and conventions".
The Israeli military said it targeted a commander of Hamas's armed wing and other fighters who had used the hospital as a "headquarters" to plan attacks on its forces.
Hamas said that Israel was spreading "false narratives" in a "blatant attempt to cover up a new war crime".
Under international law, hospitals have a protected status, but they have been repeatedly targeted during the Gaza war.
Israel accuses Hamas, which retains security control of parts of Gaza not occupied by Israeli troops, of cynically exploiting civilian infrastructure. It says the group stores weapons and runs command and control rooms in hospitals, which Hamas denies.
Israel does not allow international news organisations, including the BBC, into Gaza, making it difficult to verify what is happening in the territory.
Pictures showed extensive damage to an operating theatre, wards and a sleeping area for medics
The Nasser Medical Complex is located in the city of Khan Younis and is the largest hospital in southern Gaza, serving almost one million people.
In a video posted on social media, a paramedic from the Hamas-run Civil Defence agency who arrived at the building after the strike early on Thursday said a missile penetrated the five-storey structure and hit a room in the surgical department.
Other footage shared by activists showed thick smoke inside the building and extensive destruction on the second floor, where medical equipment and beds had been scattered by an explosion.
The hospital's director, Dr Ahmed al-Fara, later told a news conference that Israeli forces had fired two missiles at the al-Yasin surgery building but that only one exploded.
"What's happened in Nasser Medical Complex is targeting the health sector mainly. We are talking about doctors, we are talking about civilians, we are talking about patients," he said.
"Also, there is... huge damage [to] the infrastructure inside the hospital."
Footage filmed by a freelance journalist working for the BBC showed extensive damage to an operating theatre, wards and a sleeping area for medics, as well as hallways and lifts.
News agencies also published photos that appeared to show an unexploded missile.
Image source,Anadolu via Getty ImagesImage caption,
Photographs appeared to show an unexploded missile inside Nasser hospital's surgical building
Dr Mohammed Qdeih, a general surgery specialist who was wounded in the head, said he and other medical staff had just finished work around 00:30 and had been preparing to go to sleep when there was an explosion.
"My whole body was trapped under the rubble. For a moment, I felt as if I was about to lose consciousness, or that I was about to die," he told the BBC.
"I started struggling to free myself and started calling out, 'Guys! Guys!' I began crawling, trying to pull my leg out from beneath the rubble. I managed to pull myself free. It was dark, there were no lights, nothing at all."
He said he had been lying in a bed near Dr Rizq Abu Shaira, who was killed. Another colleague suffered a broken leg.
"Dr Rizq was the kindest person in this department. He was very kind and always willing to help... And of course, he was a surgeon, one of the best among us."
He added: "Patients were killed as well. There were patients in the rooms next to us who were killed. A patient comes to the hospital seeking treatment and leaves carried on people's shoulders. I do not know what kind of humanity this is."
Gaza's health ministry said surgeon Dr Rizq Abu Shaira was among those killed
The Israeli military said in a statement that its "precise strike" had targeted the commander of Hamas's Khan Younis Brigade, who it named as Mohammed Abu Ismail, alongside other fighters who were "hiding inside" Nasser hospital.
"The terrorists were struck in order to remove the threat they posed after turning the Nasser hospital compound into a headquarters and operating from there to advance dozens of terrorist plots against our forces and restore the brigade's force," it alleged.
The military added that it had issued advance warnings before the strike and released an audio recording of what it said was one given to a senior Gaza health official. But Fara insisted the hospital had received no warning of an attack.
A Hamas statement rejected the Israeli military's accusations, calling them "a blatant attempt to justify a documented crime targeting a civilian medical facility whose function and purpose are well known".
"The nature of the targeted site and the casualties inflicted on patients, doctors and medical staff expose the falsity and weakness of this narrative," it said.
However, local activists circulated claims overnight that the strike may have targeted a senior Hamas security figure who was hiding inside the building.
Fara said this was the seventh time that Nasser hospital had been struck during the war. In August 2025, a double Israeli strike killed 22 Palestinians, including journalists and health workers.
The World Health Organization (WHO) said it had documented a total of 1,056 attacks on healthcare in Gaza over the past three years, resulting in 1,010 deaths.
"Gaza's health facilities are lifelines for its people. They must be protected. They must never be militarized or attacked," warned Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the UN agency's director general.
Later on Thursday, at least four more Palestinians were reportedly killed in separate incidents in northern and central Gaza.
Medics said three were killed in Israeli air strikes in Gaza City, Jabalia and Deir al-Balah, while the fourth was killed by Israeli gunfire in Bureij refugee camp.
The Israeli military said it struck a "terrorist" in Deir al-Balah and another in Gaza City.

Israel kills six in Gaza hospital strike as 9-month-old baby freezes to death
An overnight Israeli air strike on Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza killed at least six Palestinians Thursday, including a teenage boy and a surgeon, medics said. Elsewhere in the devastated Palestinian territory, a nine-month-old baby died from the cold as families flee worsening flooding.
4 minReading timeShareBy:FRANCE 24A Palestinian man inspects damage inside a building at Nasser Hospital hit by an Israeli air strike in Khan Younis, in the southern Gaza Strip, November 12, 2026. © Ramadan Abed, Reuters
An Israeli air strike on southern Gaza's mainhospitalovernight killed at least six Palestinians including a surgeon and a teenage boy, medics said, the latest Israeli attack to undermine a year-oldceasefirein the ravaged territory.
The strike hit a building containing surgery wards at Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis.Israel's ​military alleged it had ‌targeted a seniorHamascommander and accused the militants of using the hospital complex to plan attacks, which ⁠the group denied.
Medics and witnesses said two missiles crashed through the roof of the five-storey building, causing extensive damage. The surgery department, which serves half of Gaza's 2 million people, was knocked out of service. ‌Twenty others were wounded.
Ayman Abu Obeid, a doctor who was wounded in the attack, said he was on ⁠an overnight shift in the hospital when an explosion ripped through the room where he and others were sleeping.
"All of a sudden the world turned upside down. It went dark all at once," he said from a hospital bed. Near him, piles ​of mangled furniture and medical equipment could be seen covered in dust from blown-out concrete. Torn wires hung down ‌from the ceiling.
Among those killed was Rezik Abushira, a surgeon who was featured ina 2026 documentary, "American Doctor", working alongside three visiting US doctors who help provide medical care for Palestinians in Gaza.
The dead also included a 13-year-old boy, according to Gaza's education ministry.
Mourners carry the body of Dr. Rezik Abushira, who was killed in an Israeli strike at Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, according to the Gaza health ministry, during his funeral in Khan Younis, southern Gaza Strip, November 12, 2026. © Ramadan Abed, Reuters
Three more Palestinians were killed later on Thursday in separate ‌incidents. Two were killed and several wounded in an Israeli airstrike on a car in Gaza City, and one other person was killed by Israeli gunfire in central Gaza's Bureij refugee camp, medics said, ​taking Thursday's death toll to at least nine.
Commenting on the vehicle strike, the Israeli military said it hit a Hamas militant without giving further details. It did not comment on the other incident.
In a statement on the hospital strike, Israel's ​military said it targeted a person named Muhammad Abu Ismail, describing him as "the commander of Hamas' Khan Younis Brigade". The military alleged he and other ​militants "were hiding inside the Nasser Hospital".
The military accused the militants of "turning the Nasser Hospital compound into a ​headquarters and operating from there".
Hamas rejected the military's claim that it had used the hospital as a base for operations. It did not immediately comment on whether a leader from the group had ​been targeted, wounded or killed in the strike.
Israel's military has struck the Nasser Hospital complexat least seven timessince the start of the Gaza war, hospital officials say.
Nine-month-old baby freezes to death
Heavy rain last weekflooded tens of thousands of people's tents in the Palestinian territory, where virtually the whole population has been displaced at least once by three years of Israeli bombardment.
Five people, including three children, died the day after the flooding when a sandy embankment collapsed onto their tents.
The worsening weather continues to take a heavy toll.
A nine-month-old baby died of hypothermia on Thursday, his father and a doctor told AFP.
The doctor, who saw the child and spoke on condition of anonymity, said that nine-month-old Kinan Ahmed Raqiq "died from hypothermia inside his family's displacement tent" in Khan Younis.
Ahmed Raqiq told AFP that his son Kinan died of cold during the night in their tent in southern Gaza.
"I woke up only to see his skin had turned blue so I rushed him to Nasser hospital, but he had already died from hypothermia and frozen to death," he said.
"I am in complete shock. I found myself holding my son wrapped in burial shroud," he said outside the hospital, dried tears on his face as he held his son wrapped in a white sheet.
Read morePalestinians struggle to find food in Gaza a year after ceasefire
Hundreds of displaced families have been seen fleeing camps in parts of Gaza City and central and northern areas of the territory after they were inundated by rainwater.
James Elder, spokesman on Gaza for the UN children's agency,UNICEF, warned that the flooding was just the beginning of the cold season.
"It's very important to know how bad things are in Gaza. It's not yet winter," Elder said.
"We're weeks away from winter, so we are getting unprecedented rain and cold."
A Palestinian family gathers around a fire inside a tent on a cold day in Gaza City, November 11, 2026. © Mahmoud Issa, Reuters
TheUN's Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said that as of November 8, 26,000 households were affected by storms.
Around 65 percent of Gaza's people are still living displaced in tents or other temporary shelter, OCHA said.
Israel and Hamas declared a ceasefire on October 10, 2025 but Israel has kept striking the territory, vowing to kill anyone involved inthe Hamas-led October 7 attack, the deadliest in Israel's history.

article.title: Harry Kane hướng tới cột mốc lịch sử cùng đội tuyển Anh và tham vọng danh hiệu lớn
article.summary: Tiền đạo Harry Kane chuẩn bị có trận đấu thứ 126 kỷ lục cho đội tuyển Anh, vượt qua Peter Shilton, đồng thời đặt mục tiêu chinh phục các danh hiệu lớn như World Cup, Euro và Champions League sau khi giành Quả bóng vàng.
body: Tiền đạo Harry Kane chuẩn bị thiết lập cột mốc lịch sử khi bước ra sân trong trận đấu thuộc khuôn khổ UEFA Nations League gặp Croatia tại sân vận động Wembley. Trận đấu này sẽ đánh dấu lần khoác áo thứ 126 của Kane cho đội tuyển quốc gia, giúp anh vượt qua thủ thành Peter Shilton để trở thành cầu thủ có số lần ra sân nhiều nhất trong lịch sử bóng đá nam đội tuyển Anh.

Cột mốc đáng nhớ này diễn ra trong bối cảnh chân sút 33 tuổi vừa được vinh danh là cầu thủ xuất sắc nhất thế giới với giải thưởng Quả bóng vàng vào cuối tháng trước. Chia sẻ trong buổi họp báo trước trận đấu, đội trưởng tuyển Anh khẳng định những danh hiệu cá nhân là thành quả của quá trình nỗ lực tập thể, đồng thời bày tỏ khát vọng vươn tới những đỉnh cao mới ở cả cấp độ câu lạc bộ lẫn đội tuyển quốc gia.

"Để giành được một danh hiệu lớn cùng đội tuyển Anh luôn là giấc mơ lớn nhất của tôi," Kane chia sẻ về mục tiêu vô địch Giải vô địch châu Âu hoặc World Cup. Ở cấp độ câu lạc bộ, sau khi giành các chức vô địch Bundesliga liên tiếp và cúp quốc gia Đức cùng Bayern Munich, tiền đạo này nhấn mạnh mục tiêu tiếp theo là chinh phục cúp C1 châu Âu Champions League.

Hành trình sự nghiệp của Kane đã trải qua nhiều thăng trầm, từ giai đoạn khởi đầu tại các đội trẻ cho đến 10 mùa giải gắn bó với Tottenham Hotspur mà không giành được danh hiệu tập thể lớn nào. Tuy nhiên, anh thừa nhận những khó khăn và thất bại trong quá khứ đã tạo động lực mạnh mẽ để bản thân không ngừng hoàn thiện. Dưới sự dẫn dắt của huấn luyện viên Thomas Tuchel, trận đấu sắp tới không chỉ là dịp tôn vinh kỷ lục ra sân của Kane mà còn là thời điểm để anh cùng các đồng đội tiếp tục khẳng định tham vọng giành các danh hiệu đỉnh cao.

Hơn 6 triệu lượt xem màn tốt nghiệp độc lạ, ChatGPT và Claude bất ngờ xuất hiện
Hưng Lợi12/11/2026 09:25 GMT+7Chia sẻChọn BáoThanh Niênlàmnguồn ưu tiêntrên Google tìm kiếm.Xem hướng dẫn.BƯỚC1Nhấp vào nút"ThêmThanh Niêntrên Google"hoặc mở trực tiếp đường dẫn này:https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thanhnien.vnBƯỚC2Tại trang vừa mở, tìm dòng"BáoThanh Niên"và bấm vào ô vuông bên phải.Khi ô vuông chuyển thành dấu tích xanh là bạn đã thành công rồi!LƯU Ý NHỎ:Nếu muốn kiểm tra xem cài đặt còn hiệu lực không, bạn chỉ cầnmở lại link trênlà thấy ngaydấu tích xanhvẫn đang hiển thị.Chúc bạn đọc báo vui vẻ!Thay vì xuất hiện một mình trong lễ phục cử nhân, Trần Thị Phương Thảo (tân cử nhân ngành digital marketing, Trường ĐH FPT TP.HCM đã rủ hai người bạn hóa thân thành ChatGPT và Claude để cùng mình bước lên sân khấu nhận bằng.
Chia sẻ về ý tưởng này, Phương Thảo cho biết ChatGPT là một trong những người bạn đồng hành đặc biệt trong suốt những năm đại học. Bên cạnh thầy cô và bạn bè, các công cụ AI đã hỗ trợ Thảo trong nhiều công việc học tập, từ tìm kiếm ý tưởng, giải quyết bài tập đến những lúc bí ý tưởng và chưa biết bắt đầu từ đâu. Từ trải nghiệm đó, Thảo nảy ra ý tưởng đưa hình ảnh những ứng dụng AI quen thuộc vào lễ tốt nghiệp.
"Mình muốn biến một điều rất quen thuộc trong đời sống sinh viên hiện nay thành một màn xuất hiện thật vui nhộn và khác biệt", Thảo chia sẻ.
Với nữ cử nhân, lễ tốt nghiệp không chỉ là dịp nhận tấm bằng sau nhiều năm học tập mà còn là cơ hội để nhìn lại hành trình đại học theo cách riêng
Để hiện thực hóa ý tưởng, nhóm sử dụng hộp mica, thiết kế và in hình giao diện của ChatGPT, Claude rồi dán lên bề mặt hộp. Hai người bạn chỉ cần đội hộp lên đầu, kết hợp với áo cử nhân và mũ tốt nghiệp là hoàn thành tạo hình hai ứng dụng AI phiên bản đời thực.
Khi bước lên sân khấu, Thảo cảm thấy vui và hào hứng trước sự bất ngờ của thầy cô, bạn bè, khán giả và gia đình. Nhiều người thích thú chụp ảnh, quay video để lưu lại khoảnh khắc này.
"Đây là một cột mốc chỉ có một lần trong đời sinh viên, nên mình muốn tận dụng cơ hội này để tạo ra một màn xuất hiện thật vui, có chút bất ngờ và mang đậm dấu ấn cá nhân", Thảo nói.
Là bạn hóa thân thành ứng dụng ChatGPT, Trần Tiến Đạt, sinh viên khóa K19 ngành quản trị truyền thông đa phương tiện, Trường ĐH FPT TP.HCM, cho biết cả nhóm đã dành rất nhiều thời gian, công sức và tâm huyết để chuẩn bị, từ khâu lên ý tưởng đến khi cùng nhau hiện thực hóa từng sản phẩm.
"Thú thật, từ khi nghe ý tưởng cho đến lúc bắt tay vào chuẩn bị và chính thức bước lên sân khấu, mình luôn cảm thấy rất hào hứng và mong chờ. Bởi đây không đơn thuần là một màn xuất hiện vui nhộn, mà còn là cách để chúng mình đưa một hình ảnh rất quen thuộc trong đời sống học tập của sinh viên thời đại AI vào một sự kiện trang trọng", Đạt bộc bạch.
Phương Thảo lên sân khấu cùng hai người bạn ChatGPT và Claude
Đạt cũng cho biết không chỉ có màn xuất hiện thú vị đó, bạn còn cùng chuẩn bị chiếc nón "Học cao hiểu sâu" và một tấm bằng tốt nghiệp phóng lớn, khoét ba khung ảnh để sinh viên đứng giữa hai thầy cô hướng dẫn hoặc giảng viên. Theo Đạt, ý tưởng này mang thông điệp tri ân, đồng thời tạo một cách thể hiện dí dỏm về hành trình học tập và những người đã đồng hành với sinh viên.
Đạt cho biết nhóm không đặt kỳ vọng cụ thể về số lượt xem, nhưng khá tự tin rằng những nội dung gần gũi với đời sống sinh viên, được đầu tư về ý tưởng và cách thể hiện sẽ nhận được sự quan tâm. Theo chia sẻ của Đạt, 3 màn xuất hiện độc đáo đã đạt tổng cộng hơn 6 triệu lượt xem trên các nền tảng.
Đạt chia sẻ: "Giá trị lớn nhất không chỉ nằm ở những con số lượt xem mà còn là việc chúng mình đã cùng nhau tạo nên những khoảnh khắc đáng nhớ cho một mùa tốt nghiệp".
Để những ý tưởng trên sân khấu trở thành hiện thực, phía sau còn có quá trình lên kế hoạch, sáng tạo và điều phối của Đỗ Hữu Phát, 27 tuổi, Trưởng phòng Sáng tạo nội dung tại Ban Công tác học đường - khối giáo dục FPT. Phát cho biết nhóm phụ trách sáng tạo nội dung và quản lý sản xuất video cá nhân hóa khoảnh khắc nhận bằng của tân cử nhân. Công việc không chỉ dừng ở việc gợi mở ý tưởng mà còn hỗ trợ sinh viên hiện thực hóa các màn xuất hiện, đồng thời điều phối quá trình ghi hình và sản xuất video.
Theo Phát, khó khăn lớn nhất là bảo đảm thời gian và tính phù hợp với không khí buổi lễ
Theo Hữu Phát, khó khăn lớn nhất khi triển khai những ý tưởng này là kiểm soát thời gian và bảo đảm sự phù hợp với không khí lễ tốt nghiệp. Với hàng ngàn sinh viên tham gia, mỗi lượt bước lên sân khấu chỉ kéo dài khoảng 15 - 30 giây. Vì vậy, đạo cụ cồng kềnh hoặc thao tác chuẩn bị kéo dài có thể ảnh hưởng đến tiến độ chung của buổi lễ.
"Nhóm phải kiểm tra trước kích thước, chất liệu đạo cụ, bảo đảm không che khuất tầm nhìn của đại biểu và không có yếu tố phản cảm. Ban đầu nhóm dự định chuẩn bị ba mô hình AI gồm Gemini, ChatGPT và Claude. Tuy nhiên, sau khi đánh giá kích thước và tính thẩm mỹ, nhóm quyết định chỉ sử dụng hai mô hình ChatGPT, Claude trong ngày diễn ra sự kiện", Hữu Phát cho biết thêm.
Bên cạnh đó, những ý tưởng có sự tương tác với giảng viên cũng cần được trao đổi và nhận được sự đồng thuận trước khi thực hiện. Với tấm bằng tốt nghiệp có ba khung ảnh, sự phối hợp của các thầy cô trao bằng là yếu tố giúp màn xuất hiện diễn ra thuận lợi.
Với nhiều sinh viên, khoảnh khắc bước lên sân khấu nhận bằng không chỉ đánh dấu chặng đường học tập khép lại, mà còn là dịp để lưu giữ những năm tháng thanh xuân theo cách riêng.
Không chỉ tạo tiếng cười, một số màn xuất hiện còn gửi gắm tình cảm và lòng biết ơn của sinh viên dành cho thầy cô, bạn bè. Khi được chuẩn bị phù hợp với khuôn khổ buổi lễ, những ý tưởng ấy góp phần làm cho ngày tốt nghiệp trở nên gần gũi, đáng nhớ hơn.

Bị chó nhà bất ngờ tấn công, người đàn ông chấn thương nghiêm trọng
(Dân trí) - Đang ngồi làm việc, người đàn ông ở Hà Nội đứng dậy khiến chiếc ghế đổ sát chỗ con chó đang nằm. Bị giật mình, con chó lao vào tấn công, cắn liên tiếp vùng cánh tay và cẳng tay phải của ông.
Ngày 11/11, Bệnh viện Trung ương Quân đội 108 cho biết vừa tiếp nhận và điều trị một trường hợp người đàn ông 59 tuổi ở Hà Nội bị chó nhà tấn công, gây tổn thương phức tạp ở cánh tay và cẳng tay.
Nam bệnh nhân N.V.A. (59 tuổi, phường Bạch Mai, Hà Nội) cho biết, ông đang ngồi làm việc tại nhà. Khi đứng dậy, chiếc ghế vô tình đổ xuống sát chỗ con chó đang nằm. Bị giật mình, con chó bất ngờ lao vào tấn công, cắn liên tiếp vùng cánh tay và cẳng tay ông.
Sau khi được trấn an, con chó nhả tay ông A. Ngay sau đó, người nhà đưa ông đến Bệnh viện Trung ương Quân đội 108 cấp cứu.
ThS.BS Nguyễn Bá Minh, Khoa Chấn thương Chi trên và Vi phẫu thuật, Bệnh viện Trung ương Quân đội 108, cho biết bệnh nhân có nhiều vết thương nham nhở ở mặt trước và mặt sau, kéo dài từ 1/3 dưới cánh tay đến hết cẳng tay phải.
Khi bệnh nhân nhập viện, các bác sĩ không bắt được mạch động mạch quay và động mạch trụ, đe dọa trực tiếp khả năng bảo tồn cánh tay.
Cánh tay phải người đàn ông tổn thương nghiêm trọng do bị chó nhà cắn (Ảnh: Lan Hương).
Ngay lập tức, bệnh nhân được kiểm soát chảy máu, xử trí ban đầu các vết thương và thực hiện những xét nghiệm cần thiết.
Ê-kíp trực nhanh chóng tiến hành phẫu thuật cấp cứu. Các bác sĩ cắt lọc tổ chức dập nát, làm sạch vết thương, ghép động mạch cánh tay và động mạch trụ qua đoạn ghép tĩnh mạch hiển bằng kỹ thuật vi phẫu.
Sau phẫu thuật, bệnh nhân được chăm sóc vết thương, sử dụng kháng sinh, thuốc giảm đau, theo dõi biến chứng và phục hồi chức năng. Song song với điều trị ngoại khoa, bệnh nhân được tiêm huyết thanh kháng dại, vaccine phòng dại và tiêm phòng uốn ván.
Hiệnsức khỏebệnh nhân ổn định, đang hồi phục.
BS Minh cho biết, vết thương do chó, mèo cắn không chỉ gây tổn thương tại chỗ mà còn tiềm ẩn nguy cơ nhiễm trùng. Đặc biệt, người bị chó, mèo cắn có thể đối mặt với nguy cơ mắc bệnh dại nếu con vật mang virus.
Sau khi bị chó, mèo cắn, người dân cần lập tức rửa kỹ vết thương dưới vòi nước chảy với xà phòng trong khoảng 15 phút, sau đó sát khuẩn bằng dung dịch phù hợp và nhanh chóng đến cơ sở y tế để được đánh giá, xử trí.
"Khi bị chó, mèo cắn, tuyệt đối không nên tự đắp lá, dùng thuốc dân gian, tự khâu kín vết thương hoặc trì hoãn tiêm phòng dại để chờ theo dõi con vật.
Nếu có thể, cần theo dõi chó, mèo trong 10 ngày theo hướng dẫn của cơ quan thú y. Tuy nhiên, việc theo dõi này không thay thế cho đánh giá và chỉ định dự phòng sau phơi nhiễm tại cơ sở y tế", BS Minh khuyến cáo.
Sau khi xuất hiện tình trạng nhiều người dân bị chó cắn, phường Phước Thắng, Tân Hải và xã Long Sơn (TPHCM) nhanh chóng vào cuộc xác minh, xử lý; đồng thời tuyên truyền người dân phòng ngừa bệnh dại.
Bệnh nhân chấn thương nghiêm trọng vì bị chó cắn
Nữ bệnh nhân 75 tuổi được đưa đến Bệnh viện Việt Đức cấp cứu, trong tình trạng có nhiều vết thương phức tạp sau khi bị chó cắn.
Hơn 2 tháng sau khi bị chó cắn, bé gái 9 tuổi tử vong vì bệnh dại
Bé gái 9 tuổi ở Gia Lai nhập viện với các triệu chứng bệnh dại. Gia đình cho biết hơn 2 tháng trước, cháu bị chó cắn ở gót chân, cào vào mặt nhưng không được đưa đi tiêm vắc xin phòng dại.
Chạy xe máy tông phải chó thả rông, người đàn ông chấn thương nghiêm trọng
Trong lúc di chuyển trên đường, người đàn ông 31 tuổi tông phải một con chó thả rông, gây ra chấn thương nghiêm trọng vùng mặt.
