Hơn 6 triệu lượt xem màn tốt nghiệp độc lạ, ChatGPT và Claude bất ngờ xuất hiện

Hưng Lợi12/11/2026 09:25 GMT+7Chia sẻChọn BáoThanh Niênlàmnguồn ưu tiêntrên Google tìm kiếm.Xem hướng dẫn.BƯỚC1Nhấp vào nút"ThêmThanh Niêntrên Google"hoặc mở trực tiếp đường dẫn này:https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thanhnien.vnBƯỚC2Tại trang vừa mở, tìm dòng"BáoThanh Niên"và bấm vào ô vuông bên phải.Khi ô vuông chuyển thành dấu tích xanh là bạn đã thành công rồi!LƯU Ý NHỎ:Nếu muốn kiểm tra xem cài đặt còn hiệu lực không, bạn chỉ cầnmở lại link trênlà thấy ngaydấu tích xanhvẫn đang hiển thị.Chúc bạn đọc báo vui vẻ!Thay vì xuất hiện một mình trong lễ phục cử nhân, Trần Thị Phương Thảo (tân cử nhân ngành digital marketing, Trường ĐH FPT TP.HCM đã rủ hai người bạn hóa thân thành ChatGPT và Claude để cùng mình bước lên sân khấu nhận bằng.
Chia sẻ về ý tưởng này, Phương Thảo cho biết ChatGPT là một trong những người bạn đồng hành đặc biệt trong suốt những năm đại học.
Bên cạnh thầy cô và bạn bè, các công cụ AI đã hỗ trợ Thảo trong nhiều công việc học tập, từ tìm kiếm ý tưởng, giải quyết bài tập đến những lúc bí ý tưởng và chưa biết bắt đầu từ đâu.
Từ trải nghiệm đó, Thảo nảy ra ý tưởng đưa hình ảnh những ứng dụng AI quen thuộc vào lễ tốt nghiệp.
"Mình muốn biến một điều rất quen thuộc trong đời sống sinh viên hiện nay thành một màn xuất hiện thật vui nhộn và khác biệt", Thảo chia sẻ.
Với nữ cử nhân, lễ tốt nghiệp không chỉ là dịp nhận tấm bằng sau nhiều năm học tập mà còn là cơ hội để nhìn lại hành trình đại học theo cách riêng
Để hiện thực hóa ý tưởng, nhóm sử dụng hộp mica, thiết kế và in hình giao diện của ChatGPT, Claude rồi dán lên bề mặt hộp.
Hai người bạn chỉ cần đội hộp lên đầu, kết hợp với áo cử nhân và mũ tốt nghiệp là hoàn thành tạo hình hai ứng dụng AI phiên bản đời thực.
Khi bước lên sân khấu, Thảo cảm thấy vui và hào hứng trước sự bất ngờ của thầy cô, bạn bè, khán giả và gia đình.
Nhiều người thích thú chụp ảnh, quay video để lưu lại khoảnh khắc này.
"Đây là một cột mốc chỉ có một lần trong đời sinh viên, nên mình muốn tận dụng cơ hội này để tạo ra một màn xuất hiện thật vui, có chút bất ngờ và mang đậm dấu ấn cá nhân", Thảo nói.

Là bạn hóa thân thành ứng dụng ChatGPT, Trần Tiến Đạt, sinh viên khóa K19 ngành quản trị truyền thông đa phương tiện, Trường ĐH FPT TP.HCM, cho biết cả nhóm đã dành rất nhiều thời gian, công sức và tâm huyết để chuẩn bị, từ khâu lên ý tưởng đến khi cùng nhau hiện thực hóa từng sản phẩm.
"Thú thật, từ khi nghe ý tưởng cho đến lúc bắt tay vào chuẩn bị và chính thức bước lên sân khấu, mình luôn cảm thấy rất hào hứng và mong chờ.

Bởi đây không đơn thuần là một màn xuất hiện vui nhộn, mà còn là cách để chúng mình đưa một hình ảnh rất quen thuộc trong đời sống học tập của sinh viên thời đại AI vào một sự kiện trang trọng", Đạt bộc bạch.
Phương Thảo lên sân khấu cùng hai người bạn ChatGPT và Claude

Đạt cũng cho biết không chỉ có màn xuất hiện thú vị đó, bạn còn cùng chuẩn bị chiếc nón "Học cao hiểu sâu" và một tấm bằng tốt nghiệp phóng lớn, khoét ba khung ảnh để sinh viên đứng giữa hai thầy cô hướng dẫn hoặc giảng viên.
Theo Đạt, ý tưởng này mang thông điệp tri ân, đồng thời tạo một cách thể hiện dí dỏm về hành trình học tập và những người đã đồng hành với sinh viên.
Đạt cho biết nhóm không đặt kỳ vọng cụ thể về số lượt xem, nhưng khá tự tin rằng những nội dung gần gũi với đời sống sinh viên, được đầu tư về ý tưởng và cách thể hiện sẽ nhận được sự quan tâm.
Theo chia sẻ của Đạt, 3 màn xuất hiện độc đáo đã đạt tổng cộng hơn 6 triệu lượt xem trên các nền tảng.
Đạt chia sẻ: "Giá trị lớn nhất không chỉ nằm ở những con số lượt xem mà còn là việc chúng mình đã cùng nhau tạo nên những khoảnh khắc đáng nhớ cho một mùa tốt nghiệp".

Để những ý tưởng trên sân khấu trở thành hiện thực, phía sau còn có quá trình lên kế hoạch, sáng tạo và điều phối của Đỗ Hữu Phát, 27 tuổi, Trưởng phòng Sáng tạo nội dung tại Ban Công tác học đường - khối giáo dục FPT.
Phát cho biết nhóm phụ trách sáng tạo nội dung và quản lý sản xuất video cá nhân hóa khoảnh khắc nhận bằng của tân cử nhân.
Công việc không chỉ dừng ở việc gợi mở ý tưởng mà còn hỗ trợ sinh viên hiện thực hóa các màn xuất hiện, đồng thời điều phối quá trình ghi hình và sản xuất video.
Theo Phát, khó khăn lớn nhất là bảo đảm thời gian và tính phù hợp với không khí buổi lễ
Theo Hữu Phát, khó khăn lớn nhất khi triển khai những ý tưởng này là kiểm soát thời gian và bảo đảm sự phù hợp với không khí lễ tốt nghiệp.
Với hàng ngàn sinh viên tham gia, mỗi lượt bước lên sân khấu chỉ kéo dài khoảng 15 - 30 giây.
Vì vậy, đạo cụ cồng kềnh hoặc thao tác chuẩn bị kéo dài có thể ảnh hưởng đến tiến độ chung của buổi lễ.
"Nhóm phải kiểm tra trước kích thước, chất liệu đạo cụ, bảo đảm không che khuất tầm nhìn của đại biểu và không có yếu tố phản cảm.
Ban đầu nhóm dự định chuẩn bị ba mô hình AI gồm Gemini, ChatGPT và Claude.
Tuy nhiên, sau khi đánh giá kích thước và tính thẩm mỹ, nhóm quyết định chỉ sử dụng hai mô hình ChatGPT, Claude trong ngày diễn ra sự kiện", Hữu Phát cho biết thêm.
Bên cạnh đó, những ý tưởng có sự tương tác với giảng viên cũng cần được trao đổi và nhận được sự đồng thuận trước khi thực hiện.
Với tấm bằng tốt nghiệp có ba khung ảnh, sự phối hợp của các thầy cô trao bằng là yếu tố giúp màn xuất hiện diễn ra thuận lợi.
Với nhiều sinh viên, khoảnh khắc bước lên sân khấu nhận bằng không chỉ đánh dấu chặng đường học tập khép lại, mà còn là dịp để lưu giữ những năm tháng thanh xuân theo cách riêng.
Không chỉ tạo tiếng cười, một số màn xuất hiện còn gửi gắm tình cảm và lòng biết ơn của sinh viên dành cho thầy cô, bạn bè.
Khi được chuẩn bị phù hợp với khuôn khổ buổi lễ, những ý tưởng ấy góp phần làm cho ngày tốt nghiệp trở nên gần gũi, đáng nhớ hơn.

Chủ tịch Hội đồng Liên bang Nga đến Hà Nội, bắt đầu thăm chính thức Việt Nam
Chủ tịch Hội đồng Liên bang, Quốc hội Liên bang Nga Valentina Matviyenko thăm chính thức Việt Nam từ ngày 11 đến 13/11, thúc đẩy hợp tác nghị viện và quan hệ Đối tác chiến lược toàn diện Việt Nam - Nga.
Chủ tịch Hội đồng Liên bang, Quốc hội Liên bang Nga Valentina I.Matviyenko đến Hà Nội, bắt đầu thăm chính thức Việt Nam (Ảnh: Tuấn Anh/TTXVN).
Tối 11/11, Chủ tịch Hội đồng Liên bang, Quốc hội Liên bang Nga Valentina Matviyenko đến Hà Nội, bắt đầu thăm chính thức Việt Nam, từ ngày 11 đến 13/11, theo lời mời của Chủ tịch Quốc hội Trần Thanh Mẫn.
Ra sân bay quốc tế Nội Bài đón đoàn có: Phó Chủ tịch Quốc hội, Chủ tịch Nhóm Nghị sỹ hữu nghị Việt Nam - Liên bang Nga Nguyễn Khắc Định; Phó Chủ nhiệm thường trực Ủy ban Quốc phòng, Đối ngoại, An ninh của Quốc hội Vũ Hải Hà.
Đây là chuyến thăm chính thức Việt Nam lần thứ ba của Chủ tịch Hội đồng Liên bang, Quốc hội Liên bang Nga Valentina Matviyenko sau các chuyến thăm năm 2012 và 2017.
Trong tổng thể mối quan hệ tốt đẹp giữa hai nước Việt Nam - Liên bang Nga, quan hệ hợp tác trên kênh nghị viện luôn được củng cố và phát triển tốt đẹp trong thời gian qua. Hai bên duy trì thường xuyên hoạt động trao đổi đoàn, tiếp xúc cấp cao và các cấp, góp phần tăng cường tin cậy chính trị và thúc đẩy triển khai các thỏa thuận hợp tác giữa Quốc hội hai nước.
Phó Chủ tịch Quốc hội Nguyễn Khắc Định đón Chủ tịch Hội đồng Liên bang, Quốc hội Liên bang Nga Valentina I.Matviyenko tại sân bay quốc tế Nội Bài (Ảnh: Tuấn Anh/TTXVN).
Trong khuôn khổ hợp tác đa phương, hai bên duy trì tiếp xúc, tích cực và thường xuyên phối hợp, tham vấn, trao đổi ý kiến và ủng hộ lẫn nhau tại các diễn đàn nghị viện đa phương như: Hội đồng Liên nghị viện Hiệp hội các quốc gia Đông Nam Á (AIPA), Liên minh Nghị viện thế giới (IPU), Hội nghị Chủ tịch Quốc hội các nước Á-Âu (MSEAP), Hội nghị các Chủ tịch Quốc hội thế giới...
Các cuộc tiếp xúc cấp cao thường xuyên tại các diễn đàn nghị viện đa phương góp phần duy trì tin cậy chính trị, phối hợp lập trường giữa cơ quan lập pháp hai nước.
Trong hợp tác với Hội đồng Liên bang (Thượng viện), hai bên đã ký thỏa thuận hợp tác nhân chuyến thăm Liên bang Nga của Chủ tịch Quốc hội Trần Thanh Mẫn (tháng 9/2024).
Ủy ban Thường vụ Quốc hội đã ban hành kế hoạch triển khai thỏa thuận, xác định các hoạt động cụ thể nhằm tăng cường trao đổi kinh nghiệm lập pháp, giám sát và thúc đẩy hợp tác trên các lĩnh vực cùng quan tâm.
Hai bên đang trao đổi để thống nhất dự thảo Chương trình hành động chung giai đoạn 2026-2028.
Về hợp tác với Duma Quốc gia (Hạ viện), hai bên đã ký thỏa thuận hợp tác từ năm 2009 và ký lại vào năm 2013.
Nhân chuyến thăm Việt Nam của Chủ tịch Hạ viện Vyacheslav Volodin (năm 2018), hai bên cũng đã ký thỏa thuận về việc thành lập Ủy ban hợp tác liên Nghị viện. Đây là mô hình hợp tác liên nghị viện song phương cấp cao đầu tiên giữa Quốc hội Việt Nam với một cơ quan lập pháp nước ngoài. Được tổ chức luân phiên tại mỗi nước, đến nay, Ủy ban hợp tác liên Nghị viện đã tổ chức thành công 4 phiên họp...
Trong bối cảnh quan hệ tốt đẹp giữa hai nước, chuyến thăm chính thức Việt Nam của Chủ tịch Hội đồng Liên bang, Quốc hội Liên bang Nga Valentina Matviyenko nhằm triển khai hiệu quả nội dung hợp tác theo Tuyên bố chung về việc củng cố hơn nữa quan hệ Đối tác chiến lược toàn diện Việt Nam - Nga trong giai đoạn mới, được thông qua trong chuyến thăm cấp nhà nước tới Nga hồi tháng Chín của Tổng Bí thư, Chủ tịch nước Tô Lâm, qua đó tạo bước chuyển, nâng cao vai trò hợp tác nghị viện song phương, đồng thời thúc đẩy hợp tác trong các lĩnh vực Nga có thế mạnh và Việt Nam có nhu cầu như khoa học - công nghệ, đổi mới sáng tạo, văn hóa, giáo dục, du lịch, giao lưu nhân dân.

Việt Nam và Liên bang Nga đã ra Tuyên bố chung về việc củng cố hơn nữa quan hệ Đối tác Chiến lược Toàn diện Việt Nam - Nga trong giai đoạn mới.

World Cup U.17 có Việt Nam tham dự biến động lớn: U.17 Mỹ chính thức rút lui, lý do rất bất ngờ
Giang Lao- tonylaoho@gmail.com12/11/2026 07:34 GMT+7Chia sẻChọn BáoThanh Niênlàmnguồn ưu tiêntrên Google tìm kiếm.Xem hướng dẫn.BƯỚC1Nhấp vào nút"ThêmThanh Niêntrên Google"hoặc mở trực tiếp đường dẫn này:https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thanhnien.vnBƯỚC2Tại trang vừa mở, tìm dòng"BáoThanh Niên"và bấm vào ô vuông bên phải.Khi ô vuông chuyển thành dấu tích xanh là bạn đã thành công rồi!LƯU Ý NHỎ:Nếu muốn kiểm tra xem cài đặt còn hiệu lực không, bạn chỉ cầnmở lại link trênlà thấy ngaydấu tích xanhvẫn đang hiển thị.Chúc bạn đọc báo vui vẻ!Ngày 12.11, Liên đoàn Bóng đá Mỹ (USSF) chính thức thông báo đội tuyển nước này không tham dự World Cup U.17 tại Qatar vì các lý do an ninh. Tại giải này, U.17 Việt Nam nằm ở bảng G đã có mặt chuẩn bị thi đấu.
FIFA chưa lên tiếng về quyết định của USSF
Thông báo của USSF ngày 12.11 giải thích về quyết định rút đội tuyển U.17 Mỹ khỏiWorld Cup U.17tại Qatar: "Thật không may, do hoàn cảnh hiện tại bao gồm Khuyến cáo du lịch cấp 3 dành cho Qatar của Bộ Ngoại giao Mỹ và các chỉ thị liên quan dành cho nhân viên đại sứ quán và gia đình, chúng tôi không thể tham gia giải đấu được nữa.
Sức khỏe của các cầu thủ và nhân viên sẽ luôn là ưu tiên hàng đầu của chúng tôi. Chúng tôi xin bày tỏ lòng biết ơn sâu sắc vì sự cống hiến của các bạn (cầu thủ đội tuyển U.17 Mỹ) dành cho bóng đá Mỹ, đồng thời chia sẻ nỗi thất vọng về hoàn cảnh không mong muốn này".
U.17 Mỹ rút lui, trong khi đội tuyển U.17 Việt Nam đã đến Qatar an toàn, ổn định nơi lưu trú và sẵn sàng tập luyện để chuẩn bị thi đấu World Cup U.17
Tại World Cup U.17 sắp diễn ra tại Qatar từ ngày 19.11 đến 13.12, với 48 đội tuyển tham dự. Trong đó, U.17 Mỹ nằm ở bảng J cùng với Montenegro, Chile và Algeria. Việc U.17 Mỹ rút lui, hiện chưa rõ FIFA sẽ bổ sung đội thay thế, hoặc giữ nguyên bảng đấu này với 3 đội.
Trường hợp giữ nguyên 3 đội tại bảng J, chắc chắn FIFA sẽ phải điều chỉnh điều lệ, trong đó có liên quan đến các đội hạng ba có thành tích tốt nhất đi tiếp vào vòng sau.
World Cup U.17 với 48 đội, chia thành 12 bảng, mỗi bảng 4 đội. Sau vòng bảng, 2 đội nhất nhì mỗi bảng và 8 đội hạng ba có thành tích tốt nhất vào vòng 32 đội.
FIFA chọn Nguyễn Lực là cầu thủ đáng xem nhất của U.17 Việt Nam tại World Cup 2026
U.17 Việt Nam đã đến Qatar an toàn, sẵn sàng thi đấu
Theo Liên đoàn Bóng đá Việt Nam (VFF), đội tuyểnU.17 Việt Namsau khi hoàn tất giai đoạn tập huấn tại UAE, đội đã di chuyển đến Qatar - địa điểm tổ chức vòng chung kết World Cup U.17. Toàn đội đã ổn định nơi lưu trú, sẵn sàng bước vào giai đoạn tập luyện tiếp theo nhằm hoàn thiện những khâu chuẩn bị cuối cùng, hướng tới trận ra quân gặp đội tuyển U.17 Bỉ vào ngày 20.11. "Hơi thở World Cup đã cận kề!", VFF nhấn mạnh.
Tại World Cup U.17 ở Qatar, đội tuyển U.17 Việt Nam nằm ở bảng G, đội thi đấu trận ra quân gặp U.17 Bỉ lúc 20 giờ ngày 20.11. Trận tiếp theo gặp U.17 New Zealand lúc 22 giờ 30 ngày 23.11. Và trận cuối vòng bảng gặp U.17 Mali lúc 20 giờ ngày 26.11. Tất cả đều giờ Việt Nam. Các trận của U.17 Việt Nam diễn ra trên sân Aspire Zone tại Al Rayyan.
Các đội tuyển khu vực Đông Nam Á bước vào FIFA Days tháng 11 ra sao?
Theo thống kê, có 5/11 đội tuyển ở khu vực Đông Nam Á tham gia thi đấu FIFA Days tháng 11 trước các đối thủ cực kỳ đa dạng đến từ nhiều nơi trên thế giới. Đội tuyển Việt Nam rèn quân với 2 đối thủ vừa tầm.

Chủ tịch Hội đồng Liên bang Nga đến Hà Nội, bắt đầu thăm chính thức Việt Nam

Chủ tịch Hội đồng Liên bang, Quốc hội Liên bang Nga Valentina Matviyenko thăm chính thức Việt Nam từ ngày 11 đến 13/11, thúc đẩy hợp tác nghị viện và quan hệ Đối tác chiến lược toàn diện Việt Nam - Nga.
Chủ tịch Hội đồng Liên bang, Quốc hội Liên bang Nga Valentina I.Matviyenko đến Hà Nội, bắt đầu thăm chính thức Việt Nam (Ảnh: Tuấn Anh/TTXVN).

Tối 11/11, Chủ tịch Hội đồng Liên bang, Quốc hội Liên bang Nga Valentina Matviyenko đến Hà Nội, bắt đầu thăm chính thức Việt Nam, từ ngày 11 đến 13/11, theo lời mời của Chủ tịch Quốc hội Trần Thanh Mẫn.

Ra sân bay quốc tế Nội Bài đón đoàn có: Phó Chủ tịch Quốc hội, Chủ tịch Nhóm Nghị sỹ hữu nghị Việt Nam - Liên bang Nga Nguyễn Khắc Định; Phó Chủ nhiệm thường trực Ủy ban Quốc phòng, Đối ngoại, An ninh của Quốc hội Vũ Hải Hà.

England: Harry Kane targets European Championships, World Cup and Champions League to add biggest team prizes to Ballon d'Or
England captain Harry Kane set to win record-breaking 126th England cap in Nations League this week; Kane is now targeting more team silverware after his Ballon d'Or win; follow England vs Croatia with the Sky Sports website and app on Thursday; kick-off 7.45pm
Wednesday 11 November 2026 15:29, UK
Image:Harry Kane scored twice on his 125th England appearance last month, with his record-breaking 126th cap set to come on Thursday
Harry Kane will become England's record appearance maker on Thursday night - but the Ballon d'Or winner now has his sights set on the biggest team trophies in football.
England captain Kane will win his 126th cap for his country against Croatia in the Nations League at Wembley. The landmark moment comes just weeks after he was crowned the best player in the world.
But while the striker has ended his long wait for team glory with back-to-back Bundesliga titles at Bayern Munich, as well as a German Cup, he is now eager to kick on again and land the most prestigious prizes for club and country.
"To win a team trophy with England, a major trophy, is my biggest dream," he said in a press conference on Wednesday when asked what comes next for him. "That's always been my biggest dream, to win a European Championship or a World Cup, or both, hopefully, but I know how difficult that is. Extremely motivated to do that.

"Individual accolades are incredible and things I'm proud of but ultimately they're a consequence of trying to make the team better and trying to win something with the team.
"With Bayern Munich, it's trying to win the Champions League. There are many trophies I haven't won and that's what motivates me.

In recent years, Kane has been able to shake off his reputation as a top player who didn't succeed on the big stage. He hopes that in the second half of his career he will be able to completely change the narrative about his time in the game, having gone 10 full seasons in the first team at Tottenham without lifting silverware.
However, he also recognises the difficult defeats helped propel him into becoming the player he is today.
"It was tough in those moments when you feel you're performing well and putting up great numbers but not winning the team trophies which is ultimately what you're playing for," he said.

"My situation was quite unique in that sense, I don't know if there has been another player like that who hasn't won for so long.
"If anything, it made me even more hungry. Year after year, going into the season without having won one made me motivated to do that and pushed me to another level that I might not have reached if I'd won early in my career.
"Once I won the first trophy at Bayern, it was a weight off the shoulders in terms of a talking point in interviews and press conferences. It helped me relax and feel more free without thinking too much and having that extra pressure.
"I'm in a sweet spot of my career where I've won many trophies in the last couple of years and hopefully loads more to go. Hopefully by the end of my career, I'll have 20+ trophies and those first 10 years might not be spoken about as much.
"What I achieved in those 10 years years and here at Tottenham, getting to the Champions League final, it doesn't mean nothing - it was a incredible step the club took."
Tuchel: 'Unique' Kane will build on his records
Thomas Tuchel says he will field a strong side against Croatia in a 'beautiful' night for Harry Kane as he presents the Ballon d'Or to the England fans.
Paying tribute to his captain, England boss Thomas Tuchel says he anticipates a "beautiful occasion" at Wembley on Thursday - but says Kane also has a job to do.
"It's always nice if things are proven in sports - he has his prizes and records, he will build on these records, score more goals and get more games," said Tuchel.
"He will start for us and as captain. It's a big occasion to present the Ballon d'Or trophy to our fans and have it embedded in the same day he gets his all-time record for 126 matches, it's a beautiful occasion.
"It's a match that matters a lot to us, it's not a friendly. It's on Harry to digest it as quickly as possible. There will be a lot of praise and emotions before kick-off then we need him in the best shape to win the match for us."
Tuchel praised Kane's "unique" skillset as what has set him apart from other players in the past year.

"But he was more of a dribbler and accelerator from these spaces, Harry is more a passer and an accelerator through his passing range. Everyone is different. Harry is quite unique in the way he does it.

‘I’ve had to prove people wrong’: Kane still striving before record England cap
Captain to surpass Shilton with 126th cap against Croatia
Kane aims to increase record for younger players to catch
Harry Kane says he still feels a pressure to prove his worth, even as he prepares to become England’s most capped men’s player, as he outlined his determination to set records that will stand for years.
The captain will make his 126th appearance against Croatia at ­Wembley on Thursday night, moving him ahead of Peter Shilton on the all-time list. Kane is England’s record ­goalscorer with 91, comfortably clear of Wayne Rooney, who retired with 53.
Bone broth, sweets ban and acupuncture: Harry Kane’s road to record England capRead more
Kane will be presented with a memento of his historic cap by ­Shilton before kick-off against ­Croatia. ­Shilton has held the record since 1990 when he finished his 20-year career. Kane’s achievement ofwinning the Ballon d’Orlast month will also be recognised.
“I don’t think it will ever leave me,” Kane said, when asked whether he continued to have points to prove. “It’s probably part of what makes me push myself to the limits that I do because in football, you’ve never completed it. No matter what you’ve achieved, there is always a trophy that someone else has won or a goal record that someone else has.
“Whether it’s noise from the outside, from media or the fans … it just helps motivate me to realise there’s a lot more to achieve. My biggest fear is finishing my career and thinking I could have done a bit more … if I could have just done that or done that. I want to make sure I cross every bridge and do everything possible so that whenever that day does come, I can say I’ve done everything possible. And I can sleep well at night.”
The 33-year-old is conscious that two of his England teammates have won a significant number of caps. Declan Rice has 80 at the age of 27; Jude Bellingham 60 at 23. “I’ll try to give them a good number to catch,” Kane said. “The goal record, of course, is going to be one that’s difficult to beat for a while.
“I’ve spoken about leading by example and pushing a lot of these younger players. It’s by setting standards, being available every time, getting the caps and scoring the goals. That should help motivate the younger players. If I was younger and I had a player in front of me doing what I was doing, I know that would push me to think: ‘OK, I can score those goals, I can win the Ballon d’Or, I can break the cap record.’ Whilst I’m in this place, it is to try to set these records as high as I can and one day look back to see if anyone can catch them.”
View image in fullscreenHarry Kane receives the Ballon d'Or in London.Photograph: Franck Fife/AFP/Getty Images
Kane has been doubted at ­numerous points of his career, ­starting when he was released by Arsenal as an eight-year-old. He had difficult loans from Tottenham to Norwich and Leicester in 2012‑13 and there were the one‑season‑wonder jibes after his breakthrough campaign for Spurs and England in 2014-15.
Kane has been ridiculed for ­setting lofty targets: such as in 2017, when he said hewanted to replicate the numbers of Lionel Messi and ­Cristiano Ronaldo; when he stated his ambition to win the 2018 World Cup Golden Boot. Or when he stood on the verge of his 100th England cap in September 2024 with 66 goals and said he wanted to score 100. There were questions about his place in the team after Euro 2024 when his performances were underwhelming and he was substituted in the final. Every time, he answered back.
“It’s just my mindset,” Kane said. “Because I’ve had to prove people wrong my whole career. From early academy days proving coaches wrong, proving scouts wrong – it has just been instilled in me. If someone tells me I can’t do something it motivates me more to do it.
“When you look at all the great athletes, I’ve spoken before about Tom Brady [the NFL icon] and it’s that unwavering mentality to be the best. Maybe with me, because I’m a calm person and you don’t see … like, the ego of some of these great players and I’m a bit more relaxed … but it doesn’t mean I don’t want it as much as everyone else. That I don’t put in the work and drive myself and everyone around me to be the best.
“Maybe getting released that early [by Arsenal] and ­proving them wrong and then maybe ­proving [wrong] my early coaches at ­Tottenham, who I wasn’t playing as much [under]. The loan moves that didn’t go well. Same thing: ‘I’m going to show them.’”
Kane brought up surely the lowest individual moment of his England career – the penalty miss against France in the 2-1 World Cup ­quarter‑final defeat in 2022. “That was really tough but again it was the way I bounced back,” he said.
“And even the fact I scored the next 30 [actually 31] penalties of my career. I changed the technique a little bit and it made me improve. There have been a lot of low points but maybe they are things that have helped me get to where I am now.”

Is Harry Kane England's GOAT? Ballon d'Or winner strengthens case as he becomes nation's most-capped player | Sporting NewsSkip to main content
Is Harry Kane England's GOAT? Ballon d'Or winner strengthens case as he becomes nation's most-capped player
Ending however many years of hurt it clocks in at, notwithstanding, the past couple of weeks will provide the cinematic introduction and conclusion when Harry Kane's career gets the full documentary treatment.
Kane made a particular point of thanking youth coaches and those who gave him a chance early in his career when he collected the Ballon d'Or at the London Palladium at the end of last month. Even in a room where there was plenty of hollering forArsenalfrom some overly enthusiastic local attendees, the former Tottenham hero was cheered to the rafters.
He was a popular, everyman winner in an era of tedious glitz and politicking around soccer's most coveted individual award. The Ballon d'Or is a quickly flagged and seldom realised ambition for the stars of tomorrow. Kane's flagging of his early mentors and patchy loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich andLeicester Cityin his youth highlighted how nothing was guaranteed or even expected.
Even his Tottenham breakthrough came with jibes about him being a potential "one-season wonder". When Kane scored within 79 seconds of coming on for his England debut against Lithuania in March 2015, for some it felt like a flash in a different pan. Wayne Rooney also scored that night to close in on Sir Bobby Charlton's all-time England scoring record, which he duly overhauled later that year.
MORE:Humble hero Kane the perfect heir to Matthews as Ballon d'Or comes 'home'
Kane, the fresh-faced striker who then-manger Roy Hodgson rolled the dice on that night, has now gone past both of them. Charlton and Rooney, two men rightly considered among England's greatest ever players, are specks in the distance for Kane. Rooney bowed out with 53 goals to Charlton's 49. Kane has 91 and will almost certainly double both men's tallies.
On Thursday, when the Three Lions captain leads England out at Wembley to face familiar foes Croatia in the UEFA Nations League, he will break his country's caps record. Number 126, taking his tally ahead of long-serving goalkeeper Peter Shilton.
Most appearances, most goals. It stands to reason that Kane has a very good case for being considered the best England player of all time.
Is Harry Kane England's greatest ever player?
There's a distinction to grapple with at the start of this conversation: whether Kane is the greatest English player or the greatest England player, because those are slightly different things.
Other stars of the 21st century such as Rooney, Frank Lampard, Steven Gerrard and Paul Scholes can certainly claim to have been better players than Kane and have more celebrated club careers. Rooney, Lampard and Gerrard were also cap centurions but do not come close to Kane in terms of achievements for England.
MORE:Who are the youngest Ballon d'Or winners of all-time?
A couple of generations earlier, there's Kevin Keegan. A two-time Ballon d'Or winner who excelled after joining Bundesliga heavyweights Hamburg fromLiverpoolin 1977, his career path has plenty in common with Kane. However, Keegan's peak years coincided with England failing to qualify for the 1974 and 1978 World Cups, and his 21 goals in 63 caps are a fairly modest return for a player of his vast capabilities.
It's worth dwelling on the success rate, or lack thereof, when assessing Englishmen abroad between Keegan and Kane. David Beckham was a qualified success atReal Madrid, Michael Owen less so over a shorter period. Gary Lineker did well enough atBarcelona; he has a Clasico hat-trick to his name, before being farmed out to the wing by Johan Cruyff.
Not many of England's best have tried their hand abroad, something that can be attributed partly to the financial power of the Premier League. But Kane turning up at Bayern and scoring at the rate of more or less a goal a game feels like it's been taken for granted a little too much.
Sure, Bayern are always favourites to win the modern Bundesliga and Kane had long come to be considered an inevitable goalscorer. But Englishmen simply do not join Europe's great clubs and perform as he has. Wales had John Charles at Juventus and Gareth Bale at Real Madrid generations apart, but Kane stands apart. England teammate Jude Bellingham might surpass him as his Real Madrid achievements stack up. Thomas Tuchel's two star men are trailblazers, and this conversation is likely to settle upon Bellingham in due course.
MORE:Final 2026 Ballon d'Or results with Harry Kane capturing trophy
Kane's time at Tottenham means there is not the weight of trophies that the likes of Rooney and Lampard can boast, but Kane is definitely among England's greatest before we focus purely upon his exploits for the Three Lions.
Along with his caps and goals record, Kane has captained England to two European Championship finals and two World Cup semifinals. He is joint-fifth on the World Cup's all-time top scorers list, alongside Bayern great Gerd Muller on 14. He will have designs on climbing higher up the rankings at the 2030 tournament, when he will be a few weeks shy of his 37th birthday.
The clock is ticking for Kane, and he has tended to fade at the business end of international tournaments. This is a minor gripe, given he's responsible for England reaching those stages as a matter of course for the first time in more than half a century. A major tournament success at Euro 2028 or the 2030 World Cup would give him an ironclad case. He'll be well past a century of goals by that point too.
For now,Manchester Unitedicon Charlton is probably a breath ahead. A powerhouse attacking midfielder, Charlton was talismanic for Sir Alf Ramsey's World Cup-winning side in 1966. His match-winning brace against Portugal in the semifinals is the sort of decisive major tournament performance Kane cannot yet lay claim to.
Charlton, a Ballon d'Or winner and two-time runner-up, was also named in four World Cup squads, playing at three tournaments, enjoying incredible longevity in a 106-cap career spanning 1958 to 1970.
The fact he made his England debut two months after being injured in the Munich air disaster, in which eight of his young United teammates were among 23 killed, also underlined a career where incredible human fortitude was at the foundation of everything.

England players are understood to have aired strong views about their World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in a team meeting.

BBC Sport has been told the squad feel that now they have been able to have their say, they can move on from their heartbreak in Atlanta on 15 July.
And this was demonstrated in the last international break when England, after a narrow defeat by Spain in the first game, went on to win the next three matches impressively.

Is Palmer's England career over under Tuchel?
'A beautiful story' as Bellingham brothers called up
The ramifications of the Argentina defeat, or perhaps more pertinently, the circumstances, meant some of the squad held grievances, with those feelings lingering and even growing throughout the summer.
In particular there was unhappiness about how Tuchel told them to approach the closing stages of the game after Anthony Gordon had given them a 55th-minute advantage.
Enzo Fernandez struck an equaliser with five minutes left, before Lautaro Martinez headed in a stoppage-time winner.
Asreported by BBC Sport at the time,a number of senior England players held misgivings at Tuchel's instructions for the closing stages of the Argentina loss, believing the approach was too negative and defensive.
Hindsight, of course, is 20/20. England appeared to retreat in the closing stages of the last-16 tie against Mexico earlier in the tournament - but successfully defended a 3-2 lead to reach the quarter-finals to trigger scenes of joy at the iconic Azteca Stadium.
Nevertheless, certain players felt let down by the team's apparent pragmatism during the closing stages of the loss to Argentina amid a sense that going for the South Americans' jugular would have provided greater success.
Inevitably, the game against Argentina emerged as a key theme at the squad discussion.
It is understood that Tuchel pointed to the quality of the opposition as a key factor on why they eventually succumbed to two late Argentina goals.
There is, of course, merit to that argument. Lionel Messi was in the opposition team after all.
That said, it was not an argument the players in the meeting were prepared to universally accept.
There is a strongly held view within the England squad that their team, man-for-man, was superior to Argentina, who had 38-year-old Nicolas Otamendi on the field for the closing 18 minutes of the game.
All players were afforded an opportunity to air their personal views during the meeting.
As you would expect, captain Harry Kane was strong and forthright with his views.
Jude Bellingham, too, is said to have been particularly candid in expressing his belief that this current crop of England players were more than capable of continuing to take the game to Argentina.
Bellingham's contribution to the meeting is said to have underlined his growing influence within the England squad, with many believing the Real Madrid midfielder will become the team's captain once Kane is no longer in the picture.
If the air needed to be cleared after the World Cup then it appears those honest discussions at the end of September did the trick.
Barring the 3-2 defeat by Spain at Wembley in their first Nations League fixture in September, England have bounced back from the loss to Argentina emphatically - scoring 12 goals without conceding in three fixtures against the Czech Republic and Croatia.
Similarly, the fluctuating relationship between Bellingham and Tuchel seems to have improved, too.
"It was a bit of an up and down [relationship] of course but we are in a good place," Tuchel said last week.
"I love to be his coach. He's a top player, a very influential player and I think it goes both ways."
We will get a clearer idea of how 'Tuchel 2.0' is progressing in the next few days when England host Croatia on Thursday and travel to Madrid to face world champions Spain on Sunday.

Cardinals make Carson Beck decision official for Week 10 after Gardner Minshew injury
TheArizona Cardinalshave dealt with a significant number of injuries to their offensive players this season, with wide receivers Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne out for the rest of the season. Jeremiyah Love is banged up as well.
Recently, during the Cardinals' Week 9 loss to theSeattle Seahawks, quarterback Gardner Minshew, taking over for Jacoby Brissett after his trade to theBaltimore Ravens, suffered an injury. Carson Beck was next in line at QB for Arizona.
AsESPN's Jeremy Fowlerreported Wednesday, the Cardinals have made an official decision, naming Beck the team's starting quarterback for Week 10 when the Cardinals face theLos Angeles Rams.
Cardinals name Carson Beck as Week 10 starting QB
"It's Carson Beck time in Arizona. Cardinals HC Mike LaFleur announces Beck will start for Arizona on Sunday vs. the Rams," Fowler reports. "Arizona going on its third starter in as many weeks."
The Cardinals are set to face the Rams in Week 10, and their team will look a lot different than it did when they won a couple of weeks ago.
Brissett is gone, Minshew isn't even the backup, and the wide receiver room has been decimated by injuries. But, most importantly, Beck is making his NFL starting debut.
During the Cardinals' 2026 preseason, Beck went 15 of 19 for 188 yards and one touchdown with no interceptions. It was a solid debut for Beck with the Cardinals, but now it's going to be a different challenge.
Facing the Rams, a team sitting at 5-4 and in desperation mode to keep their 2026 playoff hopes alive, Beck has a tall task in front of him if he wants to win in his NFL debut.
MORE:Myles Garrett shows Rams why they traded for him in return vs. Commanders
Not only is the matchup tough, but Beck is going to have to work with a depleted offense. Tyler Allgeier is good to go, and maybe Bam Knight is back from a concussion. Trey McBride is also still healthy and will be his best target.
But at wide receiver, Beck will be throwing to Reggie Virgil, Simi Fehoko, Devin Duvernay, and Harrison Wallace III. Wilson, Bourne, and Jalen Brooks are out for the season. Marvin Harrison Jr. was traded weeks ago as well.
Virgil, the rookie receiver out of Texas Tech, is going to be Beck's top option this week. The two linked up a few times in the preseason, but now they're going to have to mesh right away as both are now thrown into No. 1 roles in this offense.
It's a tough draw, facing Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald on this Rams defense for their debuts as starters in the NFL. But they have nothing to lose, as Beck has been announced as the starter with no one to threaten him on the depth chart. This is his job for the rest of the season.

Michael Carrick: Manchester United yet to make decision on whether to sack manager - BBC Sport
Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,
Michael Carrick has won 15 out of 32 games since taking over from Ruben Amorim as Manchester United's head coach in January
BySimon StoneManchester United reporter
Manchester United's board is yet to make a final decision on Michael Carrick's future.
The 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday means United, who are 18th in the table, have made their worst start to a domestic campaign in 40 years.
The draw was Carrick's third match in charge since the board decided to give the 45-year-old more time to improve the side's form after a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on 25 October.
The board felt Carrick - and the players - had earned the opportunity to show that they could turn the club's fortunes around, while the hierarchy were also aware that November's two-week break would offer an opportunity to reassess the situation in a calmer manner.
They are determined to do exactly that, knowing the results - one win, one draw and one defeat - and performances United have delivered in the past three games offer a mixed view of Carrick's tenure.
Conceding eight goals, winning only once and dropping into the relegation zone are obvious negatives. However, it is also felt fighting back from two goals down three times over the past two games showed that the players remain behind Carrick.
United's heirachy explored the possibility of replacing Carrick after the loss to Bournemouth last month, with ex-Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and former Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann considered.
Carrick said after the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa that he would not step down, but chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox will be influential in the decision whether to keep the former Middlesbrough boss.
United travel to arch rivals Liverpool on 22 November in their first match after the international break, with Carrick's side in 18th place in the Premier League.
With just one league win so far this term, it is United's lowest position having played 10 matches since the 1986-87 campaign.
Following the Anfield trip, five of United's next seven league opponents are in the bottom half of the league. This includes the four other sides currently in the bottom five, with meetings against Coventry, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland, all at Old Trafford.
Whether Carrick keeps his job or not, United will continue to struggle unless they stop conceding goals with such regularity.
Only Crystal Palace and Ipswich have let in more than United's 19 league goals.
They have conceded 15 times in the past three matches in all competitions. Their only clean sheet this term came against Azerbaijan title winners Sabah FK in the Champions League.
Four 'huge mistakes' that show Man Utd's defensive problems
"All the Premier League teams, whether they play home or away against Manchester United, fancy their chances because you can open them up and score goals," former United assistant boss Rene Meulensteen told BBC Radio Five Live.
"No matter what combination you find it's just not good enough. I think Michael Carrick will be constantly puzzled as to what back four he can play because there's no certainty they can keep a clean sheet."
Full-back Diogo Dalot took the brunt of fan ire at Old Trafford on Sunday.
Huge cheers greeted his number being shown to confirm he was being replaced, which then turned to boos when he reached the dugout.
Substitute Joshua Zirkzee, who suffered similar treatment when he was replaced after half an hour of a home defeat to Newcastle in December 2024, made a point of hugging Dalot as he made his way back to the bench.
Asked if it was time to take Dalot out of the firing line, Carrick urged caution.
"We've got to be careful with that," he said.
"I understand the frustration and I understand the disappointment of the supporters, I get it. We're all frustrated, we're all disappointed, and the players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that.
"Diogo gives absolutely everything. He's played in different positions and played really well at times.
"He gives a penalty away. He knows that. Maybe he can do a little bit better. He made a mistake. But I like what he brings to the team. He cares an awful lot and he's giving everything."

Nvidia’s advanced chips, which power much of today’s artificial intelligence, have put the company at the centre of the race for tech dominance between China and the US.
Since 2022, Washington has restricted sales of some of the most advanced chips to China over concerns that they could be used by the country’s military or intelligence agencies.
According to US intelligence officials cited by The New York Times, Alice Huang was tasked with getting Jensen Huang to lobby for looser restrictions on chip exports.
The Nvidia CEO had already been pushing for an easing of the rules, arguing that China’s domestic chip industry would get stronger without better access to US products.
But some experts say it is worth looking at how Alice Huang may have influenced decisions Nvidia made specifically about her former employer Megaspeed, which bought more than $4.8bn worth of Nvidia chips over the span of about two years.
Megaspeed has also been investigated over allegations that it helped Chinese companies get access to restricted chips. Megaspeed denies the allegation.
Ryan Fedasiuk, a fellow at the Foundation for American Innovation who studies Chinese technology and intelligence activities, pointed to reports from Bloomberg and The New York Times that Nvidia contacted the US Commerce Department about its investigation into Megaspeed.
He also noted that, in disclosures to the government, Nvidia appeared to vastly undercount the value of the chips it sold to the company.
“The question at hand is whether Nvidia took specific actions with respect to Megaspeed that it might not otherwise have done,” Fedasiuk told Al Jazeera, “possibly as a result of the personal relationship between the two executives.”
What sensitive information could have been a risk?
There are also questions about what sensitive information Alice Huang may have had access to through her relationship with Jensen Huang.
In an analysis published by the Council on Foreign Relations, a think tank, senior fellow Jessica Brandt pointed to information about how Nvidia designs its China-specific chips.
“Information about its conversations with policymakers could be helpful for anticipating where those controls and other policies are headed,” she said. “Understanding where it disagrees with government could expose fault lines to exploit. And that’s before we get into anything touching R&D [research and development].”
Fedasiuk raised similar concerns about what Alice Huang could have learned about Nvidia’s internal operations and plans for future products, as well as its customer base, which includes American and foreign tech companies.
He also pointed to Jensen Huang’s close ties to Trump and other senior White House officials.
“I have to wonder what kind of information about those people and about those relationships may have inadvertently made its way to Ms Huang or to Chinese intelligence,” he said.
So far, however, there is no publicly available evidence that Alice Huang got access to sensitive information from Nvidia or influenced Jensen Huang’s decisions. US intelligence also has not made public any evidence that Alice Huang was working for Chinese intelligence.
China has flatly denied the allegations of espionage.
“The claim of so-called ‘Chinese spies’ is completely groundless and is nothing but a smear campaign against China,” said Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun on Monday.

MarketsBusinessInvestingTechPolitics & PolicyVideoWatchlistInvesting ClubPROLivestreamMenu
Jim Cramer said Wednesday night that he was saddened by a news report that indicated Nvidia's board of directors is preparing to fire CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang amid a widening extramarital affair scandal. "Look, a Jensen-less Nvidia is an Nvidia many will not want to own," Jim said on "Mad Money," as not one but two bombshell articles were hitting the tape and the stock started sinking in after-hours trading. "I've always said, 'own it, don't trade it.' Well, I didn't think [anything like] this would happen. I don't know anyone who did. It's very sobering." After the show, Jim indicated that at this point he doesn't want to buy any more shares of Nvidia into the scandal-driven sell-off, nor does he want to sell ahead of next Tuesday's earnings report. However, he did express a belief that the company can still succeed over the long term even if it is without Huang at the helm. Shares of Nvidia fell more than 8% in extended trading Wednesday after The Wall Street Journal reported that the chipmaker's board was preparing to oust Huang, with plans to meet as soon as Wednesday to discuss his future. The Journal's story landed shortly after The New York Times reported that Huang had an affair with an executive who reports to him, Kimberly Powell, the chip giant's vice president of healthcare. Nvidia did not immediately respond to the Club's request for comment on Wednesday's reporting from The Journal and The Times. The reports came on top of The Times reporting Sunday that Nvidia's board was investigating an affair that Huang admitted to having with an executive at Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed — a woman U.S. intelligence agencies believe is a Chinese spy. On Tuesday, Nvidia's board said it hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead the inquiry. The Club has owned a position in Nvidia since 2019, years before the company's graphics processing units helped enable the generative AI boom, turning Nvidia into a juggernaut stock and vaulting Huang into rockstar CEO status. We downgraded our rating on Nvidia to a hold-equivalent 2 on Tuesday due to the uncertainty around Huang's future at the company. Earlier Wednesday, we said we wanted to initiate a position in rival Advanced Micro Devices due, in part, to a belief that AMD will win business as a result of the Huang scandal. However, our restrictions — which prevent us from trading any stock that Jim mentions on CNBC for a 72-hour period — stood in our way. We did, however, add AMD to our Bullpen watchlist , reflecting our intentions to initiate a stake once our restrictions lift. We also plan to exit Intel , while building up an AMD position. Jim said he vastly prefers AMD over Nvidia in this moment. Nevertheless, Jim said his experience watching Apple thrive after the death of co-founder and visionary CEO Steve Jobs is one reason why he doesn't want to blow out of Nvidia despite Huang potentially no longer serving as its chief executive. Tim Cook took Apple to even greater heights during his 15-year tenure, before passing the torch to now-CEO John Ternus on Sept. 1. Despite Huang's close association with Nvidia, Jim said he believes there is plenty of talent inside the company that can step into a potential leadership vacuum. In particular, he mentioned Ian Buck, a vice president who created the CUDA software program that was integral in Nvidia evolving from a video-game chip company into a data center and AI titan. Trump planning new military assault or tighter sanctions, say Iranian officials | Iran | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigation
An Iranian female volunteer uses a zipline in military training in Tehran on Tuesday. Some in the regime fear there could be renewed street protests if the economy worsens.Photograph: Majid Asgaripour/ReutersView image in fullscreenAn Iranian female volunteer uses a zipline in military training in Tehran on Tuesday. Some in the regime fear there could be renewed street protests if the economy worsens.Photograph: Majid Asgaripour/Reuters
Trump planning new military assault or tighter sanctions, say Iranian officials
Regime adviser says Tehran could be forced into pre-emptive strikes if stalemate continues
Senior Iranian officials believe the US is planning either further military strikes or an ever-tightening economic stranglehold that will push Tehran into retaliatory action.
The assessment comes from Mehdi Mohammadi, an adviser to Iran’s chief negotiator in talks with the US, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.
Mohammadi said on his Telegram channel that the Americans had proposed a timeframe of about two weeks after which Donald Trump would make a decision on military action. Mohammadi, who is regarded as a reliable indicator of Ghalibaf’s thinking, cast doubt on the US president’s claim that the military optionwas off the table. He claimed Washington was preparing for a limited strike and Iran was already preparing a response.
If the US sanctions continued, he said, a comprehensive pre-emptive war would be needed “to increase the cost of sanctions for the enemy”.
Mohammadi described the US response to Iran’s latest proposals on reopening the strait of Hormuz as “not only unsatisfactory but completely deceptive”. “They do not want to release the frozen funds,” he said. “They do not want to lift the sanctions and they do not want to stop the war in Lebanon.”
He also disclosed that Iran had rejected a request from the US vice-president, JD Vance, for a direct meeting with its negotiators before giving a response to Tehran’s conditions for lifting the siege on the strait.
For now, Trump has settled on a strategy of suffocating Iran through economic pressure and tightening the blockade on its oil exports while facilitating those of other Gulf states through Hormuz.
View image in fullscreenA tanker burns off Oman in the strait of Hormuz on Sunday, apparently after an attack by Iranian forces trying to stop oil shipments.Photograph: Social media/Reuters
Mohammadi’s assessments suggest some senior Iranians fear Washington’s strategy might work by destabilising the country. The thinking goes that economic turmoil might spark street protests, potentially around the anniversary of nationwide demonstrations that began in late December last year.
On this basis, the Iranian leadership might conclude that the status quo – a “no peace, no war” impasse – was not sustainable and pre-emptive action was required.
Despite Iranian claims that their blockade of the strait is working, there is concern that Brent crude is at a relatively low $93 a barrel, while Saudi oil production is near prewar levels of 9.3m barrels a day. In an attempt to close any loopholes, Iran said it bombed a US radar post on the Omani island of Didamar three days ago.
In another development, Mohsen Rezaei, the secretary of Iran’s national security council, said he had told Russia that Iran was not prepared for even a particle of its highly enriched stockpile of uranium to leave the country, saying it might be needed for planned nuclear-powered submarines.
A third senior official, Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Mojtaba Khamenei, Iran’s supreme leader, warned Europe that any complicity in the US blockade would be “an act of war that will be etched in the nation’s historical memory”.
Tehran has been increasingly clear that US bases in Europe will be targeted if fighting resumes. Rezaei said: “If American planes take off from a distant military base and come to this country to bomb Iran, we will also target that base. We are announcing this now so they have no excuse tomorrow.”
Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, gave the impression this week that the policy of economic strangulation was sufficient and described Iran’s demands as unrealistic. However, Trump is under pressure to resolve the crisis before the Democrats take charge of Congress on 3 January.
A Reuters Ipsos poll in the US shows 71% of Americans want Congress to pass legislation to end the war in Iran. The overwhelming message from the midterm elections was that the conflict was highly unpopular but the Democrats do not have a strategy to end it and open up the strait of Hormuz. This risks leaving the political initiative with the White House, and an increasingly hardline Iranian leadership.

Updated:11 November 2026 - 10:39 GMT+1
Visitors photograph The Foot Soldier, a National Mall statue mocking Donald Trump’s Vietnam War draft deferment, created by protest group Secret Handshake.
Visitors to Washington’s National Mall have been stopping to photograph a new satirical statue targeting President Donald Trump’s lack of military service, ahead of Veterans Day.
Titled “The Foot Soldier”, the gold-painted installation depicts Trump alongside a mascot named Toey. Created by protest art group Secret Handshake, it mocks the president’s Vietnam War-era medical deferment following a diagnosis of bone spurs.
A plaque beneath the statue delivers a sarcastic tribute to Trump’s military record, describing him as a soldier who reached the front lines of avoiding the draft. It also features his own remark: “I can be very military.”
The installation is the group’s latest political artwork, following previous displays including a golden statue of Trump holding hands with Jeffrey Epstein and a golden toilet.

article.title: Nga và Ukraine đạt thỏa thuận trao đổi tù binh quy mô lớn
article.summary: Sau hai ngày đàm phán tại Abu Dhabi dưới sự trung gian của Mỹ, Nga và Ukraine đã thống nhất thực hiện đợt trao đổi tù binh nhân đạo lớn nhất kể từ khi xung đột bắt đầu vào năm 2022.
body: Trong một diễn biến ngoại giao đáng chú ý, các quan chức từ Nga và Ukraine xác nhận hai bên đã đạt được thỏa thuận về một đợt trao đổi tù binh quy mô lớn. Quyết định này được đưa ra sau hai ngày đàm phán tại Abu Dhabi, Các Tiểu vương quốc Ả Rập Thống nhất, với sự tham gia trung gian từ phía Mỹ. Đây được xem là đợt giải phóng nhân đạo lớn nhất kể từ khi cuộc xung đột giữa hai quốc gia bùng nổ vào năm 2022.

Jared Kushner, đại diện phía Mỹ, cho biết các bên đã thống nhất về nguyên tắc và sẽ hoàn tất con số cụ thể trong thời gian tới. Phía Nga, đứng đầu là ông Vladimir Medinsky, và phía Ukraine, dẫn đầu bởi ông Rustem Umerov, đều xác nhận kế hoạch này. Cuộc gặp tại Abu Dhabi đánh dấu lần đầu tiên các phái đoàn hai nước ngồi lại đàm phán trực tiếp sau khoảng thời gian gián đoạn kéo dài chín tháng.

Mặc dù đạt được thỏa thuận về vấn đề nhân đạo, các nhà quan sát lưu ý rằng triển vọng về một lệnh ngừng bắn toàn diện vẫn còn rất xa vời. Ngoại trưởng Mỹ Marco Rubio đánh giá cuộc họp là "rất hiệu quả" nhưng cũng thận trọng cảnh báo rằng việc đạt được đột phá để chấm dứt chiến tranh sẽ cần thêm nhiều thời gian. Hiện tại, cả hai bên vẫn giữ lập trường cứng rắn và chưa có dấu hiệu sẵn sàng nhượng bộ đối với các yêu cầu cốt lõi của nhau.

Bối cảnh đàm phán lần này diễn ra trong tình trạng căng thẳng leo thang trên thực địa. Trong khi các cuộc thảo luận diễn ra, giao tranh vẫn tiếp diễn dọc theo tiền tuyến. Nga tiếp tục các đợt tấn công bằng tên lửa và máy bay không người lái vào cơ sở hạ tầng năng lượng của Ukraine, trong khi Ukraine cũng đáp trả bằng các đòn tấn công tầm xa vào các mục tiêu quân sự và hạ tầng dầu khí của Nga. Sự kiện này cho thấy dù các kênh đối thoại nhân đạo đang được khơi thông, con đường dẫn đến hòa bình bền vững vẫn đối mặt với nhiều thách thức phức tạp.

article.title: Cựu kỵ sĩ Tom O’Brien qua đời ở tuổi 39
article.summary: Cộng đồng đua ngựa thế giới đang bày tỏ niềm tiếc thương sâu sắc trước sự ra đi của Tom O’Brien, kỵ sĩ từng giành nhiều chiến thắng tại Cheltenham Festival, sau thời gian dài chiến đấu với căn bệnh ung thư.
body: Giới đua ngựa Anh và Ireland đang chìm trong không khí tang thương sau khi thông tin kỵ sĩ Tom O’Brien qua đời ở tuổi 39 được xác nhận. Ông ra đi sau một thời gian dài kiên cường chiến đấu với căn bệnh ung thư, để lại niềm tiếc thương lớn cho gia đình, bạn bè và đồng nghiệp trong môn thể thao này.

Trong suốt sự nghiệp kéo dài hai thập kỷ, O’Brien đã khẳng định vị thế là một trong những kỵ sĩ đáng tin cậy nhất. Ông ghi dấu ấn với hơn 1.000 chiến thắng trong các cuộc đua vượt rào, bao gồm năm danh hiệu Grade One danh giá và hai chiến thắng tại Cheltenham Festival. Những thành tựu nổi bật của ông bao gồm các chiến thắng tại Stayers’ Hurdle ở Aintree và Kauto Star Novice Chase ở Kempton cùng ngựa đua Thyme Hill. Ngoài ra, ông còn được nhớ đến với chiến thắng đầy cảm hứng cùng Dream Alliance tại giải Welsh Grand National năm 2009, câu chuyện sau đó đã truyền cảm hứng cho bộ phim điện ảnh Dream Horse.

Gắn bó phần lớn sự nghiệp với lò huấn luyện của Philip Hobbs gần Minehead, O’Brien được đồng nghiệp và các huấn luyện viên đánh giá cao không chỉ bởi tài năng trên yên ngựa mà còn bởi nhân cách tốt đẹp. Sau khi giải nghệ vào tháng 4 năm 2023, ông đã chuyển sang vai trò mới trong đội ngũ giám sát của Cơ quan Đua ngựa Anh (BHA).

Brant Dunshea, Giám đốc điều hành BHA, chia sẻ rằng sự ra đi của O’Brien là một mất mát to lớn đối với cộng đồng đua ngựa. Ông được nhớ đến như một người đồng nghiệp tận tụy, một người bạn trung thành và một người cha, người chồng mẫu mực. Sự ra đi của ông ở tuổi 39, khi vẫn còn nhiều dự định dang dở, đã để lại khoảng trống khó bù đắp trong lòng những người hâm mộ và những người từng có cơ hội làm việc cùng ông trên cả hai bờ biển Ireland.

article.title: FIFA thay đổi quy tắc bốc thăm World Cup nữ 2027
article.summary: FIFA vừa xác nhận thay đổi quan trọng trong quy trình bốc thăm World Cup nữ 2027, nhằm tách biệt bốn đội dẫn đầu bảng xếp hạng thế giới cho đến vòng bán kết.
body: Liên đoàn Bóng đá Thế giới (FIFA) vừa chính thức xác nhận một thay đổi quan trọng trong quy trình bốc thăm cho giải vô địch bóng đá nữ thế giới 2027. Theo đó, bốn đội tuyển có thứ hạng cao nhất trên bảng xếp hạng FIFA sẽ được tách biệt ở các nhánh đấu khác nhau cho đến vòng bán kết. Điều kiện tiên quyết để quy tắc này được kích hoạt là các đội bóng phải giành quyền đứng đầu bảng đấu của mình tại vòng chung kết.

Thể thức này được áp dụng tương tự như cách FIFA đã triển khai tại World Cup nam 2026. Hiện tại, Tây Ban Nha, Mỹ, Đức và Anh đang là bốn đội dẫn đầu bảng xếp hạng thế giới. Tuy nhiên, danh sách các đội hạt giống chính thức sẽ được chốt dựa trên bảng xếp hạng cập nhật ngày 7 tháng 12 tới, ngay trước thời điểm lễ bốc thăm diễn ra vào ngày 11 tháng 12 tại Rio de Janeiro.

Việc áp dụng quy tắc này nhằm đảm bảo tính cạnh tranh cao nhất cho giải đấu. Nếu các đội hạt giống duy trì được vị thế và giành quyền vào vòng trong, người hâm mộ sẽ chỉ có thể chứng kiến các cuộc đối đầu trực tiếp giữa họ từ vòng bán kết trở đi. Trong khi đó, Brazil với tư cách là chủ nhà đã được mặc định vào bảng A và sẽ tham gia trận khai mạc tại sân vận động Maracanã vào ngày 24 tháng 6 năm 2027.

Hiện tại, một số đội bóng hàng đầu như Mỹ và Anh vẫn đang trong quá trình hoàn tất thủ tục giành vé tham dự giải đấu. Các đội tuyển còn lại trong nhóm hạt giống dự kiến sẽ bao gồm Pháp, Brazil, Thụy Điển cùng các đội bóng có thứ hạng cao khác, tùy thuộc vào kết quả các trận đấu vòng loại cuối cùng.

lead_title: Russia and Ukraine agree to a large exchange of prisoners of war, officials say

Russia and Ukraine agree to a large exchange of prisoners of war, officials sayRussia and Ukraine have agreed to a large exchange of prisoners of war. U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi led to this decision, marking the biggest humanitarian release since the war began in 2022.
Russia and Ukraine agree to a large exchange of prisoners of war, officials say
Rustem Umerov, Head of Foreign Intelligence Service of Ukraine, third from the right, speaks during the coordination meeting before the trilateral talks between Russia and Ukraine mediated by the US in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, Tuesday, Nov. 10, 2026.Altaf Qadri/APhide caption
ABU DHABI, United Arab Emirates — Officials at U.S.-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine said Wednesday that the sides have agreed a large exchange of prisoners of war.
Kushner and Witkoff renew peace talks to end war between Russia and Ukraine
"One of the positives is we agreed that we're going to have the biggest humanitarian release of prisoners, which we're going to finalize the numbers tomorrow," Jared Kushner, U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law, said after the two days of talks in Abu Dhabi ended.
Vladimir Medinsky, the head of the Russian delegation, and Rustem Umerov, who led Kyiv's delegation in Abu Dhabi, confirmed the planned exchange.
Hopes were low for any major breakthrough in the first meeting in nine months between the delegations. Russia and Ukraine have from time to time swapped prisoners during their nearly five-year war.
U.S. officials say they are determined to revive Washington's peace efforts that so far have failed to deliver significant results.
Kushner says he and U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff will travel to Moscow on Thursday to meet with President Vladimir Putin, then fly to Dublin to meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
The context of the negotiations has changed since the last meeting in February in Geneva. The Trump administration has to reckon with Democrats, who could demand more support for Ukraine, taking over the U.S. Congress in January following the U.S. midterm elections.
Also, Russia's wartime economy is under heavy strain, and Ukraine is reeling from devastating aerial attacks on its power grid.
Europe to join U.S.-brokered Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, defying Kremlin objections
Umerov said Kyiv's delegation is expected to meet Wednesday with European officials.
Moscow doesn't want European countries, which are concerned about Russia's conduct and broader intentions on the continent, involved in the direct negotiations. However, representatives of European governments, the European Union and NATO were in Abu Dhabi and were consulting with the Ukrainian delegation, officials said.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Tuesday's session was "constructive and quite substantive."
The talks were largely about humanitarian issues, including possible prisoner exchanges and returning Ukrainian civilians in captivity, as well as children taken from the country, he said.
Security guarantees also were discussed, he said. However, Russia and Ukraine have shown no sign of a willingness to compromise on their demands.
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the meeting "very productive," while cautioning that a breakthrough on stopping the war will take time.
The Abu Dhabi talks are being held against the backdrop of continued fighting on the front line, where little territory has changed hands this year.
Meanwhile, both countries are battering each other with long-range missiles and drones.
Overnight, Russia struck the southern Zaporizhzhia region and the eastern city of Kharkiv, wounding seven civilians and damaging property.
Russia's Defense Ministry said that air defenses downed 627 Ukrainian drones overnight, 150 of them over the region around St. Petersburg, according to the regional Gov. Alexander Drozdenko.
He said that the drones started a fire at the port of Ust-Luga, one of the main facilities for Russian oil exports, injuring three workers.

In 27 regions of the Russian Federation, the immunodeficiency virus is spreading among the entire population, not only risk groups, according to the latest Rospotrebnadzor data. People increasingly pass the virus to one another, often unaware they are infected.
In 27 Russian regions, there is a generalised HIV epidemic. This was reported by the Central Research Institute of Epidemiology of Rospotrebnadzor. Scientists use this term for the stage when the human immunodeficiency virus spreads in the general population rather than only among risk groups.
In these regions, HIV is diagnosed in more than 1% of pregnant women. The situation is most serious in the Kemerovo, Irkutsk and Sverdlovsk regions.
And although, according to the Central Research Institute for the Prevention and Control of AIDS, 45,000 new HIV cases were detected in Russia in 2025, which is 13.4% lower than in 2024, last year a record was set for the number of HIV and hepatitis infections in medical institutions, according to statistics compiled by the specialist portalMedvestnik.
Experts record the highest level of HIV and hepatitis infections in medical facilities in 15 years
These are the highest figures in the past 15 years. Clusters of viral hepatitis C and mixed HIV plus hepatitis infections predominate, said Yelena Igonina, head of the Department for the Epidemiological Wellbeing of the Population at Rospotrebnadzor. In 2025, eight clusters of infection were recorded in healthcare facilities in Russia, with 104 patients infected.
According to Rospotrebnadzor, investigations continued in 2026 into 11 clusters of infection in the territory of ten regions of Russia, where the spread of HIV and hepatitis in medical organisations is suspected. In Moscow, an investigation is underway into a cluster in which 22 cases of viral hepatitis C have been identified.
One of the largest confirmed clusters in the past two years was the infection of 82 people in a sanatorium in Kabardino-Balkaria. While receiving medical care, 76 patients contracted viral hepatitis C and six were found to have mixed infections. In oncology hospitals in Kamchatka Territory and Buryatia, 147 and 42 patients, respectively, were infected with hepatitis. Another three hepatitis C clusters were identified in dialysis centres in the Samara and Kursk regions, where 26 people were affected.
Experts describe violations of sanitary and epidemiological rules as the main cause of the infections, including the use of single-use catheters or glucometers on several patients. In such situations, the source is usually patients with undiagnosed infections.

UN report: AIDS could end by 2030 if world leaders help ease access to treatment
Yelena Igonina notes that these "systemic and gross violations" have become entrenched in today’s Russia. Although simultaneous testing for hepatitis C antibodies and RNA covers blood, component, organ and tissue donors well, testing for RNA among other categories that should be tested, namely dialysis, haematology and transplant patients, contacts in hepatitis clusters, children under one born to mothers with HIV and patients with immunodeficiency, is significantly lagging behind.
In addition, for the first time in six years, two cases of HIV infection via transfusion of blood components were identified in 2026, the Central Research Institute of Epidemiology of Rospotrebnadzor added.
When hospitals receive large numbers of people with undiagnosed infections, international HIV consultant Aleksei Verter toldCurrent Time, this means that "the infectious process in the country is latent, hidden" and a great many people do not know they are infected.
Despite lower mortality, the number of people living with HIV is rising
Despite a decline in HIV incidence and mortality in Russia in recent years, the number of people infected continues to grow,Medvestnik’s authorsnote. Statistics show that for each death there are one and a half new infections, that is, the number of people "living with HIV continues to grow constantly", explains Natalya Ladnaya.
The decline was preceded by a long period of rising incidence, but in the past three years rates of morbidity and mortality among people with HIV have been falling and, according to her preliminary data, this trend will continue in 2026. At the same time, the expert is convinced that there is no reason to rest on one’s laurels, since "the dynamics can change rapidly".
In recent years, the number of deaths from HIV in Russia has been between 30,000 and 34,000 per year. This is an extremely high figure, stresses the head of the research department for the prevention and control of AIDS at the Central Research Institute of Rospotrebnadzor. "Among all the countries in the world there are only 15 where more than 15,000 deaths of people with HIV are recorded, including Russia." "The highest HIV incidence rates per 100,000 population in the European region are in Russia, Ukraine and North Macedonia", says Central Research Institute of Epidemiology director and Rospotrebnadzor academician Vasily Akimkin.
HIV infection has become the leading cause of death among Russians of working age. Among men aged 40 to 49, more than 3% are affected by the virus, clarifies Natalya Ladnaya, while the average age of those infected in Russia has increased over the past 15 years from 32 to 44. It is also noteworthy that two-thirds of new HIV transmissionsoccurthrough heterosexual contact.
More than 1.232 million people with a confirmed HIV diagnosis now live in Russia, which is 0.8% of the country’s population, Akimkin adds. Rospotrebnadzor has warned that if current approaches to prevention and treatment remain unchanged, the number of people living with HIV in Russia could reach 1.47 million by 2030, according to the agency’s mathematical model. Under this scenario, the annual number of new cases will be between 31,000 and 51,000, and the number of deaths included in the model could rise to 51,000 a year, which is linked, among other things, to population ageing.

'We call it war-life balance': Daryna's daily struggle to live, survive in wartime Ukraine
from our special correspondent in Ukraine –Daryna, 25, entered adulthood in a country at war. Since Russia’s full-scale invasion, her days have been shaped by air raid alerts, power outages and nights spent sheltering in the subway. Despite the uncertainty that shadows every day, she is determined to preserve a semblance of normal life in Kyiv. FRANCE 24 met a young woman who has become emblematic of a generation learning to live under daily bombardment.
Issued on:09/11/2026 - 10:10Modified:09/11/2026 - 11:29
11 minReading timeShareBy:Assiya HAMZA/Mélina HUETDaryna has adapted her life to wartime realities since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Kyiv on October 26, 2026. © Melina Huet, FRANCE 24
Daryna grew up before her time, far too quickly. War gave her no choice. TheKyivresident was barely 21 whenRussialaunched its full-scale invasion ofUkraine. Nearly five years into the conflict, she is clinging, as best she can, to what has become a dystopian version of normal life.
Read moreUkraine and Russia are taking the war underground as drones saturate the battlefield
“Some foreigners think tanks are rolling through Kyiv, that the city is an active frontline,” says the striking young woman. “Others look at my life on social media and think I live a perfectly normal life because I go to the gym, read books and go out on weekends. But my life is not normal at all.”
Living in a 19th-century building in the bohemian district of Podil, Daryna has carefully curated her apartment.
“I chose it because it was beautiful, historic and so different from the Soviet-era buildings and apartments I grew up in,” says the Rivne native from northwestern Ukraine. “I wanted to make it as beautiful as possible because it’s important to surround yourself with beauty and things that bring you comfort during wartime.”
In the spacious living room with its green walls, culture is everywhere: art books, novels, copies of the iconic American magazine The New Yorker, and music – lots of music.
An impressive vinyl collection, neatly stacked in a wooden crate, rests on the polished hardwood floor beside an electric piano. A small speaker fills the room with the haunting voice of Radiohead’s singer and songwriter Thom Yorke.
“When I think about all my books, my records, my piano, and the possibility of losing everything in an explosion, it makes me incredibly sad,” says the young woman, whose hazel eyes are tinged with melancholy. “Some people started buying fewer things when the war began. At first, I did the same. But eventually I realised I needed more things around me to make this place feel like home.”
Read moreUkraine’s Pavlohrad refuses to yield to Putin despite unrelenting bombardment
Seated comfortably in an old wooden armchair, Daryna recounts how a friend’s apartment, just a few streets away, was damaged in an explosion a few days earlier.
“It was a street people considered safe. A drone crashed into the garden and then exploded. The blast wave blew out the windows. She’s had everything repaired, but she’s still finding shards of glass everywhere,” she says, before breaking into laughter.
“Honestly, I think being a glazier is probably the most profitable business in Ukraine right now.”
Like all Ukrainians, Daryna spends much of her time checking air raid alerts on her phone and making sure her loved ones are safe in Kyiv, October 26, 2026. © Melina Huet, FRANCE 24
Daryna breaks off mid-sentence. A notification sounds. Her phone emits a shrill alert. “There’s an air raid alert. It’s a yellow alert, which means Kyiv is being targeted bydrones. I think we should check where they’re headed,” she says, scrolling through her Telegram messages. “Oh, they’re only heading towards the city centre. It should be fine, I think. It’s not very close.”
Setting her phone aside, the cybersecurity journalist resumes her explanation. “We also have red alerts, which mean there is a risk the city could come under missile attack. When the war began, there were only red alerts. They applied to both drones and missiles. But recently, the authorities changed the system to distinguish between the two. It’s very useful because it gives people a better sense of how concerned they should be and what level of anxiety they need to prepare for.”
Screenshot of Ukraine’s air raid alert app on a mobile phone in Kyiv, November 2, 2026. False alerts were reported across several regions that day. Gleb Garanich, Reuters
These alerts happen at any hour of the day or night, and last between a few minutes and several hours. Their arrival is announced by air raid sirens blaring from loudspeakers across the city. Residents are advised to seek shelter as quickly as possible.
“For a while, I slept in my walk-in closet. I moved my mattress and pillows in there. But one night, during an explosion, part of the ceiling fell on my head. I also tried sleeping in my bathtub, but that proved dangerous too because there’s a mirror in my bathroom. Since then, I’ve mostly slept in the hallway, which is considered the safest place in the apartment.”
It's constant psychological strain, one that grows heavier by the day. Some red alerts are more terrifying than others.
Read more‘Not an isolated incident’: Russian drones stalk Ukraine’s civilians in ‘human safaris’
On October 21, Kyiv residents endured a night of terror. Russia launched three waves of 21 missiles targeting residential buildings, energy infrastructure and shopping centres.
Many residents made their way to shelters, underground parking garages and subway stations. Others remained huddled in their homes, feeling the walls shake, waiting for the shock waves and listening to the explosions.
Kyiv has become nearly as dangerous as cities closer to the front line. It is a deliberateKremlinstrategy aimed at sowing panic and, potentially, triggering a mass exodus from a capital it failed to capture in the early days of the full-scale invasion in 2022.
While fear and exhaustion can sometimes be read on people’s faces, many Ukrainians no longer even react to the piercing sound of air raid alerts. It is an attitude that can surprise outsiders, even unsettle them.
But how can people keep going to shelters when the alerts come one after another? They still have to work, study or simply sleep.

What is India offering, why does it want the role, and can it deliver?
“India is ready to mediate in establishing food corridors, and we are counting on these efforts to continue,” Zelenskyy posted on X after the call. The leaders discussed Russia’s blocking of grain exports in the Black Sea, he said.
Modi did not mention food corridors or the Black Sea, but reaffirmed India’s commitment to contributing “in every possible way” towards a peaceful resolution.
Jaishankar said his call with Lavrov focused on the war and “ongoing diplomatic initiatives”.
While New Delhi has not published a formal plan, the offer builds on proposals Indian officials floated for weeks.
During a visit to Kyiv in September, Jaishankar reportedly spoke of a potential pause on strikes against Black Sea shipping and energy infrastructure. On October 4, he said India was talking to both Russia and Ukraine about shipping safety, grain and energy exports and “non-attack possibilities”.
“India has become quietly proactive of late,” Praveen Donthi, senior India analyst at the International Crisis Group, told Al Jazeera.
Previously, India was “reticent … regarding a mediation role” and limited to “rhetorical calls for diplomacy and dialogue”, he added. Jaishankar’s September visit was a sign of stepping up, he said.
By early October, Kyiv received four ceasefire proposals from India, Turkiye, Egypt and the US.

Kyiv says it will accept an energy and Black Sea truce only if the two come together. Russia has so far rejected partial ceasefires, insisting on a comprehensive peace agreement instead.
Ravi Joshi, a visiting fellow at the Observer Research Foundation in New Delhi and former civil servant, told DD India that “an immediate understanding or a ceasefire is important, and that’s what India can talk about”.
He added that insurance remains a current challenge.
“The ships are not being adequately insured. The insurers are not guaranteeing the safety of the ships,” he said.
The Black Sea tensions cost India directly.

India is also the world’s biggest importer of vegetable oils and buys most of its sunflower oil from Russia and Ukraine. Its edible oil imports fell 7 percent in September.
