Who is David Walliams? His career and controversies including Little Britain and BGT - BBC News
Image source,Getty ImagesByColin Paterson,Entertainment correspondentandIan Youngs,Culture reporter
David Walliams has been accused of grooming young fans and harassing women in the workplace, after failing to stop the Guardian and ITN publishing claims against him.
A three-year investigation,externalby the two news organisations alleged the Little Britain star and former Britain's Got Talent judgepreyed on teenage girls as young as 15 and young women,externalfor sexual purposes.
He had sought a High Court injunction to prevent publication, with his lawyers arguing if allegations were made public Walliams would likely kill himself. The court refused the request.
Walliams has denied all of the allegations but in a letter to journalists working on the investigation acknowledged "at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with".
He added: "I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me."
The 55-year-old became a household name in the early 2000s through Little Britain, his comedy sketch show with Matt Lucas broadcast on the BBC.
Walliams published his first children's book, The Boy in the Dress, in 2008, and his stories soon became best-sellers and led to comparisons with Roald Dahl.
His 23 children's books have sold more than 50 million copies worldwide, but he was dropped by publisher HarperCollins in 2025 after allegations of inappropriate behaviour, which he denied.
In 2012, Walliams became a judge on Britain's Got Talent, and was voted best TV judge at the National TV Awards (NTAs) four times. He was replaced as a judge in 2022.
Before entering showbusiness, Walliams was born David Williams but changed his surname's spelling to avoid having the same name as another member of entertainment union Equity.
He was married to Dutch model Lara Stone from 2010 to 2015 and they have a son.
That hasn't stopped speculation about Walliams' sexuality. He has described himself as "bi-curious" and called his 2012 autobiography Camp David – but said he isn't attracted to men in the way he is to women.
Matt Lucas and David Walliams as Florence and Emily in Little Britain
Walliams and Lucas won a string of awards for Little Britain including three Baftas and two International Emmys, and the programme was watched by 10 million people in the UK.
But in the two decades since it ended, views about the show and what is and is not acceptable to joke about have radically altered. The programme has been criticised for its use of blackface and for stereotyping and mocking characters from minority and marginalised groups.
In the wake of the Black Lives Matter movement in 2020, Little Britain was removed from streaming services including BBC iPlayer, Netflix and BritBox.
Another of the duo's shows, 2010 airport comedy Come Fly With Me, was also removed from BritBox a decade after its original broadcast, due to the show's use of racial stereotypes and using make-up to portray people from other ethnic groups.
Little Britain was restored to iPlayer in 2022 with several scenes cut out. Walliams and Lucas said they had re-edited the show to "better reflect the changes in the cultural landscape since the show was made".
Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,
Walliams won the National Television Award for best TV judge four times for Britain's Got Talent
Not all the criticisms of Walliams have involved new standards being applied to older work.
Walliams had to apologise after two charity performances, during which he yanked down not only the trousers but also the underwear of actor Jeremy Edwards and music producer Mark Ronson.
In 2020, he was booed while hosting the NTAs after making a joke about Caroline Flack being out of work, at a time when she had stepped down from hosting Love Island and was waiting to appear in court, having been charged for actual bodily harm following a row with her boyfriend.
Later in 2022, he was replaced as a judge on Britain's Got Talent after a Guardian story about a leaked recording of Walliams making insulting remarks about contestants during breaks from filming.
In the incident, which happened in 2020, he spoke about a pensioner to whom he had taken a strong dislike and a woman who he described as "the slightly boring girl you would meet in the pub" who "you would want to have sex with, but then decide not to". He used much stronger language when talking about both.
Walliams apologised, explaining: "These were private conversations and - like most conversations with friends - were never intended to be shared. Nevertheless, I am sorry."
He sued the show's producers Freemantle for misuse of his private information and breaching data protection laws. An "amicable resolution" was reached, with the production company apologising for the recording being made public.
Walliams raised more than £3m for the Sport Relief charity by swimming the English Channel in 2006 and the length of the River Thames in 2011.
Further controversy came in June 2025, when it emerged that Walliams had given two Nazi salutes during the recording of BBC One's Would I Lie to You? Christmas special.
Banijay UK, which owned the show's production company Zeppotron, apologised, adding: "It was immediately acknowledged during the recording that this segment would not be broadcast under any circumstances." Walliams has never commented on the incident.
Then in December 2025, HarperCollins, the publisher of his hugely successful children's books, announced that following a change of CEO, the company would no longer look after new releases by Walliams.
He was dropped over allegations he had harassed female members of staff, with HarperCollins explaining that the company took "employee wellbeing extremely seriously and has processes in place for reporting and investigating concerns".
The Daily Telegraph reported that an internal investigation had been opened the previous year after a complaint was made by a junior member of staff about his behaviour. This reportedly found that staff had been told to only meet Walliams in pairs and advised against going to his house.
Walliams' spokesperson responded by saying he "strongly denies that he has behaved inappropriately" and that he had "never been informed of any allegations raised against him" by the publisher.

Sydney private school accused of mishandling sexual abuse allegations should be banned from enrolling new students, inquiry says
Inquiry recommends police investigate allegations of sexual assault and other abuse at Redeemer Baptist school
Get ourbreaking news email,free appordaily news podcast
An investigation into a private religious school accused of mishandling allegations of sexual, physical, psychological, spiritual and financial abuse has recommended it be barred from enrolling new students.
Former students and teachers of western Sydney’s Redeemer Baptist school told aNew South Walesparliamentary inquiry about a string of disturbing allegations.
They included students being made to share beds with teachers and its principal once wandering naked through a common area.
In a report tabled in state parliament on Tuesday, a committee found the school – run by the Redeemer Baptist Church – breached basic child safeguarding standards.
Sexual assault allegations were not handled appropriately and the school put children at significant risk of harm, the committee found.
Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email
It also found staff at the school lacked essential workplace rights and failed to satisfy basic standards of good governance.
The committee recommended the school be prevented from enrolling new students while it was under investigation by the NSW Education Standards Authority.
It also recommended the allegations raised in the inquiry be investigated by NSW police and the office of the children’s guardian.
The committee chair and Greens MP, Abigail Boyd, noted the school was subjected to parliamentary scrutiny in 2006, but no procedures had been put in place to monitor what was clearly a “high-risk situation”.
View image in fullscreenRedeemer Baptist school in Parramatta.Photograph: Sarah Wilson/AAP
She said it was thanks to the bravery of those who had spoken out that the committee had enough evidence to make its strong findings and recommendations.
The school received about $6m a year in government funding, Boyd said, and had enough cash to launch legal challenges against those who raised their voices against the religious group.
“They also have deep political ties with both state and federal politicians,” she told parliament.
People who had escaped the school appeared to be absolutely terrified of its leaders, Boyd said.
“When you know that leaving means leaving with no financial assets, and when you have finally managed to escape, it’s no wonder that you would be terrified of your abuser,” she said in parliament.
The committee lashed a lack of regulatory oversight, including from the education authority, suggesting a number of alarming matters needed proper investigation.
They included allegations of persistent Centrelink fraud and dodgy tax practices.
“It is, at the very least, troubling that an asset-rich, seemingly prosperous school operates by withholding wages from its workforce, who claim benefits, while the school receives millions of dollars in public funding,” the report said.
A Redeemer Baptist school spokesperson previously said the school had fully cooperated with the relevant regulators.
“Redeemer Baptist School takes its child safety obligations extremely seriously and has an unblemished record of compliance with state and federal regulators for 45 years,” they said.
The school did not immediately respond to a request for comment following the report’s release.

fact_units.text: His career and controversies including Little Britain and BGT - BBC News
David Walliams has been accused of grooming young fans and harassing women in the workplace, after failing to stop the Guardian and ITN publishing claims against him.

A three-year investigation,externalby the two news organisations alleged the Little Britain star and former Britain's Got Talent judgepreyed on teenage girls as young as 15 and young women,externalfor sexual purposes.
He had sought a High Court injunction to prevent publication, with his lawyers arguing if allegations were made public Walliams would likely kill himself.

Walliams has denied all of the allegations but in a letter to journalists working on the investigation acknowledged "at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with".
I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me."
The 55-year-old became a household name in the early 2000s through Little Britain, his comedy sketch show with Matt Lucas broadcast on the BBC.
Walliams published his first children's book, The Boy in the Dress, in 2008, and his stories soon became best-sellers and led to comparisons with Roald Dahl.
His 23 children's books have sold more than 50 million copies worldwide, but he was dropped by publisher HarperCollins in 2025 after allegations of inappropriate behaviour, which he denied.
In 2012, Walliams became a judge on Britain's Got Talent, and was voted best TV judge at the National TV Awards (NTAs) four times.
He was replaced as a judge in 2022.
Before entering showbusiness, Walliams was born David Williams but changed his surname's spelling to avoid having the same name as another member of entertainment union Equity.
He was married to Dutch model Lara Stone from 2010 to 2015 and they have a son.
He has described himself as "bi-curious" and called his 2012 autobiography Camp David – but said he isn't attracted to men in the way he is to women.
Matt Lucas and David Walliams as Florence and Emily in Little Britain
Walliams and Lucas won a string of awards for Little Britain including three Baftas and two International Emmys, and the programme was watched by 10 million people in the UK.
But in the two decades since it ended, views about the show and what is and is not acceptable to joke about have radically altered.
The programme has been criticised for its use of blackface and for stereotyping and mocking characters from minority and marginalised groups.
In the wake of the Black Lives Matter movement in 2020, Little Britain was removed from streaming services including BBC iPlayer, Netflix and BritBox.

Another of the duo's shows, 2010 airport comedy Come Fly With Me, was also removed from BritBox a decade after its original broadcast, due to the show's use of racial stereotypes and using make-up to portray people from other ethnic groups.
Little Britain was restored to iPlayer in 2022 with several scenes cut out.
Walliams and Lucas said they had re-edited the show to "better reflect the changes in the cultural landscape since the show was made".
Walliams won the National Television Award for best TV judge four times for Britain's Got Talent
Not all the criticisms of Walliams have involved new standards being applied to older work.
Walliams had to apologise after two charity performances, during which he yanked down not only the trousers but also the underwear of actor Jeremy Edwards and music producer Mark Ronson.

In 2020, he was booed while hosting the NTAs after making a joke about Caroline Flack being out of work, at a time when she had stepped down from hosting Love Island and was waiting to appear in court, having been charged for actual bodily harm following a row with her boyfriend.
Later in 2022, he was replaced as a judge on Britain's Got Talent after a Guardian story about a leaked recording of Walliams making insulting remarks about contestants during breaks from filming.

In the incident, which happened in 2020, he spoke about a pensioner to whom he had taken a strong dislike and a woman who he described as "the slightly boring girl you would meet in the pub" who "you would want to have sex with, but then decide not to".
He used much stronger language when talking about both.
Walliams apologised, explaining: "These were private conversations and - like most conversations with friends - were never intended to be shared.
He sued the show's producers Freemantle for misuse of his private information and breaching data protection laws.
An "amicable resolution" was reached, with the production company apologising for the recording being made public.
Walliams raised more than £3m for the Sport Relief charity by swimming the English Channel in 2006 and the length of the River Thames in 2011.
Further controversy came in June 2025, when it emerged that Walliams had given two Nazi salutes during the recording of BBC One's Would I Lie to You?

Banijay UK, which owned the show's production company Zeppotron, apologised, adding: "It was immediately acknowledged during the recording that this segment would not be broadcast under any circumstances." Walliams has never commented on the incident.

Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,
Senior officials from Ukraine, Russia and the US will reconvene on Wednesday for a second day of talks
ByLaura GozziandAbdujalil Abdurasulov,Reporting fromKyiv
Published10 November 2026, 00:09 GMT
The first day of trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine has concluded in Abu Dhabi.
While senior officials from Kyiv and Moscow were tight-lipped after the four hour-long discussions - due to resume on Wednesday - US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who did not attend the talks, said they had been "very productive".
Although expectations for a breakthrough that ends Russia's full-scale war on Ukraine are low, US officials said earlier that Moscow and Kyiv were privately showing "a little bit of flexibility" on the issue of who would control Ukraine's eastern regions in a postwar scenario.
At the start of Tuesday's talks President Donald Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, told delegates that the US had "narrowed the gaps" between the two sides, without providing details, and hoped to move towards a "solution that hopefully ends the war".
Kushner said earlier the talks would be focused on addressing the "postwar security concerns" of both Russia and Ukraine.
He and Trump peace envoy Steve Witkoff also met Ukrainian and European and Nato officials on the sidelines of the main meeting.
European leaders have largely been excluded from peace talks until now, but they have pushed to be included in the discussions amid concerns that decisions about their continent's security would be made without them.
The Americans appear to support this, with Rubio acknowledging during a visit to Paris that the Europeans "are a part of solving this problem for the long term".
However, "the Russians have a bad taste in their mouth with the Europeans", according to a US official.
Some proposals favoured by EU officials - such as calling an unconditional ceasefire as a prerequisite for peace negotiations - are routinely rejected by Moscow. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said on Tuesday that a truce would just allow Kyiv to regroup. "We will not agree to it," he said.
Moscow and Kyiv's positions are still far apart on ending the conflict.
A key area of disagreement involves Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is mostly occupied by Russia.
Moscow has demanded that Ukraine relinquish the parts of Donetsk it still holds, while Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line to maintain control over those areas, which it says are crucial to its future security.
While neither side has budged on these demands, the US official speaking on the eve of the talks suggested that this was just the public stance and that Moscow and Kyiv had shown "a little bit of flexibility, privately".
However, he acknowledged the issue would not be solved without discussions about a new "security architecture".
"They will not solve the Donetsk issue and the territorial issue until they know what the security architecture is going to be after the war," the official said. "And keep in mind, we're not going to be able to finalise one without the other."
For Ukraine, a post-war "security architecture" may include reassurance that allies will come to its aid if it comes under attack again. For Russia, that could be its longstanding ambition to see Nato roll back from Eastern Europe – which would be alarming to Europeans.
The framework being proposed includes security consultations and crisis communications hotlines, as well as "reciprocal de-escalation measures" between the two. The officials also floated the re-activation of the Nato-Russia Council that has been largely paused since 2022.
Image source,AFP via Getty ImagesImage caption,
Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff are part of the US delegation that will attend the talks in Abu Dhabi
The last round of trilateral talks, held in Geneva in February, ended without a breakthrough. Soon after, the US-Israel war on Iran diverted Washington's attention from Ukraine, and no other discussions were held since.
From the start of his second term in office, US President Donald Trump – who once boasted he could end the war in Ukraine within a day – has spearheaded several rounds of talks to end the conflict, albeit with little success.
Meanwhile, his increasingly conciliatory approach towards Moscow has fuelled deep unease in Kyiv and across the European Union.
After meeting Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev in Washington last week, Trump touted a forthcoming "big, beautiful agreement" on Ukraine that "might involve all of Europe".
Many in Ukraine are sceptical that this would result in a fair peace.
Ukrainian MP Oleksandr Merezhko, head of the foreign affairs parliamentary committee, told the BBC he believed Trump wanted "a quick deal at the expense of Ukraine", which will certainly be rejected by Kyiv.
The only way to make Russia's Vladimir Putin start real negotiations was by putting greater pressure on Russia through sanctions and deep strikes, Merezhko said.
"While Putin has a war machine up and running, he has no incentives to negotiate." He also mentioned recent moves by Trump, such as his deal to buy diesel from Russia, as something that "only encourages Moscow to continue the war".
Moscow's delegation in Abu Dhabi includes Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky, deputy foreign ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, spy chief Igor Kostyukov and army general Yury Zhigarlovsky.
Kyiv has sent several senior officials who have been part of previous negotiating teams, including Foreign Intelligence Service head Rustem Umerov, Volodymyr Zelensky's chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov, and MP Davyd Arakhamiya.
Away from Abu Dhabi, Russia continues to pummel Ukraine with deadly bombardments and strikes on energy infrastructure, viewed in Kyiv as proof that Moscow wants to corner Ukraine into accepting a deal on Russia's terms.
On Monday, Kushner was cautious to point out that the Abu Dhabi talks could at most "build momentum toward the next phase of negotiations".
"This is an extraordinarily difficult and complicated conflict," he wrote on X, adding the US was "approaching these discussions with determination and realism."

Coinbase Receives Approval To Become A Chartered Trust Bank
Coinbase receives approval to become a chartered trust bank
The new status lets the company handle payments and custody services.
BySteve DentNov. 9, 2026 8:40 am ESTMamun_Sheikh/ShutterstockAdd Engadget on Google:Preferred SourceGoogle Discover
Coinbase has receivedapprovalfrom the US Office of the Comptroller of Currency to become a nationally chartered trust bank, the crypto companyannounced. The designation is more limited than a full bank charter, so Coinbase won't be able to handle regular deposits or grant loans. However, the new status will allow it to conduct payments and custody services, and expand its stablecoin business.
"This is an important step forward for Coinbase and the broader crypto industry," the company said in a press release. "Coinbase has always pursued clear, consistent and best-in-class regulatory oversight that will move the financial industry, and American leadership in digital assets forward."
Other digital asset companies have sought to become trust charters, including Block and Wise, but only Circle Internet Group, Ripple and now Coinbase have been successful. Coinbase says it's the world's largest crypto custodian, and recentlypartneredwith Citigroup to do stablecoin-to-currency conversions.
The company's past is far from squeaky-clean, though. In 2022 and 2023, the SECsued Coinbaseover theillegal salesof unregistered securities and alleged violations of securities laws, respectively. In 2023, the company settled with the state of New Yorkfor $100 millionover violations related to money transmitting and other irregularities. Last year, the company was hacked and the perpetrators demanded $20 million to keep the information private.

Image Credits:Zipline /Transportation
Zipline hits $21.5B valuation as Walmart expands bet on drone delivery
Kirsten Korosec7:40 AM PST · November 5, 2026
Ziplinehas raised $1.5 billion and ramped up its partnership with Walmart, a pair of deals that have raised the autonomous drone delivery and logistics startup’s profile and valuation.
Zipline and Walmart reached a new multi-year agreement to add 300 drone delivery sites across the United States. The two companies have had a drone delivery agreement since 2021, but this deal is a significant jump from the 21 active drone delivery sites they have together today.
On the fundraising side, Zipline’s $1.5 billion raise was led by Paradigm, WCM Investment Management, and Layer Global, with participation from Valor Equity Partners, Fidelity Management & Research Company, Uber, Tiger Global, J.P. Morgan, ARK Invest, and Salesforce Ventures. Zipline is now valued at $21.5 billion.
The company, which has developed a drone delivery ecosystem that includes aircraft, launch and landing systems, and logistics software, said it plans to use the funds to expand its U.S. manufacturing facilities and hire more workers to build out a nationwide drone delivery network.
Founded in 2014, Zipline got its start in Africa, where it used its autonomous drones to deliver blood in Rwanda, and later expanded to Ghana and Nigeria. The California-based company began its first operations in the U.S. in 2020, ferrying medical equipment and supplies to Novant Health in North Carolina. The following year, it struck a deal with Walmart.
But it was in 2022 that Zipline’s business really started to take off in the United States. Zipline received itsPart 135 air carrier certificationfrom the Federal Aviation Administration that year, a critical regulatory hurdle that authorized the company to complete long-range commercial drone deliveries. It has locked in a number of partnerships since then, including withUber earlier this year.
Zipline now uses its drones to deliver food, retail, agricultural, and health products in five African countries, several cities in the United States, and Japan. Zipline’s home delivery service uses Zipline’s Platform 2 drones, which are designed to carry up to eight pounds and travel to customers within a 10-mile radius. Its larger Platform 1 drones are used for long-range deliveries for enterprise, business, and government that can cover 120 miles round trip.
The company said Thursday that its share of delivery revenue grew from 10.8% to 34.9% between March and October of this year. This latest funding aims to push that metric even higher.

Zipline hits $21.5B valuation as Walmart expands bet on drone delivery | TechCrunch
Zipline hits $21.5B valuation as Walmart expands bet on drone delivery
Kirsten Korosec7:40 AM PST · November 5, 2026
Ziplinehas raised $1.5 billion and ramped up its partnership with Walmart, a pair of deals that have raised the autonomous drone delivery and logistics startup’s profile and valuation.
Zipline and Walmart reached a new multi-year agreement to add 300 drone delivery sites across the United States.
The two companies have had a drone delivery agreement since 2021, but this deal is a significant jump from the 21 active drone delivery sites they have together today.

On the fundraising side, Zipline’s $1.5 billion raise was led by Paradigm, WCM Investment Management, and Layer Global, with participation from Valor Equity Partners, Fidelity Management & Research Company, Uber, Tiger Global, J.P.
Zipline is now valued at $21.5 billion.
The company, which has developed a drone delivery ecosystem that includes aircraft, launch and landing systems, and logistics software, said it plans to use the funds to expand its U.S.
manufacturing facilities and hire more workers to build out a nationwide drone delivery network.
Founded in 2014, Zipline got its start in Africa, where it used its autonomous drones to deliver blood in Rwanda, and later expanded to Ghana and Nigeria.
The California-based company began its first operations in the U.S.
in 2020, ferrying medical equipment and supplies to Novant Health in North Carolina.
The following year, it struck a deal with Walmart.
But it was in 2022 that Zipline’s business really started to take off in the United States.

Zipline received itsPart 135 air carrier certificationfrom the Federal Aviation Administration that year, a critical regulatory hurdle that authorized the company to complete long-range commercial drone deliveries.
It has locked in a number of partnerships since then, including withUber earlier this year.
Zipline now uses its drones to deliver food, retail, agricultural, and health products in five African countries, several cities in the United States, and Japan.
Zipline’s home delivery service uses Zipline’s Platform 2 drones, which are designed to carry up to eight pounds and travel to customers within a 10-mile radius.
Its larger Platform 1 drones are used for long-range deliveries for enterprise, business, and government that can cover 120 miles round trip.
The company said Thursday that its share of delivery revenue grew from 10.8% to 34.9% between March and October of this year.
This latest funding aims to push that metric even higher.

lead_title: Sales of tinned food and bottled water jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

evidence_pages.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqev:
Tinned food and bottled water sales jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch - BBC News
Image source,JUSTIN TALLIS/AFP via Getty Images
Sales of essential goods such as bottled water and canned food soared in the 10 days following the launch of the government's "Be Ready" emergency preparedness campaign on 22 October, research indicates.
Hand sanitiser sales were up 83%, sales of bottled water rose 67% and tinned and jarred goods climbed 37%, according to data from retail research firm Worldpanel by Numerator.
The government'spublic awareness campaignencouraged people to stock up in case of disruption to essential services by severe weather or cyberattacks.
However, Worldpanel said that while households were stockpiling essentials, they were not panic buying.
The government campaign encouraged people to keep three days-worth of food and water in their homes.
Wet wipes, a torch and cash were also recommended.
After the campaign launch, the equivalent of an extra 400,000 people per day bought tinned meat, Worldpanel said, although the typical amount remained at 500g, which suggests a gradual stocking-up.
"Shoppers clearly took notice of the 'Be Ready' campaign, but this wasn't panic buying, with less than a third of households buying bottled water in October," said Fraser McKevitt, head of retail and consumer insight at Worldpanel by Numerator.
"Growth came from more people adding the recommended items on the government's checklist to their weekly shop, not from shoppers piling their trolleys high, which is very much in line with what the government wanted households to do," he said.
Further evidence of stockpiling came from food firm Princes on Tuesday, which said demand for tinned tuna, meat and vegetables had risen following the government's campaign.
Princes interim chief executive Giuseppe Mastrolia said the jump in demand "further reinforces the relevance of our core categories in providing affordable, nutritious and convenient food solutions".
The "Be Ready" campaign warns that severe weather and cyber attacks could disrupt essential services, and British households need to make sure they have what they need - for example, bottled water, and long-life food that doesn't need to be kept in the fridge such as dried fruit and nuts.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said everyone should have "those supplies in the house to get you through those moments".

Novoposted quarterly earnings ahead of expectations early Wednesday as sales of its Wegovy pill blew past estimates amid continued GLP-1 volume growth globally, sending shares up as much as 6% in early trading.
The company updated its outlook to now see adjusted revenue and operating profit growth between negative 2% and 2% at constant exchange rates. It previously saw full-year sales and operating profits, which it hiked in August, at negative 6% to flat for both metrics.
Sales in the third quarter came in at 79.2 billion Danish kroner ($11.9 billion), up 4% year-on-year at constant exchange rates and ahead of FactSet estimates of 73.6 billion kroner. Adjusted operating profit (EBIT) was 31.7 billion kroner, compared with the expected 28.6 billion kroner.
Novo saw "strong momentum" in the U.S., CEO Mike Doustdar told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Wednesday. "We today continue to see 80% market share with our product, despite the fact that competition has come and strengthened their presence," he said.
It comes as the Danish weight-loss drug maker is looking to regain momentum following a tumultuous year in which it fell behind rivalEli Lilly.
While Novo pioneered the GLP-1 weight-loss drugs now used by around 10% of Americans, it has struggled to keep the momentum going as chief rival Eli Lilly quickly caught up and surpassed Novo in their by far biggest market, the U.S. Several other pharma companies are also eyeing entry into the lucrative market.
Investors are now laser-focused on the pair's next-generation weight-loss drugs, and whether they can treat obesity-linked diseases such as heart and kidney conditions, sleep apnea and arthritis.
Novo is preparing to launch CagriSema, a combination of the GLP-1 receptor agonist semaglutide and the long-acting amylin analogue cagrilintide. Despite what Novo has touted as CagriSema's superior benefits over rival treatments, analysts have repeatedly questioned its commercial viability after the drugfailed to beat Lilly's medicinesthat are already available.
Novo ADR's have underperformed Eli Lilly shares year-to-date.
Following the results, Citi analysts maintained their neutral rating on Novo stock, citing continued uncertainty over the near-, mid-, and long-term weight-loss drug pricing and a lack of a clear Wegovy successor in the pipeline.
Novo said sales of its Wegovy pill, launched earlier this year, totaled 5.4 billion kroner, compared with the roughly 4.5 billion kroner analysts expected.
Sales of injectable Wegovy and diabetes treatment Ozempic were 20.4 billion kroner and 29.7 billion kroner, respectively, also above expectations.
Novo also announced that Chief Financial Officer Karsten Munk Knudsen is leaving at the end of 2026 after 27 years at the company, including nine years as CFO. Luigi La Corte, currently CFO of Swiss dermatology companyGalderma, will succeed him.
Novo's Wednesday earnings report comes after Lillyhiked its full-year outlooklast week on the back of a better-than-expected third quarter, driven by strong demand for its diabetes and weight-loss injections Mounjaro and Zepbound.
Lilly's weight-loss pill Foundayo, however, missed analysts' expectations in the quarter even as the company's chief financial officer said total U.S. prescriptions and the number of new Foundayo patients doubled from the previous quarter.
Novo's Copenhagen-listed shares were last seen up 3.4%, bringing year-to-date losses to about 13%. The stock fell nearly 8% in one session in September after Novofailed to reassure investors with itspost-Wegovy growth strategy.

Novo CEO Mike Doustdar told reporters early Wednesday that the company's recovery was gaining traction following successive upgrades to its full-year guidance, but cautioned that a turnaround could not be established on the basis of a single strong quarter.
"Turnaround and recovery is not done based on one data point, on one quarterly good result," Doustdar said, pointing to the progressive improvement in the company's outlook throughout the year.
"That gives me confidence that we're going in the right direction, and then we'll just have to continue working hard to see the recovery in full," he added.

Thu Minh: Học trò tôi ai cũng là 'khủng long'

Mẫu váy đính đá pha lê và cườm ánh bạc tôn trọn vóc dáng quyến rũ, kết hợp cùng găng tay đồng điệu giúp "nữ hoàng nhạc dance" khẳng định nhan sắc bất chấp thời gian khi bùng nổ trên sân khấu với bản hitI am Diva.Với chất giọng cao vút cùng cách xử lý kỹ thuật, nữ ca sĩ khuấy động không khí, khiến khán phòng trở nên sôi động.

Khi chuyện khó nói của bệnh nhân thành "trò cười" trên trang cá nhân bác sĩ | Báo Dân trí
Khi chuyện khó nói của bệnh nhân thành "trò cười" trên trang cá nhân bác sĩ
(Dân trí) - Để câu view, một số bác sĩ biến chuyện riêng tư, bệnh lý nhạy cảm của bệnh nhân thành nội dung trên mạng xã hội, nơi nỗi lo của người đi khám lại trở thành đề tài giễu cợt của cộng đồng mạng.
Bên cạnh những nội dung chia sẻ kiến thức y khoa, các câu chuyện riêng tư, bệnh lý nhạy cảm của người bệnh đang trở thành chất liệu thu hút tương tác trên không ít tài khoản mạng xã hội của bác sĩ, phòng khám.
Ghi nhận của phóng viênDân trí, trên TikTok, tài khoản mang tên B.S.T.D., tự giới thiệu có chuyên môn trong lĩnh vực thẩm mỹ, hiện sở hữu hơn 500.000 lượt theo dõi. Chủ tài khoản này còn có một kênh khác mang tên T.M.T.D., với hơn 250.000 lượt theo dõi.
Đáng nói, nhiều video trên các kênh này đề cập đến vấn đề thẩm mỹ vùng kín phụ nữ bằng những cụm từ lóng, cách nói lái những từ nhạy cảm...
Kênh TikTok B.S.T.D. với những nội dung về sức khỏe được thể hiện bằng ngôn từ phản cảm (Ảnh: Chụp màn hình).
Trong một số video, người được giới thiệu là bác sĩ liên tục sử dụng những câu hỏi, cách diễn đạt mang tính đùa cợt khi đề cập đến các vấn đềsức khỏephụ nữ. Những từ ngữ, hình ảnh tục tĩu được nhân vật nói lái, nhắc đi nhắc lại trong nhiều video.
Chẳng hạn, video có tiêu đề “Bác sĩ đã gặp con ‘chem chép’ nào có mùi kinh hồn bạt vía chưa?” thu hút hàng chục nghìn lượt thích, chia sẻ cùng hàng nghìn bình luận.
Bên dưới những video này, bên cạnh một số ý kiến trao đổi về sức khỏe, không ít tài khoản sử dụng ngôn từ thô thiển, bình phẩm, đùa cợt về vùng kín phụ nữ.
Những vấn đề vốn cần được tư vấn bằng kiến thức chuyên môn, trong môi trường nghiêm túc và tôn trọng người bệnh, lại được thể hiện theo hướng khơi gợi tò mò, tạo tiếng cười để thu hút tương tác.
Đáng chú ý, khi các chủ đề nhạy cảm được khai thác theo cách này, phần bình luận cũng dễ trở thành nơi những câu chuyện về cơ thể, bệnh lý của phụ nữ bị đem ra chế giễu.
Công khai cả giọng nói, nơi làm việc của bệnh nhân mắc bệnh xã hội
Không chỉ sử dụng ngôn từ gây tranh cãi, một số tài khoản mạng xã hội còn đăng tải những cuộc trao đổi trực tiếp vấn đề nhạy cảm với người bệnh, trong đó chứa các thông tin có nguy cơ khiến danh tính bệnh nhân bị nhận diện.
Điển hình là kênh TikTok T.T.X.N.O., được giới thiệu là kênh của một đơn vị xét nghiệm, đặc biệt liên quan đến các bệnh lây truyền qua đường tình dục.
Dù mới đăng tải nội dung, kênh đã thu hút sự chú ý với hàng loạt video ghi lại cảnh người mặc áo blouse gọi điện thông báo kết quả xét nghiệm cho bệnh nhân.
Nhiều video được đặt tiêu đề hoặc chú thích bằng các cụm từ gợi mở đến các công việc nhạy cảm của bệnh nhân như “đào nam”, “KTV”, gắn với những cuộc hội thoại về tình trạng mắc bệnh xã hội.
Kênh TikTok thường đăng nội dung về kết quả xét nghiệm bệnh xã hội (Ảnh: Chụp màn hình).
Trong các cuộc gọi được đăng tải, giọng nói của người bệnh vẫn được giữ nguyên. Một số video còn đề cập đến những địa bàn, nơi làm việc cụ thể như KCN Vân Trung (Bắc Ninh), KCN Điềm Thụy (Thái Nguyên), KCN Quế Võ (Bắc Ninh).
Đặc biệt, một video ghi lại cuộc gọi thông báo kết quả xét nghiệm cho bệnh nhân mắc nhiều bệnh xã hội đã đạt hơn 2,5 triệu lượt xem, hơn 45.000 lượt thích, gần 1.000 bình luận.
Ngay trong video, người mặc áo blouse trực tiếp giới thiệu: “Đây là một mẫu của một bạn KTV”.
Việc công khai giọng nói, kết hợp với những thông tin gợi mở về nghề nghiệp, nơi làm việc hoặc địa bàn sinh sống, có thể làm tăng nguy cơ người quen nhận ra bệnh nhân, ngay cả khi khuôn mặt không xuất hiện.
Thực tế, bên dưới một video của kênh, có tài khoản bình luận: “Nghe giọng phát biết ai ở B.G. luôn”.
Dù chưa thể xác định người bình luận có thực sự nhận ra bệnh nhân hay không, chi tiết này cho thấy nguy cơ nhận diện người bệnh từ những thông tin tưởng chừng không trực tiếp tiết lộ danh tính.
Đối với các bệnh lây truyền qua đường tình dục, việc thông tin sức khỏe cá nhân bị lan truyền có thể dẫn đến sự kỳ thị, phán xét, ảnh hưởng đến đời sống và các mối quan hệ của người bệnh.
Câu hỏi đặt ra là những bệnh nhân xuất hiện trong các cuộc gọi này có biết nội dung trao đổi về tình trạng sức khỏe của mình được đăng tải công khai hay không, và việc sử dụng những thông tin đó đã được họ đồng ý đến mức độ nào?
Hình ảnh nhạy cảm của bệnh nhân thành content
Không dừng ở các video thông báo kết quả xét nghiệm, những hình ảnh nhạy cảm, tiền sử phẫu thuật và cả câu chuyện đời tư trong quá trình thăm khám cũng xuất hiện trên trang mạng xã hội của một số bác sĩ.
Trên trang cá nhân mang tên Đ.D.N., người tự giới thiệu là bác sĩ thẩm mỹ đến từ Quảng Ngãi, từng học tại một trường đại học y khoa lớn ở TPHCM, nhiều hình ảnh nhạy cảm của bệnh nhân được đăng tải kèm những mô tả chi tiết về khuyết điểm cơ thể.
Trang cá nhân mang tên Đ.D.N. của người tự giới thiệu là bác sĩ thẩm mỹ đến từ Quảng Ngãi (Ảnh: Chụp màn hình).
Các thông tin tự giới thiệu này có điểm trùng khớp với hồ sơ của một bác sĩ được Sở Y tế TPHCM công khai thông tin hành nghề trong chuyên khoa phẫu thuật tạo hình.
Đáng chú ý, có bài đăng khai thác cả tiền sử phẫu thuật, những biến chứng và tâm lý thất vọng của bệnh nhân sau lần làm đẹp trước đó, từ đó giới thiệu kết quả can thiệp của người đăng.
Trong một bài viết, tài khoản kể lại việc một phụ nữ từng nâng ngực nhưng gặp tình trạng bao xơ, ngực căng cứng, túi ngực tụt lệch và quầng vú giãn rộng. Kết quả không như kỳ vọng khiến người này buồn bã, thậm chí từng nghĩ đến việc tháo túi ngực.
Sau đó, bài viết mô tả quá trình bác sĩ bóc bao xơ, chỉnh sửa khoang đặt túi, thu gọn quầng vú và nhấn mạnh sự cải thiện về hình dáng bầu ngực sau phẫu thuật.
Đi kèm là 4 hình ảnh cận cảnh bầu ngực của bệnh nhân. Bài đăng thu hút gần 600 lượt yêu thích cùng hàng chục bình luận.
Ở đây, thông tin về tiền sử can thiệp y khoa, những vấn đề nhạy cảm trên cơ thể và cả trạng thái tâm lý của bệnh nhân được sử dụng làm nội dung giới thiệu kết quả thẩm mỹ.
Một trường hợp khác là tài khoản có dấu tích xanh mang tên “bác sĩ H.T.”, được biết đến là bác sĩ sản phụ khoa và hiếm muộn tại TPHCM.
Một nội dung khai thác vào vấn đề nhạy cảm của bệnh nhân (Ảnh: Chụp màn hình).
Trên tài khoản này, những cuộc trò chuyện về đời tư người bệnh thậm chí được ghi hình ngay trong lúc thăm khám, sau đó đăng tải công khai để thu hút tương tác.
Ngày 12/10, bác sĩ H.T. đăng bài viết có tên “70 tuổi muốn vá màng trinh”, kèm video trao đổi với một bệnh nhân.

Nữ ca sĩ cũng bày tỏ niềm tự hào khi nhắc đến học trò Trúc Nhân, Hương Tràm và tiết lộ lý do chưa có sản phẩm chung với học trò.
Thu Minh: Học trò tôi ai cũng là 'khủng long'
Tại thảm đỏ sự kiệnTikTok Awards Đông Nam Á 2026, ca sĩ Thu Minh trở thành tâm điểm truyền thông khi diện thiết kế dạ hội đuôi cá xuyên thấu do nhà thiết kế Nguyễn Minh Tuấn thực hiện riêng.

Mẫu váy đính đá pha lê và cườm ánh bạc tôn trọn vóc dáng quyến rũ, kết hợp cùng găng tay đồng điệu giúp "nữ hoàng nhạc dance" khẳng định nhan sắc bất chấp thời gian khi bùng nổ trên sân khấu với bản hitI am Diva.Với chất giọng cao vút cùng cách xử lý kỹ thuật, nữ ca sĩ khuấy động không khí, khiến khán phòng trở nên sôi động.
Thu Minh cho rằng Trúc Nhân, Hương Tràm nỗ lực không ngừng để gặt hái thành công như hiện tại
Tại sự kiện, giọng caTaxicũng chia sẻ quan điểm về tốc độ phát triển mạnh mẽ của mạng xã hội trong những năm gần đây.
Ngoài ra, Thu Minh không giấu được niềm tự hào khi nhắc đến thành công hai học trò Trúc Nhân vàHương Tràmsau khi bước ra từ chương trìnhGiọng hát Việt 2012.
Chứng kiến sự nghiệp ngày càng thăng hoa của các học trò, Thu Minh cho rằng thành công của Trúc Nhân và Hương Tràm không chỉ đến từ tài năng mà còn là kết quả của quá trình nỗ lực, bền bỉ.
Dù đã gặt hái nhiều dấu ấn riêng trong âm nhạc, Thu Minh và Trúc Nhân đến nay vẫn chưa có sản phẩm kết hợp.
Đây cũng là điều khiến nữ ca sĩ sinh năm 1977 không khỏi trăn trở và mong muốn có cơ hội thực hiện trong tương lai.
TikTok Awards Đông Nam Á 2026gồm 11 hạng mục, nhằm tôn vinh những nhà sáng tạo nội dung có dấu ấn nổi bật trong nhiều lĩnh vực như giải trí, giáo dục, thể thao, ẩm thực...
Theo đó, mỗi hạng mục có một đại diện Việt Nam tranh tài tại lễ trao giải khu vực, dự kiến diễn ra ở Bali (Indonesia) vào ngày 27.11.2026.
Thu Minh nói về mâu thuẫn với Hương Tràm, tiết lộ xích mích chồng vì đánh con

Chiều 10.11, Quốc hội thảo luận ở hội trường về chủ trương đầu tư 3 dự áncao tốcBảo Hà - Lai Châu, đoạn Bảo Hà - Tân Phong; Quảng Ngãi - Kon Tum; Mộc Châu - Sơn La - Điện Biên, địa phận tỉnh Sơn La.
Đáng chú ý, 3 dự án cao tốc trên đi qua một số địa phương có nguồn lực còn hạn chế, do đó, khả năng cân đối vốn ngân sách địa phương là vấn đề được nhiều đại biểu quan tâm.
Quang cảnh phiên thảo luận chiều 10.11
Để dự án sớm triển khai và phát huy hiệu quả, đại biểu Nguyễn Thị Việt Nga (đoàn Hải Phòng) đề nghị xem xét mức tham gia của ngân sách địa phương phù hợp với khả năng cân đối thực tế của Lai Châu.
"Tôi đồng tình với cách tiếp cận ngân sách Trung ương và ngân sách địa phương cùng tham gia đầu tư. Nhưng với Lai Châu, cần cân nhắc kỹ mức đóng góp trong tương quan với nguồn lực và những nhiệm vụ thiết yếu tỉnh đang phải bảo đảm", bà Nga nêu.
Theo phương án Chính phủ trình, tỉnh Lai Châu dự kiến bố trí khoảng 2.004 tỉ đồng. Tài liệu tổng hợp sơ bộ về 7 dự án cao tốc do địa phương quản lý cho thấy khoản này tương đương 38,7% kế hoạch vốn ngân sách địa phương giai đoạn 2026 - 2030 của Lai Châu.
Bà Nga cho rằng, tỷ lệ này cho thấy áp lực cân đối rất đáng quan tâm với Lai Châu. Dành một phần lớn nguồn vốn địa phương cho cao tốc sẽ làm thu hẹp nguồn lực dành cho trường học, cơ sở y tế, nước sinh hoạt, hạ tầng nông thôn và các nhiệm vụ giảm nghèo.
Từ đó, nữ đại biểu đề nghị Chính phủ rà soát đầy đủ khả năng cân đối, nghiên cứu tăng mức hỗ trợ từ ngân sách Trung ương, kể cả phương án Trung ương bảo đảm toàn bộ vốn dự án nếu điều kiện cho phép, trên cơ sở đó, trình cấp có thẩm quyền quyết định phương án phù hợp...
Cùng quan điểm, đại biểu Nguyễn Đặng Ân (đoàn Lạng Sơn) băn khoăn khả năng cân đối vốn của địa phương, nhất là Lai Châu, trong điều kiện thu ngân sách địa phương hằng năm hạn chế. Ông Ân đề nghị Chính phủ rà soát, xác định mức vốn địa phương tham gia phù hợp với lại khả năng ngân sách của tỉnh.
Bộ trưởng Bộ Xây dựng Trần Hồng Minh
Giải trình sau đó, về khả năng cân đối vốn địa phương, Bộ trưởng Bộ Xây dựng Trần Hồng Minh cho biết, ngân sách Trung ương đã ưu tiên cân đối, bố trí 119.398 tỉ đồng trên tổng số hơn 162.393 tỉ đồng (đạt tỷ lệ khoảng 75%).
Đoạn qua đồng bằng tốc độ 100 - 120 km/giờ
Về vai trò cơ quan chủ quản và vốn đối ứng địa phương, Bộ trưởng Trần Hồng Minh cho hay, hiện có 15 địa phương được giao làm cơ quan chủ quản thi công các tuyến cao tốc và đều bố trí ngân sách địa phương tham gia (gồm: Hà Nội, TP.HCM, Khánh Hòa, Đắk Lắk, Đồng Nai, An Giang, Cần Thơ, Sóc Trăng, Gia Lai, Nghệ An, Sơn La, Phú Thọ, Ninh Bình, Cao Bằng, Tuyên Quang, Điện Biên).
Một số tỉnh miền núi dù điều kiện khó khăn vẫn cam kết đóng góp 50% đến 100% kinh phí giải phóng mặt bằng. "Việc duy trì chính sách này đảm bảo sự đồng bộ, bình đẳng giữa các địa phương trong quá trình triển khai. Hai địa phương Quảng Ngãi và Lai Châu là cơ quan chủ quản 2 dự án cao tốc và đã đồng ý đề xuất bỏ ra 50% tiền giải phóng mặt bằng", Bộ trưởng nói thêm.
Ông cũng khẳng định cả 3 dự án cao tốc đều tuân thủ nguyên tắc phù hợp với quy chuẩn và tiêu chuẩn thiết kế.
Tại vùng miền núi có địa hình khó khăn, độ dốc lớn (đặc biệt đoạn Mộc Châu - Sơn La - Điện Biên có chênh cao địa hình trên 1.000 m), tốc độ thiết kế 4 làn xe được lựa chọn là 80 km/giờ để đảm bảo kỹ thuật và an toàn. Với các đoạn qua vùng đồng bằng, tốc độ thiết kế đảm bảo từ 100 - 120 km/giờ.
Cả 3 tuyến cao tốc được lựa chọn trên nguyên tắc phù hợp với quy hoạch, đáp ứng yêu cầu kỹ thuật, điều kiện địa hình, hạn chế tối đa ảnh hưởng đến các khu vực nhạy cảm về môi trường tự nhiên, xã hội, danh lam thắng cảnh, đất quốc phòng và hạn chế tối đa chi phí giải phóng mặt bằng.
Trình Quốc hội đầu tư 3 cao tốc, tỉnh cuối cùng cả nước sắp có cao tốc
Sáng 7.11, thừa ủy quyền Thủ tướng Chính phủ, Bộ trưởng Xây dựng Trần Hồng Minh đã trình Quốc hội chủ trương đầu tư 3 dự án cao tốc Mộc Châu - Sơn La - Điện Biên, Bảo Hà - Lai Châu và Quảng Ngãi - Kon Tum.Chia sẻChọn BáoThanh Niênlàmnguồn ưu tiêntrên Google tìm kiếm.Xem hướng dẫn.

Vĩnh Long tăng tốc xử lý 750 trụ sở dôi dư sau nhập tỉnh, sắp xếp bộ máy
(Dân trí) - Sau sắp xếp, tỉnh Vĩnh Long có 750 cơ sở nhà, đất dôi dư cần xử lý. Theo Sở Tài chính, đến ngày 8/11, địa phương đã xử lý triệt để 604 cơ sở, còn 146 cơ sở.
Sau sắp xếp, tinh gọn tổ chức bộ máy và đơn vị hành chính, tỉnh Vĩnh Long có 750 cơ sở nhà, đất dôi dư cần xử lý. Trong đó, 531 cơ sở thuộc địa phương và 219 cơ sở do Trung ương chuyển giao về địa phương quản lý.
Trụ sở UBND tỉnh Bến Tre cũ (Ảnh: CTV).
Thực hiện Công điện của Thủ tướng Chính phủ về đẩy nhanh tiến độ xử lý, khai thác nhà, đất dôi dư sau sắp xếp tổ chức bộ máy, đơn vị hành chính, UBND tỉnh Vĩnh Long đã chỉ đạo các sở, ngành, đơn vị liên quan khẩn trương rà soát, phân loại và triển khai phương án xử lý đối với từng cơ sở.
Tỉnh Vĩnh Long hiện nayđược thành lập từ 1/7/2025 trên cơ sở sáp nhập 3 tỉnh cũ gồmVĩnh Long, Bến Tre và Trà Vinh.Tỉnh có tổng cộng 124 xã, phường, với diện tích gần 6.300km2, dân số 4,6 triệu người.
Theo Sở Tài chính, đến ngày 8/11, địa phương đã xử lý triệt để 604 cơ sở (tăng 33 cơ sở so với tuần trước), còn 146 cơ sở.
Trong số này, Trung tâm Tư vấn xây dựng đang quản lý, xử lý 104 cơ sở. Có 97 cơ sở đã được thông báo cho thuê; 4 cơ sở đang lập phương án giá đợt 6, đã được Sở Xây dựng trình UBND tỉnh xem xét và 3 cơ sở còn lại đang hoàn thiện hồ sơ cải tạo làm nhà ở công vụ.
Đối với 42 cơ sở do Trung tâm Phát triển quỹ đất thực hiện, có 6 cơ sở đã được phê duyệt giá khởi điểm và thông báo cho thuê trên Cổng thông tin điện tử của tỉnh. Trong số còn lại, 16 cơ sở đã được UBND tỉnh phê duyệt danh mục cho thuê ngắn hạn, đang được Trung tâm Tư vấn xây dựng phối hợp với Sở Nông nghiệp và Môi trường xác định giá khởi điểm để trình UBND tỉnh. Riêng 20 cơ sở đã được Sở Nông nghiệp và Môi trường trình UBND tỉnh phê duyệt danh mục cho thuê ngắn hạn, dự kiến đưa vào khai thác từ ngày 10/12.
Đối với 11 cơ sở nhà, đất được xác định không có khả năng khai thác, Sở Tài chính đã có văn bản hướng dẫn các địa phương phối hợp quản lý, khai thác, xử lý nhà, đất dôi dư, tránh để tài sản công bỏ trống, xuống cấp, gây lãng phí.
Đồng thời, Sở Tài chính chủ trì, phối hợp Trung tâm Tư vấn xây dựng và UBND các xã, phường rà soát các cơ sở nhà, đất trên địa bàn, ưu tiên đưa vào danh mục cho các hợp tác xã thuê, dự kiến thời gian chậm nhất ngày 13/11.
Sở Nông nghiệp và Môi trường phối hợp Trung tâm Phát triển quỹ đất khẩn trương xác định giá khởi điểm đối với 36 cơ sở đã được UBND tỉnh phê duyệt danh mục cho thuê ngắn hạn, phấn đấu đưa vào khai thác chậm nhất ngày 24/11.
Bộ Tài chính thúc xử lý 408 cơ sở nhà, đất dôi dư tại Cần Thơ
Theo kế hoạch, ngày 13/11, lãnh đạo UBND TP Cần Thơ sẽ có buổi làm việc với một số đơn vị có liên quan về tài sản nhà, đất dôi dư sau sắp xếp đơn vị hành chính trên địa bàn thành phố.
Chủ tịch UBND tỉnh Phú Thọ Trần Duy Đông yêu cầu khẩn trương sắp xếp và đề xuất phương án xử lý, khai thác 521 nhà, đất dôi dư trên địa bàn.
Lâm Đồng có 1.255 cơ sở nhà, đất dôi dư sau sáp nhập
Tỉnh Lâm Đồng hiện có 1.255 cơ sở nhà, đất dôi dư và địa phương này đề xuất các đơn vị liên quan rà soát, quản lý, xử lý theo quy định.
An Giang tìm cách khai thác hơn 1.100 cơ sở nhà đất dôi dư
An Giang đã tháo gỡ vướng mắc cho 474 dự án tồn đọng, đồng thời triển khai phương án xử lý 1.155 cơ sở nhà, đất dôi dư.

Chiều 10.11, Quốc hội thảo luận ở hội trường về chủ trương đầu tư 3 dự áncao tốcBảo Hà - Lai Châu, đoạn Bảo Hà - Tân Phong; Quảng Ngãi - Kon Tum; Mộc Châu - Sơn La - Điện Biên, địa phận tỉnh Sơn La.
Đáng chú ý, 3 dự án cao tốc trên đi qua một số địa phương có nguồn lực còn hạn chế, do đó, khả năng cân đối vốn ngân sách địa phương là vấn đề được nhiều đại biểu quan tâm.
Quang cảnh phiên thảo luận chiều 10.11
Để dự án sớm triển khai và phát huy hiệu quả, đại biểu Nguyễn Thị Việt Nga (đoàn Hải Phòng) đề nghị xem xét mức tham gia của ngân sách địa phương phù hợp với khả năng cân đối thực tế của Lai Châu.
"Tôi đồng tình với cách tiếp cận ngân sách Trung ương và ngân sách địa phương cùng tham gia đầu tư.
Nhưng với Lai Châu, cần cân nhắc kỹ mức đóng góp trong tương quan với nguồn lực và những nhiệm vụ thiết yếu tỉnh đang phải bảo đảm", bà Nga nêu.
Theo phương án Chính phủ trình, tỉnh Lai Châu dự kiến bố trí khoảng 2.004 tỉ đồng.
Tài liệu tổng hợp sơ bộ về 7 dự án cao tốc do địa phương quản lý cho thấy khoản này tương đương 38,7% kế hoạch vốn ngân sách địa phương giai đoạn 2026 - 2030 của Lai Châu.
Bà Nga cho rằng, tỷ lệ này cho thấy áp lực cân đối rất đáng quan tâm với Lai Châu.
Dành một phần lớn nguồn vốn địa phương cho cao tốc sẽ làm thu hẹp nguồn lực dành cho trường học, cơ sở y tế, nước sinh hoạt, hạ tầng nông thôn và các nhiệm vụ giảm nghèo.

Từ đó, nữ đại biểu đề nghị Chính phủ rà soát đầy đủ khả năng cân đối, nghiên cứu tăng mức hỗ trợ từ ngân sách Trung ương, kể cả phương án Trung ương bảo đảm toàn bộ vốn dự án nếu điều kiện cho phép, trên cơ sở đó, trình cấp có thẩm quyền quyết định phương án phù hợp...
Cùng quan điểm, đại biểu Nguyễn Đặng Ân (đoàn Lạng Sơn) băn khoăn khả năng cân đối vốn của địa phương, nhất là Lai Châu, trong điều kiện thu ngân sách địa phương hằng năm hạn chế.
Ông Ân đề nghị Chính phủ rà soát, xác định mức vốn địa phương tham gia phù hợp với lại khả năng ngân sách của tỉnh.

Giải trình sau đó, về khả năng cân đối vốn địa phương, Bộ trưởng Bộ Xây dựng Trần Hồng Minh cho biết, ngân sách Trung ương đã ưu tiên cân đối, bố trí 119.398 tỉ đồng trên tổng số hơn 162.393 tỉ đồng (đạt tỷ lệ khoảng 75%).
Đoạn qua đồng bằng tốc độ 100 - 120 km/giờ

Về vai trò cơ quan chủ quản và vốn đối ứng địa phương, Bộ trưởng Trần Hồng Minh cho hay, hiện có 15 địa phương được giao làm cơ quan chủ quản thi công các tuyến cao tốc và đều bố trí ngân sách địa phương tham gia (gồm: Hà Nội, TP.HCM, Khánh Hòa, Đắk Lắk, Đồng Nai, An Giang, Cần Thơ, Sóc Trăng, Gia Lai, Nghệ An, Sơn La, Phú Thọ, Ninh Bình, Cao Bằng, Tuyên Quang, Điện Biên).
Một số tỉnh miền núi dù điều kiện khó khăn vẫn cam kết đóng góp 50% đến 100% kinh phí giải phóng mặt bằng.
"Việc duy trì chính sách này đảm bảo sự đồng bộ, bình đẳng giữa các địa phương trong quá trình triển khai.
Hai địa phương Quảng Ngãi và Lai Châu là cơ quan chủ quản 2 dự án cao tốc và đã đồng ý đề xuất bỏ ra 50% tiền giải phóng mặt bằng", Bộ trưởng nói thêm.
Ông cũng khẳng định cả 3 dự án cao tốc đều tuân thủ nguyên tắc phù hợp với quy chuẩn và tiêu chuẩn thiết kế.

Tại vùng miền núi có địa hình khó khăn, độ dốc lớn (đặc biệt đoạn Mộc Châu - Sơn La - Điện Biên có chênh cao địa hình trên 1.000 m), tốc độ thiết kế 4 làn xe được lựa chọn là 80 km/giờ để đảm bảo kỹ thuật và an toàn.
Với các đoạn qua vùng đồng bằng, tốc độ thiết kế đảm bảo từ 100 - 120 km/giờ.

Cả 3 tuyến cao tốc được lựa chọn trên nguyên tắc phù hợp với quy hoạch, đáp ứng yêu cầu kỹ thuật, điều kiện địa hình, hạn chế tối đa ảnh hưởng đến các khu vực nhạy cảm về môi trường tự nhiên, xã hội, danh lam thắng cảnh, đất quốc phòng và hạn chế tối đa chi phí giải phóng mặt bằng.

lead_title: California voters reject proposed one-time tax on billionaires' wealth

evidence_pages.https://www.france24.com/en/americas/202:
California voters reject proposed one-time tax on billionaires' wealth - France 24Skip to main content
California voters reject proposed one-time tax on billionaires' wealth
California voters have rejected a proposed 5% tax on the net worth of billionaires, handing a victory to tech leaders who poured hundreds of millions of dollars into defeating the measure. The defeat of Proposition 40 also marks a setback for progressives seeking to tax the wealth of the ultra-rich.
3 minReading timeShareBy:FRANCE 24A man's shirt and sticker are displayed at the Billionaire Tax Now booth at the 2026 California Democratic Party State Convention in San Francisco, 21 February 2026. © Jeff Chiu, AP
Californiavoters have rejected a first-in-the-nation tax on the net worth of billionaires following a contentious ballot fight that generated huge spending by some prominent tech leaders eager to stop theirtaxesfrom going up.
The measure’s failure is a win for Democratic leaders who opposed it, including Gov.Gavin Newsom, who may run for president in 2028. Critics of the tax, known as Proposition 40, said it would have prompted ultrawealthy taxpayers to leave the state.
Most Californians vote by mail, and any ballot postmarked by Election Day that arrives within a week is counted, meaning it often takes days or even weeks for close races to be settled. The Associated Press determined Monday that ‘no’ had received enough votes to win.
The “no” side raised roughly 10 times as much as the “yes” side.Googleco-founder Sergey Brin alone dumped more than $100 million into a political action committee working to defeat the measure.
The measure would have imposed a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of Californians whose net worth exceeds $1 billion.Most of the money would have been used to backfill federal funding cuts to healthcare, and 10% would have gone towardeducationand food-assistance programs. SEIU United Healthcare Workers West, which backed the tax, said it was necessary to replace an estimated $100 billion the state will lose in federal healthcare funding over five years.
Proposition 40 was the nation’s biggest test yet on an idea progressives have long championed: raising taxes on the ultra-rich by targeting the main way they make their money — through their investments as opposed to the paychecks they receive from work.
The measure attracted support from liberal leaders beyond the state, including Vermont Sen.Bernie Sanders, who rallied in cities across California in the race’s closing weeks to urge voters to pass it. The “Yes on 40” campaign did not immediately respond to a message seeking comment.
Billionaires donated millions of dollars to a political action committee, Building a Better California, working to defeat the measure. The committee, which backed other measures on the ballot designed to nullify the tax, raised more than $333 million, nearly a third of which came from Brin.
The AP Voter Poll indicates that the majority of young voters in California — those younger than 30 — voted “yes” on Proposition 40. Older voters were far less supportive, with roughly 7 in 10 voters who were 65 and older saying they voted “no” on the ballot measure.
About half of voters with a household income under $100,000 annually said they were in support of the initiative. Closer to 6 in 10 California voters with an income of $100,000 or higher said they were opposed.
Brin, along with his fellow Google co-founder Larry Page, was among the billionaires who started cutting ties with the state in anticipation of the possible tax. Another tech mogul,Mark Zuckerberg, said he would remain in the state for eight years and made a deal with Meta to help him pay the tax without losing his ownership stake in the company.
Some traditional Democratic allies, including Planned Parenthood and the California Medical Association, were part of a coalition opposing it. They were concerned about how the tax revenue would be divvied up and about the potential impact on the state’s budget if there was a mass exodus of wealthy taxpayers. California’s budget relies heavily on the income tax of the state’s richest residents.
“Proposition 40 was a reckless experiment conducted on our state’s economy with little regard for the harms it would cause,” the coalition said in a statement.
Robert Swonger, an auto glass technician living near Sacramento who’s politically independent, said before voting concluded Nov. 3 that he planned to vote against it.
“Obviously, I would like billionaires not to have as much money as they do,” he said. “But I don’t believe taxing them out of existence is going to work.”
Progressive politicians, including Sanders and Massachusetts Sen.Elizabeth Warren, have long supported a federal wealth tax. Newsom says a California wealth tax would disadvantage the state, but he supports a national minimum tax on anyone with a net worth above $100 million.
Days before Sanders held rallies in California cities last month, Newsom told reporters that the senator’s focus on wealth inequality was “spot-on.” But he said that “on this issue, we fundamentally disagree.”
Supporters of the California tax started running ads recently in New Hampshire, New Mexico and Virginia, states that will vote early in the Democratic presidential primary in 2028, that criticize Newsom for his opposition to the measure.

California voters fail to pass proposed one-time tax on billionaires’ wealth | California | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigation
Supporters hold signs advocating for the Billionaire Tax Now coalition in Los Angeles in April.Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenSupporters hold signs advocating for the Billionaire Tax Now coalition in Los Angeles in April.Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images
California voters fail to pass proposed one-time tax on billionaires’ wealth
Campaign over Prop 40, as measure was known, was most expensive in state history, flush with Silicon Valley dollars
California billionaires won a contentious ballot measure campaign, defeating a proposed one-time tax on their wealth.
The bruising campaign over Proposition 40 was the most expensive in state history and witness to back-and-forth dealing from tech billionaires and democratic leaders, including Gavin Newsom, the governor, who steadfastly opposed the measure. While supporters of Prop 40 cast it as a solution to drastic healthcare cuts from Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act, opponents led by prosperous billionaires mounted an influential campaign saying the billionaire tax was instead “an everyone tax”.
This result could hamper nationwide momentum on demands that billionaires pay their fair share and states enacting new laws to tax the ultra-wealthy.
Prop 40 proposed a one-time 5% tax on all individuals in California with a net worth of more than $1bn as of 1 January 2026. It was sponsored by the healthcare union SEIU-United Healthcare Workers West, and dictated that the proceeds from the tax would fund healthcare programs, along with some education and food assistance.
The state’s major unions, and progressive politicians such as Bernie Sanders, the Vermont senator, and Ro Khanna, a California congressman, backed Prop 40. But both the Democratic and Republican candidates for governor, as well as organizations such as Planned Parenthood Affiliates of California, a lobbying branch of the healthcare group, opposed it – pointing to its structure as a one-off tax that would only fund certain healthcare programs. Prop 40’s most vocal critics, however, were the state’s billionaires.
Donors to the opposition campaignwere a who’s who of Silicon Valley, including executives from Google, Palantir, DoorDash, Stripe and Reddit, along with several prominent venture capitalists. The biggest donor, by far, was Sergey Brin, a Google co-founder, who contributed at least $132m to fight the tax, according to campaign finance filings.
All told, the billionaires mounted a nearly $425m battle against Prop 40, making it the most expensive opposition campaign in state history. In the first two weeks of October, spending surpassed $2.5m a day, according to the most recentcampaign finance filings.
Part of the opposition campaign’s strategy was mounting two separate counter-measures on the ballot, Proposition 41 and 42. Prop 41 directly targeted the billionaire tax, while Prop 42 was a general proposal on limiting certain new taxes and would ban any taxation on billionaire wealth. If either measure received more yes votes than Prop 40, they would stop the billionaire tax from taking effect – even if it passed.
Supporters of the billionaire tax called Props 41 and 42 “poison pills”.

Californians reject Prop 40 wealth tax for billionaires - BBC News
Image source,Bloomberg via Getty ImagesBySareen HabeshianReporting fromLos Angeles
Published10 November 2026, 03:00 GMT
California voters have voted to reject a wealth tax on its billionaires.
The ballot proposal would have levied a one-time tax on the state's mega wealthy to help fund healthcare. It took nearly a week of counting votes after the midterm election to determine a projection on the measure.
There are about 200 billionaires in the state,including Meta's Mark Zuckerberg, reality television star Kim Kardashian and media mogul Oprah Winfrey.
Proposition 40 targeted Californians with a wealth of more than $1.1bn (£800m) with a 5% tax on their total wealth, including assets such as shares as well as income. It failed amid divisions among Democrats and labour unions.
Are California voters about to impose 'world's first' tax on billionaires?
Had it passed, experts believe it would have been the world's first wealth tax targeting billionaires.
The tax would have raised about $100bn to make up for federal funding cuts to healthcare in California as a result of President Donald Trump's sweeping tax and spending bill.
Those who backed the measure had argued it would help ensure that the ultra-wealthy were contributing their fair share and helping backfill gaps in the state's budget.
The wealth tax faced fierce opposition, including from Google co-founder Sergey Brin, as well as California Governor Gavin Newsom and labour unions.
Newsom, whose tenure as governor is coming to an end, had expressed concerns that the measure could cause the wealthy to leave the state and drive out their crucial income tax revenue.
Some billionaire critics of the measure spent millions trying to crush it, with a handful even moving out of the state to evade the possible tax. Brin gave more than $100m to a political organisation funding ballot measures that could block the tax, according to the Los Angeles Times.
Dave Regan, head of the union that led the charge for the measure, said on election night that the billionaires' efforts to block the tax created "a lot of confusion and a lot of second-guessing among people who really in their hearts know what the right the thing to do is".
Regan, who is president of Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West, pledged to seek a billionaire tax once more in 2028.
The measure had odds stacked against it, with two other propositions on the ballot that would have effectively reversed it, even if it passed.
California, home to some 23 million registered voters, has the largest economy in the country and boasts the fourth largest global economy. It is home to one of the highest concentrations of billionaires in the world, but also has one of the highest wealth gaps.

Three tax proposals targeting the rich the new Congress could reviveSkip Navigation
MarketsBusinessInvestingTechPolitics & PolicyVideoWatchlistInvesting ClubPROLivestreamMenu
The Democrats' midterm wins have revived calls to tax the ultra-wealthy, with Sen. Ron Wyden, D-Ore., already putting billionaires on notice.
Several proposals before the Senate Committee on Finance target carried interest, large trusts, and borrowing against stock.
While the Democrats do not have enough seats to override a presidential veto, tax lawyers told CNBC that these proposals are worth watching as they may shape the priorities of the next administration.
Sen. Ron Wyden, D-Ore., is seen during votes in the U.S. Capitol on Wednesday, June 17, 2026.Tom Williams | Cq-roll Call, Inc. | Getty Images
A version of this article appeared in CNBC's Inside Wealth newsletter, a weekly guide to the high-net-worth investor and consumer.Sign upto receive future editions, straight to your inbox.
Democrats' sweeping midterm victories have renewed momentum for taxing the wealthy on a national level. Sen. Ron Wyden, D-Ore., who is set to retake control of the Senate Committee on Finance, has already put billionaires on notice. Several proposals are already before the committee, including measures to close the carried-interest tax break and impose taxes on large trust assets.
"On taxes, the committee will redouble its efforts to ensure billionaires pay their fair share and hold tax cheats accountable. Democrats will spearhead a tax agenda that puts American families first and requires the ultra-rich and corporations to pay their fair share," Wyden said in a statement Wednesday morning.
Tax lawyers told CNBC that proposed wealth taxes and other tax hikes are unlikely to become law because the Democrats have notwon enough seats to overcome a veto from President Donald Trump. However, the measures are worth monitoring as they shape the party's agenda heading into the next presidential election, they said.
"The proposals are not necessarily anything that will pass over the next two years. But if there is an administration change two years from now, they do give you an indication of what might be on the table during the next administration," said Justin Miller, partner and national director of wealth planning at Evercore Wealth Management.
Here are three tax proposals sitting with the Senate Committee on Finance that could gain traction after the blue tsunami.
Ending the Carried Interest Loophole Act
In April, Wyden and Sen. Angus King, I-Maine, introduced a bill eliminating the preferential tax treatment ofcarried interest, a popular Wall Street tax break. Under current law, fund managers can have a share of a fund's profits taxed at the lower capital-gains rate if the investments are held for at least three years. The Ending the Carried Interest Loophole Act would tax investment profits as ordinary income and also require fund managers to recognize and pay tax on deemed compensation annually, rather than deferring taxes until the fund realizes income.
Lawmakers on both sides of the aisle have proposed changing the taxation of carried interest for nearly two decades, according to Holland & Knight partner Joshua Odintz, a former tax counsel at the Department of Treasury and the Senate Committee on Finance. President Trump repeatedly criticized the provision, saying during his 2016 presidential campaign that it was "unfair to American workers."
Odintz said he expects more scrutiny of carried interest as Congress faces pressure to shore up the Social Security trust fund, which is expected to run out of reserves by the end of 2032. However, he thinks it is more likely that the tax break will be eliminated as part of a budget reconciliation bill rather than a standalone bill.
"I think an issue like carried interest have to be addressed in the context of a larger tax bill, where it's challenging for members to say, 'No, I'm going to stand up just on this one issue and crater a bill,'" he said. "It's much easier when there are a series of trade-offs, and members can point to the different trade-offs and say, 'Look, I got this. I guess I had to give up that, but on net, this is better for my jurisdiction.''"
Fair Trusts for Fiscal Responsibility Act
Sen. Patty Murray, D-Wash., introduced a bill targeting trusts used to transfer assets while minimizing or avoiding estate and gift taxes. The Fair Trusts for Fiscal Responsibility Act sets a graduated annual tax on trust assets exceeding $50 million, with the rate rising to 3% for assets above $1 billion. It would also create a withholding-credit system: taxes paid each year would be tracked in an account and credited against estate or generation-skipping taxes when assets are later transferred or the trust ends. Any unused credit against estate taxes could be refunded.
"This is something that should be watched because if it gets traction, it would fundamentally change estate planning for ultra-high-net-worth individuals," said David Blum, partner and chair of Akerman's national tax practice group.
Miller said he is skeptical that the bill would pass given how complicated it would be to implement. He thinks it is more realistic that the U.S. would follow the examples of the United Kingdom and Canada and periodically tax assets held in trust every set number of years. In the U.K., an inheritance tax is levied every 10 years, and Canada imposes a 21-year rule on most personal and family trusts.

California voters reject proposed one-time tax on billionaires' wealth
California voters have rejected a proposed 5% tax on the net worth of billionaires, handing a victory to tech leaders who poured hundreds of millions of dollars into defeating the measure.
The defeat of Proposition 40 also marks a setback for progressives seeking to tax the wealth of the ultra-rich.
3 minReading timeShareBy:FRANCE 24A man's shirt and sticker are displayed at the Billionaire Tax Now booth at the 2026 California Democratic Party State Convention in San Francisco, 21 February 2026.

Californiavoters have rejected a first-in-the-nation tax on the net worth of billionaires following a contentious ballot fight that generated huge spending by some prominent tech leaders eager to stop theirtaxesfrom going up.
The measure’s failure is a win for Democratic leaders who opposed it, including Gov.Gavin Newsom, who may run for president in 2028.
Critics of the tax, known as Proposition 40, said it would have prompted ultrawealthy taxpayers to leave the state.
Most Californians vote by mail, and any ballot postmarked by Election Day that arrives within a week is counted, meaning it often takes days or even weeks for close races to be settled.
The Associated Press determined Monday that ‘no’ had received enough votes to win.
The “no” side raised roughly 10 times as much as the “yes” side.Googleco-founder Sergey Brin alone dumped more than $100 million into a political action committee working to defeat the measure.

The measure would have imposed a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of Californians whose net worth exceeds $1 billion.Most of the money would have been used to backfill federal funding cuts to healthcare, and 10% would have gone towardeducationand food-assistance programs.
SEIU United Healthcare Workers West, which backed the tax, said it was necessary to replace an estimated $100 billion the state will lose in federal healthcare funding over five years.

Proposition 40 was the nation’s biggest test yet on an idea progressives have long championed: raising taxes on the ultra-rich by targeting the main way they make their money — through their investments as opposed to the paychecks they receive from work.

The measure attracted support from liberal leaders beyond the state, including Vermont Sen.Bernie Sanders, who rallied in cities across California in the race’s closing weeks to urge voters to pass it.
The “Yes on 40” campaign did not immediately respond to a message seeking comment.
Billionaires donated millions of dollars to a political action committee, Building a Better California, working to defeat the measure.
The committee, which backed other measures on the ballot designed to nullify the tax, raised more than $333 million, nearly a third of which came from Brin.
The AP Voter Poll indicates that the majority of young voters in California — those younger than 30 — voted “yes” on Proposition 40.
Older voters were far less supportive, with roughly 7 in 10 voters who were 65 and older saying they voted “no” on the ballot measure.
About half of voters with a household income under $100,000 annually said they were in support of the initiative.
Closer to 6 in 10 California voters with an income of $100,000 or higher said they were opposed.
Brin, along with his fellow Google co-founder Larry Page, was among the billionaires who started cutting ties with the state in anticipation of the possible tax.
Another tech mogul,Mark Zuckerberg, said he would remain in the state for eight years and made a deal with Meta to help him pay the tax without losing his ownership stake in the company.
Some traditional Democratic allies, including Planned Parenthood and the California Medical Association, were part of a coalition opposing it.
They were concerned about how the tax revenue would be divvied up and about the potential impact on the state’s budget if there was a mass exodus of wealthy taxpayers.
California’s budget relies heavily on the income tax of the state’s richest residents.
“Proposition 40 was a reckless experiment conducted on our state’s economy with little regard for the harms it would cause,” the coalition said in a statement.
Robert Swonger, an auto glass technician living near Sacramento who’s politically independent, said before voting concluded Nov.
3 that he planned to vote against it.
“Obviously, I would like billionaires not to have as much money as they do,” he said.
“But I don’t believe taxing them out of existence is going to work.”
Progressive politicians, including Sanders and Massachusetts Sen.Elizabeth Warren, have long supported a federal wealth tax.
Newsom says a California wealth tax would disadvantage the state, but he supports a national minimum tax on anyone with a net worth above $100 million.

Days before Sanders held rallies in California cities last month, Newsom told reporters that the senator’s focus on wealth inequality was “spot-on.” But he said that “on this issue, we fundamentally disagree.”

Supporters of the California tax started running ads recently in New Hampshire, New Mexico and Virginia, states that will vote early in the Democratic presidential primary in 2028, that criticize Newsom for his opposition to the measure.

Tỉ phú Elon Musk cùng các ông trùm tài chính nổi tiếng lên tiếng ủng hộ CEO NVIDIA Jensen Huang, giữa lúc ông bị điều tra nội bộ về quan hệ tình cảm với một phụ nữ bị nghi liên quan tình báo Trung Quốc.
TheoThe Guardianngày 10.11, nhiều nhân vật có ảnh hưởng tạiThung lũng Siliconđã công khai bênh vực ôngJensen Huangkhi thông tin về cuộc điều tra gây xôn xao giới công nghệ Mỹ.

Tỉ phú Elon Muskbày tỏ đồng tình với nhà đầu tư mạo hiểm Shaun Maguire - người cho rằng CEO NVIDIA đã mắc sai lầm nghiêm trọng trong đời tư nhưng vẫn là "một trong những doanh nhân vĩ đại nhất thế hệ này". Ông Maguire nhấn mạnh vai trò của ông Huang đối với ngànhtrí tuệ nhân tạo(AI) Mỹ, đồng thời cảnh báo không nên để vụ việc gây tổn hại đến năng lực cạnh tranh công nghệ của nước này.
Tỉ phú Bill Ackman, nhà quản lý quỹ đầu cơ nổi tiếng, cũng kêu gọi công chúng ủng hộ ông Huang và gia đình. "Ngay cả những người tuyệt vời cũng có thể mắc sai lầm", ông viết. Tuy nhiên, ông Ackman sau đó làm rõ rằng sự ủng hộ không đồng nghĩa với việc CEO NVIDIA được miễn trách nhiệm, đồng thời bày tỏ hy vọng vụ việc không ảnh hưởng đến an ninh quốc gia Mỹ.
"Tôi nghĩ anh ấy là một người chính trực", Tổng thống Mỹ Donald Trump ủng hộ CEONVIDIA, đồng thời cho rằng ông Jensen Huang nên tiếp tục giữ chức vụ.
Làn sóng ủng hộ xuất hiện sau khi ông Huang bị điều tra nội bộ về mối quan hệ ngoài hôn nhân với bà Alice Huang, nữ doanh nhân bị giới tình báo Mỹ nghi hoạt động cho chính phủ Trung Quốc.

TheoThe New York Times, giới tình báo Mỹ nghi bà Alice Huang đã tìm cách tác động để ông Jensen Huang vận động Tổng thống Donald Trump nới lỏng các hạn chế xuất khẩu chip tiên tiến sang Trung Quốc. NVIDIA khẳng định không có bí mật thương mại hay thông tin liên quan an ninh quốc gia Mỹ bị xâm phạm. Vụ việc đặt NVIDIA trước những bất ổn về tương lai lãnh đạo, khi tập đoàn giữ vai trò then chốt trong sự bùng nổ AI toàn cầu.
